Generally speaking, it is recommended to sacrifice bulk instead of offensive power if wanting to reallocate to Speed. 3 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed negative Speed nature Aegislash . 11 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested base 60 Speed targets such as Clefable before Mega Evolution, Primarina, and Aegislash. 12 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar . 16 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Scizor before Mega Evolution. 18 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Corviknight , though its superior bulk and access to Body Press mean that it is still overwhelmingly favored in the matchup. 21 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Clefable , though keep in mind that Mega Clefable often receives Speed boosts from Baton Pass Espathra . 26 Speed : This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor .

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description_plain: With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a powerful revenge killer and bulky attacker. Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave : Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp . Kowtow Cleave is usually needed as a second Dark-type attack, though, particularly for Substitute users like Mega Gengar that can play around Sucker Punch. Swords Dance : Kingambit's amazing bulk allows it to consistently survive big hits such as Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, letting it set up a Swords Dance and fire back with +2 Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Low Kick : Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina , Mimikyu , and Mega Floette . Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage. Items Black Glasses : Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp. Lum Berry : If Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance ahead of time, Lum Berry will prevent Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W from switching in and completely ruining its momentum. Chople Berry : Chople Berry allows Kingambit to withstand some weaker Fighting-type attacks, such as Close Combat from Aegislash and Scizor and unboosted Body Press from Corviknight . With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny 's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast. Alternate EV Spread 8 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def / 24 Spe with Adamant : This spread maintains enough bulk to almost always survive Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's +2 Play Rough after Stealth Rock damage as well as Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake from full health. After maximizing Attack, the remaining SPs are invested into Speed, allowing Kingambit to outrun threats such as Mega Clefable with 2 Speed SPs.

• With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a powerful revenge killer and bulky attacker.

  • Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave: Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp.   • Iron Head versus Low Kick: Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina, Mimikyu, and Mega Floette. Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage.

Items

  • Black Glasses: Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp.

  • Lum Berry: If Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance ahead of time, Lum Berry will prevent Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W from switching in and completely ruining its momentum.

With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Kingambit is one of the top threats of Regulation M-A, trading damage comfortably and threatening many top threats such as Basculegion-M , Aegislash , and Mega Floette . Additionally, Kingambit's typing allows it to defensively answer both Glimmora 's and Mega Gengar 's STAB moves. Sucker Punch : Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed and threatens faster Pokemon such as Basculegion-M. Sucker Punch is also useful for late-game one-on-ones, as it pressures the opponent to guess whether Kingambit will choose Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Low Kick : Iron Head is used to threaten Mega Floette, Mega Meganium , and Sylveon while dealing decent damage to Sneasler . Low Kick is used to threaten opposing Kingambit, Incineroar , and Tyranitar . However, Kingambit cannot damage the Fairy-types and Sneasler much if it opts for Low Kick. Other Options Swords Dance : Swords Dance allows Kingambit to become a setup sweeper. This move is typically seen with Black Glasses to maximize damage, as Black Glasses- and Swords Dance-boosted Sucker Punch can OHKO Mega Charizard Y and frailer Garchomp . However, Low Kick and Iron Head tend to be more consistent moves and preferred over Swords Dance, as Kingambit prefers trading damage rather than becoming a setup sweeper in this metagame. SP Spreads 20 HP / 25 Atk / 21 Spe with Adamant : This alternative SP spread allows Kingambit to outspeed bulkier Mega Gengar in Tailwind and some Corviknight , and the HP investment lets it survive bulky Sneasler's Close Combat with Chople Berry. The rest of the SPs have been put into Attack to maximize damage. Items Chople Berry : In conjunction with its standard SP spread, Kingambit can survive Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, as well as opposing Kingambit's and Tyranitar's Low Kick. Black Glasses : Black Glasses allows Kingambit to deal more damage with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch always OHKOes Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and can OHKO snow-boosted Mega Froslass most of the time. Abilities Defiant : This ability allows Kingambit to punish Icy Wind Milotic , Incineroar, and even Moonblast's Special Attack drops from Mega Floette and Whimsicott . Defiant's boost allows Kingambit to OHKO Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Even with Chople Berry, Kingambit does not have the best matchup against Sneasler. Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar and Close Combat from Aegislash threaten to OHKO Kingambit as well. Without Iron Head, Mega Floette and Sylveon will outdamage Kingambit. Mega Charizard Y is faster than Kingambit and will threaten to OHKO it, while Excadrill and Garchomp are Ground-types that threaten it super effectively. Even though Kingambit has a decent matchup against Tyranitar, losing speed control can result in Kingambit losing, since Tyranitar can hit it with Low Kick before it can move. Good Partners and Synergies : Kingambit likes being on balance-oriented teams where it can utilize its great bulk. Basculegion-M can cover for Kingambit's Fighting, Fire, and Ground weaknesses; Mega Charizard Y can cover for its Fighting and Ground weaknesses; and Mega Floette and Sylveon can cover for its Fighting weakness. Basculegion-M and Sinistcha can block Sneasler's Close Combat and, in Sinistcha's case, set up Trick Room for Kingambit. Garchomp can threaten opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Tyranitar. Basculegion-M and Sneasler are Kingambit's best partners overall, as Sneasler can threaten opposing Kingambit and Mega Scovillain , while Basculegion-M can threaten Excadrill and Glimmora. How to Overcome Kingambit's Weaknesses : Position Kingambit out of the face of Sneasler to let Kingambit's partners take care of it. Aerodactyl can OHKO Sneasler with Dual Wingbeat and set up Tailwind for Kingambit's other partners. Having Ghost-type Pokemon in the back such as Basculegion-M and Sinistcha as switch-ins to Sneasler's Close Combat is a good idea to cover for Kingambit's Fighting weakness. It is a good idea to have Garchomp and Kingambit on the field at the same time, as they perfectly cover for each other's weaknesses; Kingambit covers Pokemon such as Alolan Ninetales , Mega Froslass, and Mega Gardevoir , while Garchomp handles Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and opposing Kingambit.

movesets.name: Fake Out Pivot
movesets.description_plain: Incineroar is the premier support Pokemon in all of VGC, using Fake Out to deny attacks and constantly cycling said Fake Out while also applying offense stat drops with Parting Shot and Intimidate to gain control of the damage on the board. Thanks to its good natural bulk and exceptional typing, it can switch in with ease on attacks such as the powerful Ghost-type onslaught from the likes of Aegislash and Mega Gengar as well as Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y . Flare Blitz : Flare Blitz allows Incineroar to make use of its high Attack stat, preventing foes from ignoring it especially when the sun is up. Flare Blitz notably threatens Kingambit , which usually scares away Incineroar due to Defiant. Throat Chop versus Darkest Lariat : Throat Chop deals a decent chunk of damage while also preventing sound-based moves; this means common moves such as Sylveon 's and Primarina 's Hyper Voice and opposing Incineroar's Parting Shot are blocked. Darkest Lariat, on the other hand, ignores Archaludon 's Stamina boosts, though that is rather irrelevant in most matchups; the most enticing part of Darkest Lariat is its higher Base Power, allowing Incineroar to always 2HKO Shield forme Aegislash. Parting Shot : Parting Shot allows Incineroar to continuously lower foes' damage. Using Parting Shot also typically allows Incineroar to switch out last due to its low Speed, allowing frailer allies like Sneasler to come in safely. Other Options Protect : By dropping one of Incineroar's STAB attacks, Protect allows it to better position itself around the board. This is almost exclusively seen on Perish trap teams, where Incineroar plays a key role of in using Fake Out and Protect to stall Perish Song turns and then using Parting Shot to pivot around. Will-O-Wisp : Will-O-Wisp allows Incineroar to further weaken physical attacks on top of Intimidate and allows Incineroar to cripple Pokemon immune to Intimidate, namely Defiant Kingambit and Inner Focus Dragonite . Taunt : Taunt notably allows Incineroar to deny Trick Room from Farigiraf and Sinistcha , as well as crippling Pokemon that thrive off of their status moves, especially Whimsicott and Sableye . Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry grants Incineroar more sustainability, allowing it to avoid a 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite 's Hurricane and almost always avoiding a 2HKO from Timid offensive Mega Floette 's Moonblast. Chople Berry : While this is mostly used when Sitrus Berry has already been taken, Chople Berry still has its uses; most notably, it allows Incineroar to survive Close Combat from Sneasler, though only once. Abilities Intimidate : Intimidate is what makes Incineroar so strong; it can switch in, drop the foes' Attack stat, switch out, and repeat that same process over and over again. SP Spreads 32 HP / 20 Def / 12 SpD / 2 Spe with Careful : With the given bulk, Incineroar, after an Intimidate, survives Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M . Additionally, it avoids a 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Bomb, and it survives Hyper Beam from Sylveon and Light of Ruin from Mega Floette. The Speed investment allows Incineroar to outspeed non-invested Tyranitar , possibly letting it get off a crucial Parting Shot. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Incineroar is very prone to the rain teams that plague the format, where Pokemon such as Pelipper , Politoed , and Basculegion-M can all OHKO Incineroar when they're in the rain. Incineroar also struggles against White Herb Sneasler and the less popular White Herb Garchomp , since thanks to White Herb, they can ignore Intimidate and fire back with Close Combat and Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake, respectively. Incineroar also struggles against Rock-type Pokemon due to its inability to damage them hard; these Rock-type Pokemon include Mega Tyranitar , Mega Aerodactyl , Mega Glimmora , and their base formes. Good Partners and Synergies : Sinistcha is a great defensive partner for Incineroar, switching into the many Fighting-, Ground-, and Water-type moves that would threaten Incineroar, while Incineroar can switch into the Fire-, Dark-, and Ghost-type attacks that threaten Sinistcha. Sinistcha also provides Trick Room for Incineroar to circumvent its relatively low Speed. Offensively, Basculegion-M threatens the many Rock-types that beat Incineroar and opposing Fire-types as well as walling most Sneasler out entirely. Mega Gengar can do the same to Sneasler, while Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Sneasler with Dual Wingbeat. Mega Charizard Y can prevent Pelipper and Politoed from hitting Incineroar with a super effective Weather Ball and can threaten Water-types with Solar Beam. Incineroar also functions well on Perish trap teams, working as a slow pivot that can use Fake Out to prevent foes from doing much while their Perish Song counters ticks down. How to Overcome Incineroar’s Weaknesses : Bringing Pokemon that heavily benefit from the support Incineroar provides, such as Calm Mind Mega Floette and Mega Charizard Y, allows you to use it to its full potential; these Pokemon deal huge damage, compensating for Incineroar's passivity and allowing your team to break through would-be threats like Garchomp and Archaludon. Building your team with some way to circumvent rain is also advised, as this lets Incineroar avoid the powerful Water-type Weather Ball from Pelipper. Mega Charizard Y is the most effective, as it also matches up well against Sneasler that decide to forego Rock Slide; however, Incineroar doesn't typically fit on Mega Charizard Y structures due to stacking of Fire-types, so alternative weathers from the likes of Mega Froslass and Mega Tyranitar can also work.

movesets.name: Offensive Stealth Rock
movesets.description_plain: Garchomp's excellent Speed tier and power make it one of the premier offensive choices for setting up Stealth Rock. Outrage : Despite this set usually being used early-game to set up Stealth Rock, Outrage still gives Garchomp good cleaning potential and makes it a decent revenge killer if Focus Sash is still intact. Rock Tomb versus Poison Jab : Rock Tomb is a perfect fit for the early-game playstyle of this set, ensuring foes like Mega Gyarados and Dragonite won't be able to set up Dragon Dance freely after Garchomp's Focus Sash is broken, in addition to being a great response to both Mega Charizard formes. Focus Sash : Despite Garchomp's above average bulk, its sheer prominence means enough Pokemon are aiming to OHKO it, which makes Focus Sash worth using for the more reliable Stealth Rock setup. Other Options Poison Jab : If Mega Meganium is a serious issue for your team, Poison Jab can potentially flip that matchup. Dragon Tail : While usually better sorted towards more defensive Garchomp sets, Dragon Tail still has merit due to preventing bulky Steel-types like Iron Defense Corviknight and Swords Dance Mega Scizor from setting up.

• Garchomp's excellent Speed tier and power make it one of the premier offensive choices for setting up Stealth Rock.

  • Outrage: Despite this set usually being used early-game to set up Stealth Rock, Outrage still gives Garchomp good cleaning potential and makes it a decent revenge killer if Focus Sash is still intact.

  • Rock Tomb versus Poison Jab: Rock Tomb is a perfect fit for the early-game playstyle of this set, ensuring foes like Mega Gyarados and Dragonite won't be able to set up Dragon Dance freely after Garchomp's Focus Sash is broken, in addition to being a great response to both Mega Charizard formes.

  • Focus Sash: Despite Garchomp's above average bulk, its sheer prominence means enough Pokemon are aiming to OHKO it, which makes Focus Sash worth using for the more reliable Stealth Rock setup.

  • Dragon Tail: While usually better sorted towards more defensive Garchomp sets, Dragon Tail still has merit due to preventing bulky Steel-types like Iron Defense Corviknight and Swords Dance Mega Scizor from setting up.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description_plain: Garchomp's good bulk and coverage place it near the top of the food chain of Swords Dance sweepers! Scale Shot : Scale Shot's reliability issues and reduction of Garchomp's bulk may make it seem like a strange choice for a sweeper, but the Speed boost makes Garchomp so much harder to revenge kill that it's worth it overall. Poison Jab versus Fire Fang : Poison Jab punctures through Mega Meganium , which otherwise can wall and revenge kill Garchomp fairly easily, as well as dealing with the rare Mega Clefable . Fire Fang, however weak it may be, is Garchomp's best shot of chewing through a weakened Corviknight , which otherwise is a strong Garchomp check. Other Options Outrage : Outrage makes Garchomp very vulnerable to being revenge killed, but its perfect accuracy and sheer power make it worth considering. Outrage pairs especially well with Lum Berry to cure confusion and block Yawn from Hippowdon , which is almost always 2HKOed by boosted Outrage even when it chomps down on a Sitrus Berry! Items Focus Sash : Focus Sash severely punishes teams that are unable to set up Stealth Rock, in addition to enhancing Garchomp's revenge killing capabilities. The vulnerability to entry hazards does sometimes conflict with this set's preference for late-game sweeping, though. Lum Berry : Lum Berry is an excellent response to common status users like Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash , leaving even less defensive answers for Garchomp. Life Orb : Life Orb gives Garchomp a tremendous power boost, now being able to OHKO offensive Mega Metagross without a boost! This comes at the cost of the recoil making Garchomp more vulnerable to priority attacks. Haban Berry : Choice Scarf Dragon-types such as opposing Garchomp and Hydreigon are common enough where Haban Berry can be useful to put less pressure on boosting Speed with Scale Shot. Roseli Berry : Roseli Berry can be a deadly surprise for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and bulky Primarina that are expecting to revenge kill Garchomp.

  • Outrage: Outrage makes Garchomp very vulnerable to being revenge killed, but its perfect accuracy and sheer power make it worth considering. Outrage pairs especially well with Lum Berry to cure confusion and block Yawn from Hippowdon, which is almost always 2HKOed by boosted Outrage even when it chomps down on a Sitrus Berry!

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash severely punishes teams that are unable to set up Stealth Rock, in addition to enhancing Garchomp's revenge killing capabilities. The vulnerability to entry hazards does sometimes conflict with this set's preference for late-game sweeping, though.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is an excellent response to common status users like Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash, leaving even less defensive answers for Garchomp.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb gives Garchomp a tremendous power boost, now being able to OHKO offensive Mega Metagross without a boost! This comes at the cost of the recoil making Garchomp more vulnerable to priority attacks.

  • Haban Berry: Choice Scarf Dragon-types such as opposing Garchomp and Hydreigon are common enough where Haban Berry can be useful to put less pressure on boosting Speed with Scale Shot.

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry can be a deadly surprise for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and bulky Primarina that are expecting to revenge kill Garchomp.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description_plain: Garchomp's impressive power, Speed, and bulk make it arguably among the apex Choice Scarf revenge killers of Pokemon Champions Singles! Outrage : While locking Garchomp into a Rampaging state makes it easy prey for Fairy-types like Primarina and Mimikyu , the power Outrage offers turns Garchomp into a ferocious late-game cleaner and an effective revenge killer of most Dragon-type foes. Poison Jab : Poison Jab is Garchomp's preferred Fairy-type deterrent, OHKOing offensive Mega Meganium after Stealth Rock and usually 2HKOing the rare Mega Clefable as well. Rock Tomb versus Dragon Claw : Rock Tomb not only OHKOes Mega Charizard Y but also ensures that fast setup sweepers that may come in after the KO such as Dragon Dance Dragonite and opposing Swords Dance Garchomp will be easier to revenge kill thanks to the Speed drop. Dragon Claw, on the other hand, is Garchomp's most reliable Dragon-type STAB move, perfect for revenge killing weakened Dragon-types without fearing the wrath of Fairy-types getting a free KO. Jolly versus Adamant : Opposing Choice Scarf Garchomp are common enough that Jolly is the safer nature to use; Jolly also lets Garchomp outspeed Jolly Mega Dragonite . However, Adamant's power boost does make Garchomp a better late-game cleaner, granting it a good chance of OHKOing Mega Delphox with Outrage for example. Other Options Stealth Rock : Stealth Rock may seem nonsensical on a revenge killer, but it does give Garchomp some early-game utility if fitting in a more dedicated Stealth Rock setter is difficult for your team, at the cost of some revenge killing prowess. It also can be used to fool your opponent into thinking this set doesn't have Choice Scarf. Rock Slide : While it offers less utility than Rock Tomb, Rock Slide's flinch chance has the potential to flip a bad matchup. Iron Head : Poison Jab is usually preferred due to OHKOing Mega Meganium, but Iron Head's flinch chance could flip matchups against Fairy-types Garchomp can't OHKO, such as Mega Clefable, Mega Floette , and Sylveon . Additionally, Iron Head KOes Mimikyu after Disguise is broken without Stealth Rock support.

movesets.name: Chonky Chomp (Phazer)
movesets.description_plain: Garchomp uses its fantastic bulk to inflict double trouble, placing entry hazards and using Dragon Tail to disrupt and rack up damage on opposing teams. Spikes : Combining Spikes with Stealth Rock can make it much harder for defensive staples like Hippowdon to stay healthy throughout a match. Rock Slide : Even without Attack investment, Rock Slide is still strong enough to OHKO offensive Mega Charizard Y . SP Spread : The given SP spread has enough physical bulk to avoid the OHKO from opposing Jolly Garchomp's Outrage as well as Mega Kangaskhan 's Ice Punch if using Sitrus Berry. The special bulk investment allows Garchomp to dodge the OHKO from Modest Primarina 's Moonblast and Mega Gengar 's Icy Wind. The leftover SPs are put into Speed. Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry's burst recovery helps Garchomp stay healthy and continue to be a nuisance. Particularly after big attacks like Primarina's Moonblast, Garchomp can heal out of range of a follow-up Aqua Jet. Haban Berry : Haban Berry is the most reliable method of letting Garchomp tank Draco Meteor from the likes of Archaludon and Hydreigon .

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Bulky Garchomp utilizes its high Speed and Attack in conjunction with defensive items to become an all-rounder that can be brought to almost any matchup, with coverage to threaten top Pokemon like Sneasler , Mega Charizard Y , opposing Garchomp, and sometimes even Mega Floette . Rock Slide vs Stomping Tantrum : Rock Slide allows Garchomp to fish for flinches and threaten Mega Charizard Y with serious damage. Stomping Tantrum, on the other hand, offers a secondary, single-target Ground-type STAB option, bypassing Wide Guard from Aegislash and Aerodactyl and giving Garchomp the ability to threaten Ground-type damage without also threatening its partner with Earthquake. Protect vs Poison Jab : Protect is an amazing tool for any team, allowing Garchomp to defensively position itself throughout the game. Poison Jab can be run to threaten Fairy-types, namely Mega Floette, Sylveon , and Whimsicott ; it is only run on Garchomp sets with Roseli Berry, because Poison Jab commonly misses OHKOs and Roseli Berry lets Garchomp take a Fairy-type attack before finishing the job with another Poison Jab. Other Options Rock Tomb : Rock Tomb, similar to Rock Slide, provides coverage against Mega Charizard Y but avoids Wide Guard from the likes of Aerodactyl. It also provides a form of Speed control but is really only useful against Mega Charizard Y because of its inability to fish for flinches or damage both foes. Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry grants Garchomp far more longevity by allowing it to avoid 2HKOs from attacks such as Close Combat from Sneasler. Roseli Berry : Roseli Berry allows Garchomp to take on the format's Fairy-types when used in combination with Poison Jab in one-on-one scenarios. Abilities Rough Skin : Rough Skin punishes attacks like Close Combat and Liquidation from Sneasler and Basculegion-M , respectively, breaking their Focus Sashes. It also punishes Fake Out from Incineroar ; at low HP, Incineroar often cannot afford to use Fake Out on Garchomp without KOing itself. SP Spreads 19 HP / 26 Atk / 21 Spe with Jolly : The Attack investment allows Garchomp to OHKO uninvested Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide, while the Speed investment lets it outrun maximum Speed Hisuian Arcanine . The bulk allows Garchomp to almost always survive Last Respects from Basculegion-M after two of its allies have fainted and always survive Knock Off from Jolly Mega Tyranitar after a Dragon Dance. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Even with Roseli Berry, Garchomp can struggle against Fairy-types, as Poison Jab doesn't OHKO them, leaving Garchomp vulnerable to being OHKOed by Mega Floette's Light of Ruin and Sylveon's Hyper Beam. Garchomp also struggles to damage Mega Froslass , which can OHKO it with Blizzard. Opposing Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite , Archaludon , and Hydreigon can be issues for Garchomp, as they can survive Dragon Claw or Earthquake and retaliate with Draco Meteor. Without an offensive item like Soft Sand, Garchomp may also struggle to deal damage to the likes of Incineroar and Mega Scovillain , especially after being affected by Intimidate or a burn, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Charizard Y is a great partner for Garchomp, resisting the Fairy-type attacks that threaten Garchomp, OHKOing Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales , and, when the two are next to each other, allowing Garchomp to use Earthquake freely. Fairy-type partners like Whimsicott and Mega Floette can threaten opposing Dragon-types, while partners like Mega and base Glimmora and as well as Sneasler can threaten opposing Fairy-types. How to Overcome Garchomp's Weaknesses : Keeping Garchomp in the back and removing threats to it early on are good ideas, as its amazing coverage lets it easily clean up a lot of the format's common Pokemon. Having switch-ins to Fairy-types is also a must, as they pose a huge threat to Garchomp even with Roseli Berry. Garchomp also appreciates allies that can stay on the field alongside it while it continuously deals damage with Earthquake, such as Mega Aerodactyl , which can provide Tailwind, use Rock Slide to hit opposing Flying-types, and use Dual Wingbeat to weaken and threaten Sinistcha , a Pokemon Garchomp can struggle to hit.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description_plain: Choice Scarf Garchomp is able to leverage its high offensive stats, good typing, and coverage to become a versatile threat fit for many teams; thanks to its Choice Scarf, it can outspeed and deal heavy damage to otherwise faster Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Sneasler . Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum : Earthquake gives Garchomp a strong spread damage option, while Stomping Tantrum offers single-target Ground-type damage when trying to avoid Wide Guard or when positioned next to a Pokemon that is not immune to Earthquake. Knowing when to pick either one is vital, as locking into Earthquake when Garchomp's partner cannot safely take it can lose the game; alternatively, locking into Stomping Tantrum against redirection from the likes of Sinistcha and Vivillon can render Garchomp nearly useless. Rock Slide : Rock Slide allows Garchomp to OHKO or deal heavy damage to Mega Charizard Y . Thanks to Choice Scarf, Garchomp can fish for flinches against fast Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Delphox , a role Garchomp without Choice Scarf is incapable of fulfilling. Other Options Rock Tomb : Rock Tomb is an alternative to Rock Slide, offering speed control and still offering a way to hit Mega Charizard Y hard. It loses the ability to cause flinches and deal spread damage, however. Items Choice Scarf : Choice Scarf allows Garchomp to outrun faster foes such as Mega Froslass and Aerodactyl , allowing it to revenge kill the aforementioned foes before they threaten it with Blizzard or set up Tailwind, respectively. Abilities Rough Skin : Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from foes like Incineroar and Sneasler, providing chip damage and, in Sneasler's case, potentially breaking its Focus Sash. SP Spreads 29 Atk / 15 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant : The SPs invested in Special Defense allow Garchomp to survive Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette , while the Speed investment lets Garchomp outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M when holding a Choice Scarf of its own. The remaining SPs are invested in Attack. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant : This spread opts for more Speed and power, ensuring that Garchomp at least Speed ties other Choice Scarf Garchomp, outspeeds Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash and Mega Aerodactyl , and deals as much damage as possible. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Sylveon , Mega Gardevoir , and Whimsicott all threaten Garchomp with OHKOs or 2HKOs from their Fairy-type STAB attacks while also boasting an immunity to Dragon Claw, easily taking advantage of Garchomp's inability to switch moves. Whimsicott in particular also resists Garchomp's Ground-type STAB attacks and can use Tailwind to allow partners like Mega Floette to outspeed and OHKO Garchomp with Moonblast. Mega Froslass is able to easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard, while Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar can take advantage of Garchomp's inability to use Protect, leaving it vulnerable to attacks such as Draco Meteor from Hydreigon and Archaludon . Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can easily take advantage when Garchomp locks into a Ground-type move, threatening it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively, while Archaludon and opposing Garchomp are able to switch in on Rock Slide and threaten Garchomp with Draco Meteor and Dragon Claw, respectively. Rotom-Wash can also easily take attacks from Garchomp while threatening to burn it with Will-O-Wisp, and Mega Scovillain is able to redirect Garchomp's attacks, burning it in the process. Sinistcha and Farigiraf can set up Trick Room right in front of Garchomp, turning the Speed boost from Choice Scarf into a hindrance. Corviknight resists or, in the case of Ground-type attacks, is immune to all of Garchomp's STAB options, can shrug off Rock Slide, and can either set up Tailwind or use Bulk Up in the face of Garchomp, setting up an ally for success or turning itself into a win condition, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Charizard Y is able to sit next to Garchomp while it freely uses Earthquake and make Blizzard from Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales inaccurate by setting sun. Additionally, it is able to resist Fairy-type attacks and fire back with Weather Ball and Heat Wave while threatening to OHKO Mega Froslass and Sinistcha with the same moves. Incineroar also threatens Mega Froslass and Sinistcha and can safely switch into their attacks while using Fake Out against foes like Hydreigon to keep Garchomp safe for another turn or Parting Shot to safely bring in Garchomp. In return, Garchomp is able to threaten Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Lycanroc-D and deal with opposing non-Choice Scarf Garchomp. Mega Froslass, Sinistcha, and Farigiraf are all threatened by Kingambit 's Kowtow Cleave; Fairy-types fear Iron Head; and Hydreigon and Archaludon take solid damage from Low Kick. Kingambit appreciates Garchomp's positive matchup against Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Mega Floette is able to threaten the Dragon-types Garchomp fears with heavy damage, as well as easily take out Rotom-Wash and take attacks from Mega Froslass before retaliating with Moonblast or Light of Ruin. Mega Aerodactyl deals heavy damage to Sinistcha with Dual Wingbeat, deterring it from attempting to redirect Garchomp's attacks; Mega Aerodactyl is also capable of using Ice Fang to OHKO opposing Garchomp. How to Overcome Garchomp's Weaknesses : Bringing Choice Scarf Garchomp alongside offensive threats that complement it well, such as Mega Charizard Y, is a must to ensure it isn't easily stopped by Pokemon that resist or are immune to whatever move it has decided to lock into. When teambuilding, placing Garchomp on a team with Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type damage is preferred, though not necessary thanks to Garchomp's flexibility, as it often functions as glue for teams. Mega Charizard Y threatens the Fairy- and Ice-type Pokemon that scare away Garchomp and, more importantly, appreciates Garchomp's ability to threaten opposing Mega Charizard Y and Dragon-types with Rock Slide and Dragon Claw, respectively. Mega Floette and Sylveon appreciate Garchomp's Ground-type attacks threatening Kingambit and Sneasler and, in return, provide coverage against problematic Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite. Kingambit and Mega Aerodactyl perform similar roles against Ice-types and other foes that trouble Garchomp, appreciating the wide array of coverage Garchomp has at its disposal to dispatch nearly any Pokemon. Kingambit has the added benefit of deterring Trick Room from Sinistcha and Farigiraf thanks to its naturally low Speed and can hit them hard with Kowtow Cleave.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description_plain: Basculgion-M is enjoying a fantastic offensive type combination in the current metagame, which, when combined with Adaptability, makes it a standout pick as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects and a potent early-game scout with Flip Turn. Choice Scarf : Choice Scarf gives Basculegion-M the Speed it needs to chunk foes and get out safely early-game while also allowing you to bring it in late-game without spending a turn to set up Agility. However, Basculegion-M's pitiful base 78 Speed means that it will be outsped by most of the other Choice Scarf users in the format, as well as most Dragon Dance users, so you need to be careful when positioning Basculegion-M. Wave Crash : Wave Crash will be Basculegion-M's primary early-game damage option if you elect to not pivot it out. Last Respects : Even after just one team member is KOed, Last Respects becomes an extremely potent move that's very difficult to switch into, and it gives Basculegion-M immense sweeping power once both allies have fainted. Flip Turn : Adaptability allows Flip Turn to deal notable damage for a pivoting move. Aqua Jet : Adaptability-boosted Aqua Jet does a considerable amount of damage and can get Basculegion-M out of trouble against other priority users or Speed-boosted foes. Other Options Ice Fang : Ice Fang provides coverage against Dragon-types and threatens Garchomp and Dragonite right out of the gate. Head Smash : Head Smash gives Basculegion-M a heavily damaging coverage option that threatens Gyarados and Dragonite.
movesets.description_html:
• Basculgion-M is enjoying a fantastic offensive type combination in the current metagame, which, when combined with Adaptability, makes it a standout pick as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects and a potent early-game scout with Flip Turn.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf gives Basculegion-M the Speed it needs to chunk foes and get out safely early-game while also allowing you to bring it in late-game without spending a turn to set up Agility. However, Basculegion-M's pitiful base 78 Speed means that it will be outsped by most of the other Choice Scarf users in the format, as well as most Dragon Dance users, so you need to be careful when positioning Basculegion-M.

  • Wave Crash: Wave Crash will be Basculegion-M's primary early-game damage option if you elect to not pivot it out.

  • Last Respects: Even after just one team member is KOed, Last Respects becomes an extremely potent move that's very difficult to switch into, and it gives Basculegion-M immense sweeping power once both allies have fainted.

  • Flip Turn: Adaptability allows Flip Turn to deal notable damage for a pivoting move.

  • Aqua Jet: Adaptability-boosted Aqua Jet does a considerable amount of damage and can get Basculegion-M out of trouble against other priority users or Speed-boosted foes.

Other Options

  • Ice Fang: Ice Fang provides coverage against Dragon-types and threatens Garchomp and Dragonite right out of the gate.

  • Head Smash: Head Smash gives Basculegion-M a heavily damaging coverage option that threatens Gyarados and Dragonite.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description_plain: This Agility set gives Basculegion-M the freedom to outspeed and threaten the majority of its metagame-relevant foes while enabling it to use multiple moves. Opposing Priority Users : While setting up Agility can make Basculegion-M an absolutely terrifying sweeper, late-game checks such as Aegislash , Mimikyu , and Kingambit are quite popular in the current metagame, so be careful when you see these during Team Preview. Adamant Nature : Agility's boost is going to give Basculegion-M plenty of Speed to set up its sweep. As Basculegion-M lacks an Attack-boosting setup move, an Adamant nature is preferred over Jolly. Adamant Basculegion-M is already outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp with an Agility boost, while a Jolly nature won't allow it to outspeed the likes of Choice Scarf Jolly Meowscarada . Items Mystic Water versus Spell Tag : These items will allow Basculegion-M's STAB moves to do hilariously high damage. Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon with Wave Crash and has the added bonus of juicing up Aqua Jet's damage when it needs to rely on priority. On the other hand, Spell Tag will allow Last Respects to tear through walls, letting it OHKO maximum HP Mega Scizor after Stealth Rock at 150 Base Power. Focus Sash : Focus Sash ensures that Basculegion-M is going to tank a hit while it sets up Agility, but because entry hazards are very popular in the current metagame, saving your Focus Sash user for last can be a risky venture.

movesets.name: Revenge Killer
movesets.description_plain: Basculegion-M is one of the strongest revenge killers in the metagame, able to function both with and without rain. Along with acting as an offensive pivot against opposing frail leads, Basculegion-M also offers the ability to constantly threaten an OHKO on several common threats and Mega Evolutions, such as Aerodactyl , Talonflame , Mega Tyranitar , and Mega Charizard Y . Basculegion-M also possesses relatively decent natural bulk, allowing it to survive the occasional neutral hit. Basculegion-M's bulk also lets it act as a late-game sweeper more reliably by making use of its allies to remove its checks in the early game or to ultimately expend enough of the opponent's resources to allow Basculegion-M to enter, outspeed, and then brute force stragglers through the use of Last Respects or Wave Crash. Last Respects : Last Respects's damage, when powered up by fallen allies, is often enough to OHKO most of the common non-Ghost-resistant metagame threats even after defensive investment. Still, it is generally recommended to avoid locking into the move before allies have started fainting to allow Last Respects to reach its coveted OHKO capabilities. 150 Base Power is a reliable goal to hit once Basculegion-M settles on the field, as Last Respects becomes able to OHKO common Water-resistant foes such as Pelipper and Rotom-Wash , which would otherwise survive a Wave Crash even under rain. Aqua Jet : Aqua Jet is used to allow Basculegion-M to finish off low-health targets and ensure damage when you're on the back foot, with the added benefit of allowing Basculegion-M to potentially evade Kingambit 's Sucker Punch. Positioning : Flip Turn is Basculegion-M's primary tool to pivot and reset momentum. Basculegion-M largely prefers not being led with, due to the predictability of being locked into a move and lack of Base Power. Flip Turn, when combined with Choice Scarf, also allows Basculegion-M to put in some chip damage and reset unfavorable positioning before the opponent's Pokemon can move. The set thrives on picking off weakened foes, so priority should be placed on removing threats to Basculegion-M. Other Options Icy Wind : Icy Wind may be used as a speed control replacement over Aqua Jet, sacrificing a priority option for the ability to drop the foe's Speed before they can move and break Focus Sash with its chip damage. It also heavily chips Garchomp , which is particularly vulnerable to it in the early-game. If you opt for this move, greater caution should be exercised when positioning Basculegion-M, as it will offer very little damage while locked into the move and will also invite opposing switch-ins. Kingambit and Milotic are potentially catastrophic; not only do they resist Icy Wind, but it will also trigger Defiant and Competitive, respectively. Items Choice Scarf : A Choice Scarf will allow Basculegion-M to reach Talonflame's Speed and outspeed the most common options above base 100 Speed, such as Sneasler , Mega Floette , and Mega Froslass . Abilities Adaptability : Adaptability allows Basculegion-M to pick up several key OHKOs; Wave Crash threatens a reliable OHKO on Aerodactyl, its Mega Evolution, and Excadrill . Meanwhile, 150-Base Power Last Respects will reliably remove many common neutral targets, like Sneasler and Talonflame, and it also threatens a potential OHKO against most Mega Floette sets. SP Spreads Jolly : A Jolly nature may be chosen to outpace Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox , which would otherwise outspeed Basculegion-M and, in Mega Gengar's case, threaten it with super effective damage. This will also allow Basculegion-M to outspeed Aerodactyl and Talonflame, which allows Basculegion-M to potentially deny them from setting Tailwind. Adamant : An Adamant nature allows Wave Crash to OHKO uninvested Mega Floette as well as Maushold and 150-Base Power Last Respects to OHKO Mega Scovillain semi-reliably. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Priority attackers pose the biggest threat to Basculegion-M. Kingambit is at the forefront of said threats, as it can threaten Basculegion with Sucker Punch for an OHKO while often having enough bulk to survive a rain-boosted Wave Crash. Basculegion-M is also threatened by bulky Water-resistant pokemon, particularly Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur that can hit it for super effective damage in return. Archaludon poses a serious threat to Basculegion-M in the rain with its Electro Shot and high physical bulk supplemented by Stamina. Basculegion-M's Speed tier means it will often be outran by other Choice Scarf users, like Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Vivillion, and especially speedy threats such as Mega Aerodactyl , and it's also particularly vulnerable to foes' Tailwind if it's unmatched. Common sun leads, such as Whimsicott with its Prankster ability, can specifically pose an indirect threat to Basculegion-M, nullifying its Speed advantage or forcing weather control through Sunny Day. Good Partners and Synergies : Basculegion-M is part of a known core made up of Sneasler, Kingambit, and itself. Basculegion-M appreciates Sneasler's capability to remove threats such as Kingambit and Incineroar with its Close Combat while also offering Fake Out support to help Basculegion-M with repositioning. Sneasler can cover many of Basculegion-M's weaknesses while being a fine choice to lead, which Basculegion-M specifically tends to avoid. Archaludon walls Basculegion-M early-game but lacks Stamina's Defense boost, which makes it particularly susceptible to Sneasler leads. Kingambit rounds out the trio by discouraging Intimidate through its Defiant ability and threatening Farigiraf , which is immune to Basculegion-M's Last Respects, while also discouraging Trick Room thanks to its lower Speed tier. Kingambit also renders the matchup against opposing Choice Scarf Basculegion-M less volatile by pressuring them with Sucker Punch, letting Basculegion-M avoid a Speed tie. Basculegion-M appreciates Pelipper's ability to set rain, which boosts its damage output and enables it to outspeed faster Choice Scarf users by setting Tailwind. Also, Pelipper's Hurricane provides coverage against bulky Grass-types that may otherwise threaten Basculegion-M like Sinistcha and Venusaur . How to Overcome Basculegion-M's Weaknesses : Basculegion-M's primary weakness to priority and susceptibility to Intimidate and common sun leads means it greatly appreciates being with partners with access to pivoting moves such as Incineroar with Parting Shot, which through its typing and bulk can be an effective defensive pivot that can sponge hits, particularly from Dark-, Ghost-, and Grass-type attacks that threaten Basculegion-M. Redirection users such as Sinistcha and Mega Scovillain are also greatly appreciated as a way to keep Basculegion-M safe from priority such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and any threatening single-target damage. Fake Out users like Sneasler and the previously mentioned Incineroar can buy the time for Basculegion-M to pivot out safely or get a key attack off. Basculegion-M overall greatly appreciates being paired with Tailwind users like Talonflame and Pelipper, as they allow Basculegion-M to overcome its weakness to faster Choice Scarf users, as well as avoiding the Speed tie with other Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. Weather control options such as Pelipper with Drizzle and Sableye with Rain Dance bolster Basculegion-M's power, allowing Wave Crash to score otherwise unattainable OHKOs on Pokemon like Sylveon while also counteracting the potential damage loss incurred from opposing sun teams. Allies like Sneasler and Garchomp, with their Fighting- and Ground-type coverage, respectively, help deal with Basculegion-M's biggest obstacle: Kingambit.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Basculegion-M is able to output monstrous amounts of damage with the combination of Adaptability and its high-Base Power moves. This set takes advantage of its strong natural bulk to ease matchups that would otherwise heavily favor the opponent, such as Kingambit and Mega Gengar , while still maintaining offensive prowess through the use of Mystic Water or using Sitrus Berry to alleviate Wave Crash's recoil damage. Wave Crash : Wave Crash is Basculegion-M's most consistent STAB move, allowing it to threaten Trick Room setters such as Farigiraf , as Basculegion-M's bulk usually isn't enough to outlast Trick Room, while also OHKOing or 2HKOing most Pokemon. Crucially, it lets Basculegion-M OHKO Sneasler . In combination with its defensive typing, Basculegion-M can almost always serve as a band-aid for Sneasler-weak teams. Last Respects : This move allows Basculegion-M to function as a late-game sweeper, letting it OHKO most Pokemon in the format after two of its allies faint. However, it is also usable after just one ally has fainted, usually in situations where Wave Crash recoil needs to be avoided. At 100 Base Power, it is able to OHKO Pokemon such as non-Kasib Berry Sinistcha , Mega Froslass , and Sneasler. Items Mystic Water : Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to reach OHKOs on important metagame threats such as bulky Mega Floette , bulky Mega Gengar, and medium-bulk Mega Charizard Y in the sun with Wave Crash. Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry allows Basculegion-M to heal enough to safely use Wave Crash instead of knocking itself out due to recoil damage. This can be important against Pokemon such as Kingambit, which would invalidate Wave Crash as an option after a Sucker Punch.

movesets.name: Focus Sash Attacker
movesets.description_plain: This Basculegion-M set utilizes Focus Sash to mitigate Basculegion-M's worst matchups, allowing it to deal consistent damage without having to reposition in front of Kingambit or Mega Gengar , as Focus Sash allows it to survive a hit and threaten heavy damage in return. Liquidation : This set uses Liquidation instead of Wave Crash, as the recoil damage from Wave Crash would invalidate Focus Sash. While it does not threaten OHKOs in the same fashion as Wave Crash, Liquidation still allows Basculegion-M to threaten Dark-types such as Incineroar , Kingambit, and Tyranitar . It also allows Basculegion-M to threaten an OHKO on foes such as Mega Delphox at the start of the match. Items Focus Sash : Focus Sash lets Basculegion-M safely threaten the likes of Mega Gengar and Mega Froslass , even without speed control or redirection. It pairs well with Basculegion-M's Ghost typing, preventing Fake Out from breaking Focus Sash. However, it does mean that Basculegion-M cannot attack Garchomp effectively until at least one ally has fainted due to Last Respects' low Base Power and Garchomp's Rough Skin breaking Focus Sash if Basculegion-M hits it with Liquidation or Aqua Jet. SP Spreads 16 HP / 24 Atk / 6 Def / 20 Spe with Adamant : This spread allows Basculegion-M to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp in Tailwind while always surviving Sucker Punch from non-Black Glasses Kingambit. It is also able to almost always survive Shadow Ball from bulky Mega Gengar and Timid Mega Froslass. The Attack investment allows Basculegion-M to always OHKO bulky Mega Floette with Wave Crash when equipped with Mystic Water. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant : This spread is only used by Focus Sash Basculegion-M, as it does not need any bulk and instead prefers to maximize its damage output and Speed. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Kingambit is Basculegion-M's biggest enemy. It is bulky enough to survive Wave Crash while resisting Last Respects and not taking much damage from Liquidation. On top of that, it threatens Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, both of which are able to OHKO Basculegion-M when Kingambit is holding Black Glasses. Sinistcha is also able to take all of Basculegion-M's moves if Last Respects has no Base Power boosts, and it can redirect them while its partner takes out Basculegion-M. Alternatively, Sinistcha can threaten Basculegion-M directly with Matcha Gotcha. However, once one of Basculegion-M's allies has fainted, Last Respects will almost always OHKO Sinistcha unless it is holding Kasib Berry. If using Mystic Water or Sitrus Berry without speed control, opposing Basculegion-M and Mega Charizard Y also check it, as Basculegion-M is OHKOed by Last Respects and Solar Beam, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies : While not necessary for Basculegion-M to function, it appreciates speed control such as Trick Room or Tailwind, as it lets Basculegion-M beat tough matchups such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Gengar. Mega Floette is a great partner, as it threatens Kingambit and Archaludon with Light of Ruin. It is also able to OHKO Garchomp, which Basculegion-M can sometimes regret targeting due to the additional recoil from Rough Skin adding up quickly with Wave Crash's recoil. Kingambit can also support Basculegion-M, as it OHKOs opposing Ghost-types such as Basculegion-M and Sinistcha. Additionally, if Kingambit has Low Kick, it is able to help clear opposing Kingambit out for Basculegion-M while also covering Kingambit's biggest weakness, Sneasler . On top of that, Kingambit deters Intimidate from opposing Incineroar, which would otherwise be especially effective against Basculegion-M. How to Overcome Basculegion-M's Weaknesses : Due to Basculegion-M's coverage and defensive options, very little can explicitly force it to switch out. While Sneasler and Mega Floette help with Sinistcha and Kingambit, an allied Kingambit can also take care of Mega Gengar and Mega Froslass. Additionally, it threatens Sinistcha, and, if holding Chople Berry, it can threaten opposing Kingambit with Low Kick. As such, when Basculegion-M is being threatened, it can use Protect while a partner mitigates the threat. Examples include setting speed control such as Tailwind with Whimsicott or Talonflame or simply knocking out the threat if Basculegion-M cannot hit it for significant damage. Setting up Basculegion-M for success in the late game is also a viable gameplan. When doing so, one should prioritize taking out the likes of Kingambit, Incineroar, and Sinistcha while setting some form of speed control to allow Basculegion-M to outspeed Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Mega Froslass.

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Kingambit is Basculegion-M's biggest enemy. It is bulky enough to survive Wave Crash while resisting Last Respects and not taking much damage from Liquidation. On top of that, it threatens Basculegion-M with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, both of which are able to OHKO Basculegion-M when Kingambit is holding Black Glasses. Sinistcha is also able to take all of Basculegion-M's moves if Last Respects has no Base Power boosts, and it can redirect them while its partner takes out Basculegion-M. Alternatively, Sinistcha can threaten Basculegion-M directly with Matcha Gotcha. However, once one of Basculegion-M's allies has fainted, Last Respects will almost always OHKO Sinistcha unless it is holding Kasib Berry. If using Mystic Water or Sitrus Berry without speed control, opposing Basculegion-M and Mega Charizard Y also check it, as Basculegion-M is OHKOed by Last Respects and Solar Beam, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: While not necessary for Basculegion-M to function, it appreciates speed control such as Trick Room or Tailwind, as it lets Basculegion-M beat tough matchups such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Gengar. Mega Floette is a great partner, as it threatens Kingambit and Archaludon with Light of Ruin. It is also able to OHKO Garchomp, which Basculegion-M can sometimes regret targeting due to the additional recoil from Rough Skin adding up quickly with Wave Crash's recoil. Kingambit can also support Basculegion-M, as it OHKOs opposing Ghost-types such as Basculegion-M and Sinistcha. Additionally, if Kingambit has Low Kick, it is able to help clear opposing Kingambit out for Basculegion-M while also covering Kingambit's biggest weakness, Sneasler. On top of that, Kingambit deters Intimidate from opposing Incineroar, which would otherwise be especially effective against Basculegion-M.

  • How to Overcome Basculegion-M's Weaknesses: Due to Basculegion-M's coverage and defensive options, very little can explicitly force it to switch out. While Sneasler and Mega Floette help with Sinistcha and Kingambit, an allied Kingambit can also take care of Mega Gengar and Mega Froslass. Additionally, it threatens Sinistcha, and, if holding Chople Berry, it can threaten opposing Kingambit with Low Kick. As such, when Basculegion-M is being threatened, it can use Protect while a partner mitigates the threat. Examples include setting speed control such as Tailwind with Whimsicott or Talonflame or simply knocking out the threat if Basculegion-M cannot hit it for significant damage. Setting up Basculegion-M for success in the late game is also a viable gameplan. When doing so, one should prioritize taking out the likes of Kingambit, Incineroar, and Sinistcha while setting some form of speed control to allow Basculegion-M to outspeed Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Mega Froslass.

movesets.name: Redirection Support
movesets.description_plain: Sinistcha is the go-to redirector in the Regulation M-A metagame, setting itself apart from other redirectors with its immunity to Fake Out, good defensive stats, access to Trick Room, and Hospitality. Its typing allows it to support metagame-defining threats well, redirecting away moves such as Sneasler 's Close Combat and Dire Claw, as well as Water-type moves and Electro Shot from rain teams. Trick Room versus Protect : Trick Room is useful to turn the tables on fast threats, like Chlorophyll Venusaur , and Tailwind, even when it necessarily isn't used for a Trick Room sweeper. However, Protect can be used over Trick Room if there is conflict with other speed control options on Sinistcha's team or to give Sinistcha another tool to assist with positioning itself or other teammates. Life Dew versus Protect : Life Dew is great for partners with setup moves, particularly Calm Mind Mega Floette . When using Trick Room, Protect could be used over Life Dew to help position Sinistcha to safely set it up. For instance, Sinistcha can use Protect while its partner switches to a Fake Out user, which would then give it a better opportunity to set Trick Room. Other Options Strength Sap : Strength Sap is a rather effective self-healing option, in addition to being a way to manage physical threats such as Garchomp and Incineroar . Shadow Ball : Shadow Ball is a more proactive tool to help manage the common Ghost-types in the metagame, such as other Sinistcha, Mega Gengar , Mega Froslass , and Ceruledge , as well as some Psychic-types like Mega Delphox . Items Kasib Berry : With Kasib Berry, Basculegion-M can't OHKO Sinistcha with a 150-Base Power Last Respects, while Sinistcha resists its Water-type STAB moves and threatens to both 2HKO Basculegion-M with Matcha Gotcha. Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry is useful for general healing and helps Sinistcha avoid 2HKOs from attacks such as Fairy Feather Sylveon 's Hyper Voice, Mega Floette's Moonblast, Mega Aerodactyl 's Dual Wingbeat after Intimidate, and Incineroar's Flare Blitz after Intimidate. Colbur Berry : Colbur Berry is most useful to help manage Kingambit , allowing Sinistcha to take a Kowtow Cleave more easily; instead of requiring Sinistcha to stay at full HP to survive Kowtow Cleave, it only needs half of its HP. This allows Sinistcha to more safely use Rage Powder in front of Kingambit, nullifying Sucker Punch and allowing its partner to attack safely. SP Spreads 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Bold : The Defense investment allows Sinistcha to avoid being OHKOed by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The rest of the SPs are invested into Special Defense for general bulk. A Relaxed nature could also be used for Trick Room, though it doesn't allow Sinistcha to underspeed anything noteworthy aside from other Sinistcha. 32 HP / 11 Def / 23 SpD with Calm This spread allows Sinistcha to more effectively redirect special attacks, notably Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball, with the remaining SPs invested into Defense. More Special Defense could be used to live attacks such as Timid Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, though it comes at the cost of taking more damage from common physical attackers like Kingambit and Incineroar. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Sinistcha has many exploitable weaknesses, most notably Mega Charizard Y 's sun-boosted Heat Wave, which both ignores Rage Powder and OHKOes Sinistcha. Mega Froslass with Blizzard and Mega Delphox with Heat Wave are similarly effective against Rage Powder Sinistcha, (AC) even if they don't OHKO it. Mega Aerodactyl with Dual Wingbeat and Kingambit with Kowtow Cleave do significant damage to Sinistcha. Ceruledge can 2HKO Sinistcha with Bitter Blade or OHKO it after a Bulk Up while resisting Matcha Gotcha and being immune to burn. Basculegion-M, while being 2HKOed by Matcha Gotcha, can threaten an OHKO with a boosted Last Respects unless Sinistcha holds a Kasib Berry. Mega Tyranitar is similar; it can outright OHKO Sinistcha with Knock Off and is naturally faster than Sinistcha to avoid Matcha Gotcha. Incineroar both resists and cannot be burned by Matcha Gotcha, and it can chunk Sinistcha for around half its health with Throat Chop or for even more with Flare Blitz. Pelipper is often a rain team's first line of defense against Sinistcha, as its Hurricane OHKOes it after slight chip damage. Good Partners and Synergies : Hospitality makes Sinistcha a great partner for Mega Floette, which also appreciates redirection for threatening attacks like Sneasler's Dire Claw or Gunk Shot while it sets up. Mega Floette can then threaten to OHKO Sinistcha checks such as Kingambit with a +1 Moonblast or spread damage with Dazzling Gleam. Other Pokemon that use boosting moves can naturally make excellent use of Sinistcha's redirection and Hospitality. Black Glasses Swords Dance Kingambit and Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar are a couple of Pokemon that appreciate being able to set up in the face of extremely effective Close Combats from Sneasler and can threaten Sinistcha's checks; they outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Sucker Punch and Rock Slide, respectively, after a boost. Slower Pokemon such as Kingambit and non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can most effectively take advantage of Sinistcha's Trick Room. Overcoming Sinistcha's Weaknesses : Incineroar can both make use of the extra healing and complements Sinistcha's typing near-perfectly, forming a core that can switch into each other's weaknesses and repeatedly activate Intimidate and Hospitality. Fake Out can help ensure Trick Room is set up, and Parting Shot can also allow Sinistcha to heal a teammate in the same turn by switching out Sinistcha, using Parting Shot, then switching it back in again mid-turn. While Incineroar does give Kingambit a Defiant boost, it still resists Kingambit's STAB moves and threatens to 2HKO with Flare Blitz. Similar to Incineroar, Basculegion-M both resists Fire and has access to Flip Turn to pivot. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can also threaten key threats to Sinistcha such as Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Delphox with its speedy Wave Crash, and although Mega Charizard Y can mitigate the damage with Drought, it will still be easily 2HKOed with Wave Crash while Sinistcha threatens to redirect its Solar Beam. Sneasler threatens Kingambit and other Dark-types with STAB Close Combat. Kingambit itself is a good source of Fighting-type damage with Low Kick and a partner Sinistcha is a great way to avoid Low Kick from opposing Kingambit. Kingambit additionally helps overcome Ghost-type threats such as Mega Froslass and Basculegion-M. Garchomp is an excellent check to both Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit, 2HKOing both with Rock Slide and Earthquake, respectively; Mega Charizard Y is even able to be OHKOed if it does not have Defense investment. Pelipper and Politoed effectively neuter Sinistcha's biggest check in Mega Charizard Y, as well as other Fire-types such as Incineroar and Mega Delphox.

strategies.overview_plain: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

movesets.name: Unburden Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: With the powerful Unburden ability, Sneasler can become a dangerous cleaner that wrecks havoc on frailer teams. Throat Chop versus Shadow Claw : When covering Psychic- and Ghost-types, Throat Chop is usually preferred for its higher power over Shadow Claw. However, Adamant Sneasler with Shadow Claw has about a 50/50 chance to knock out offensive Mimikyu after Disguise breaks. Swords Dance : If allowed to set up a Swords Dance, Sneasler can quickly spiral out of control and even overpower Hippowdon and Corviknight if they have been chipped. Fake Out : Fake Out can help get targets into KO range of its more powerful attacks, and the priority helps Sneasler catch faster foes prior to activating Unburden. Adamant versus Jolly : Adamant is usually preferred to maximize sweeping potential, and with Unburden active, Sneasler can effortlessly outrun even Choice Scarf Dragapult . WIth maximum investment, Adamant Sneasler also maintains enough Speed to outrun threats like Mega Glimmora and unboosted Garchomp before Unburden's boost. Jolly gives Sneasler a little more consistency, allowing it to outrun more threats such as Mega Starmie and Focus Sash Gengar before Unburden activates. Other Options Acrobatics : Acrobatics is Sneasler's best move against threats like Mega Venusaur , Volcarona , and opposing Sneasler, though the move's damage is reliant on Sneasler consuming its item beforehand. Rock Slide : Rock Slide landing a clean OHKO on Mega Charizard Y is huge, but its uses are otherwise limited. Fling : Fling with King's Rock or Light Ball is the most flexible method of triggering Sneasler's Unburden, but the sacrifice to damage and coverage makes it a hard sell. Items White Herb : White Herb synergizes fantastically with Sneasler, allowing it to activate Unburden through its best attack Close Combat while also nullifying the defense drops once. White Herb can also function as insurance against Intimidate users. Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry can give the somewhat frail Sneasler a bit more survivability, especially against priority attacks. However, it does make Sneasler reliant on the opponent to trigger Unburden for it. Lum Berry : Lum Berry puts Sneasler into a more niche role for its team, focused on countering status users like Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash .

movesets.name: Offensive Support
movesets.description_plain: Sneasler is the fastest relevant Fake Out user in Regulation M-A, guaranteeing a threat will be halted so that Sneasler's ally can move safely, and it's undoubtedly the fastest Pokemon in the format with Unburden active. Thanks to its STAB combination, Sneasler also threatens many prominent Pokemon like Kingambit , Mega Floette , and Sylveon . Close Combat : In addition to handling Dark- and Normal-types like Incineroar , Mega Tyranitar , and Maushold , Close Combat's drawback can be used with White Herb to grant Sneasler unparalleled Speed. Dire Claw : Though it shouldn't be relied upon, Dire Claw's suite of status conditions can potentially push a critical situation in your favor. Other Options Coaching : Coaching can be slotted over Protect to provide support to physically offensive teammates like Garchomp , as the extra power and bulk granted to such Pokemon can justify the inability to make defensive plays. Rock-type Coverage : Rock Slide and Rock Tomb can be considered to severely damage Mega Charizard Y and Talonflame . Rock Slide deals spread damage and can let you game for flinches, while Rock Tomb is a more reliable alternative that trades damage output for the potential to let Sneasler's teammates hit an otherwise faster foe like Mega Froslass before it moves. Throat Chop : Throat Chop lets Sneasler threaten Ghost-types like Aegislash and Mega Gengar and act as a late-game emergency check to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M with Focus Sash. Gunk Shot : Although it's less accurate than Dire Claw, Gunk Shot's ability to let even Jolly Sneasler one-shot most bulky variants of Mega Floette and Sylveon makes it worth considering. Additionally, Adamant Sneasler's Gunk Shot is very likely to OHKO Mega Delphox . Items White Herb : White Herb is the most common item on Sneasler, as the item grants it on-demand speed control with use of Close Combat. White Herb also gives it a buffer against stat drops incurred by Incineroar's Intimidate and Milotic 's Icy Wind. Focus Sash : Focus Sash generally ensures Sneasler will make at least one move before fainting, though it'll be harder to activate Unburden without a would-be fatal blow. Focus Sash is also a contested item that teammates like Aerodactyl may need to function effectively. Abilities Unburden : Unburden's Speed boost is crucial to outspeed faster foes like Choice Scarf Garchomp, Sand Rush Excadrill , and Chlorophyll Venusaur . SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant or Jolly : An Adamant nature lets Sneasler OHKO maximum HP Sylveon with Dire Claw and have a favored chance to OHKO Chople Berry Kingambit with Close Combat while still outspeeding neutral-natured weather attackers like Venusaur and Excadrill with Unburden active. A Jolly nature allows Sneasler to outspeed opposing Adamant Sneasler, Maushold, and Alolan Ninetales , letting it use Fake Out first against the former; note that positive-natured variants of Venusaur and Excadrill are uncommon. 32 HP / 4 Atk / 29 Def / 1 Spe with Jolly : A bulky spread is an option on White Herb sets to allow Sneasler to survive otherwise deadly attacks and still pack enough power to 2HKO neutral foes like Garchomp with Close Combat. This spread allows it to survive Aerodactyl's and Sharp Beak Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat and Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum while outspeeding Adamant Garchomp and Modest Mega Floette, as well as Jolly Sand Rush Excadrill with Unburden active. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Sneasler is walled by Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Aegislash; they resist Dire Claw and ignore Fake Out and Close Combat, letting them safely come in on predicted attacks. Mega Gengar is a very threatening Ghost-type, as Gengar can force Sneasler out and Mega Evolve to trap its teammates. Sinistcha , in particular, can set up Trick Room and render Sneasler very vulnerable to attacks; Farigiraf accomplishes the same while preventing Fake Out from hitting its team and directly threatening it with Psychic or Twin Beam. Without Unburden active, faster attackers like Choice Scarf Garchomp, Sand Rush Excadrill, Mega Delphox, and Aerodactyl can easily OHKO it, with the latter even bypassing Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat and matching Unburden with Tailwind. Good Partners and Synergies : Kingambit is one of the best partners for Sneasler, as it threatens Ghost-types and prominent Trick Room setters with its STAB Dark-type moves. Basculegion-M appreciates Sneasler's good matchup against opposing Kingambit, which can threaten its late-game sweeps with Sucker Punch, while Dragon-types like Garchomp and Archaludon can safely let their STAB moves loose with opposing Fairy-types removed by Sneasler. How to Overcome Sneasler's Weaknesses : Choosing Kingambit during Team Preview will give Sneasler security when facing Ghost-types alongside it or ensure you have a reliable switch-in to them. Kingambit also benefits from Trick Room, making it a potential counterlead against Sinistcha and Farigiraf. Against faster threats, aim to have Unburden activated by the time they come out; if that's not plausible, priority moves like Kingambit's Sucker Punch can help lessen their Speed advantage. Weather setters like Mega Charizard Y can also nullify the Speed advantage of opposing weather attackers like Excadrill, though keep in mind that opponents will often attempt to fight for weather control with their own setters like Mega Tyranitar.

This spread allows it to survive Aerodactyl's and Sharp Beak Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat and Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum while outspeeding Adamant Garchomp and Modest Mega Floette, as well as Jolly Sand Rush Excadrill with Unburden active.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sneasler is walled by Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Aegislash; they resist Dire Claw and ignore Fake Out and Close Combat, letting them safely come in on predicted attacks. Mega Gengar is a very threatening Ghost-type, as Gengar can force Sneasler out and Mega Evolve to trap its teammates. Sinistcha, in particular, can set up Trick Room and render Sneasler very vulnerable to attacks; Farigiraf accomplishes the same while preventing Fake Out from hitting its team and directly threatening it with Psychic or Twin Beam. Without Unburden active, faster attackers like Choice Scarf Garchomp, Sand Rush Excadrill, Mega Delphox, and Aerodactyl can easily OHKO it, with the latter even bypassing Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat and matching Unburden with Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Kingambit is one of the best partners for Sneasler, as it threatens Ghost-types and prominent Trick Room setters with its STAB Dark-type moves. Basculegion-M appreciates Sneasler's good matchup against opposing Kingambit, which can threaten its late-game sweeps with Sucker Punch, while Dragon-types like Garchomp and Archaludon can safely let their STAB moves loose with opposing Fairy-types removed by Sneasler.

  • How to Overcome Sneasler's Weaknesses: Choosing Kingambit during Team Preview will give Sneasler security when facing Ghost-types alongside it or ensure you have a reliable switch-in to them. Kingambit also benefits from Trick Room, making it a potential counterlead against Sinistcha and Farigiraf. Against faster threats, aim to have Unburden activated by the time they come out; if that's not plausible, priority moves like Kingambit's Sucker Punch can help lessen their Speed advantage. Weather setters like Mega Charizard Y can also nullify the Speed advantage of opposing weather attackers like Excadrill, though keep in mind that opponents will often attempt to fight for weather control with their own setters like Mega Tyranitar.

movesets.name: Tailwind Support
movesets.description_plain: Whimsicott is able to provide crucial Tailwind support to many Pokemon that rely on it, such as Mystic Water Basculegion-M , offensive Mega Floette , and bulky Garchomp . At the same time, it can shut down almost any attempts at setting up with Encore, making Whimsicott ideal for both support and disruption. Encore : While Tailwind teams can sometimes struggle with setup Pokemon or moves such as Fake Out, Encore attaches a risk to these moves by forcing foes to switch out or prevent Encore in other ways risk being locked into a useless move. It synergizes well with Whimsicott's Grass typing, which allows it to ignore Rage Powder from Sinistcha attempting to redirect Encore. Encore can also be used to lock foes into resisted attacks, such as opposing Basculegion-M's Wave Crash instead of Last Respects, protecting Whimsicott and potentially its partner. Items Focus Sash : Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to run more Speed but means it cannot be as offensive as Fairy Feather variants, as quite a few SPs are still required in bulk to survive Dual Wingbeat from Aerodactyl . Fairy Feather : Fairy Feather allows Whimsicott to threaten a 2HKO on bulky Sitrus Berry Garchomp with Moonblast while leaving room for a lot of SPs in bulk. This item is mostly used when Focus Sash is used by a different Pokemon. SP Spreads 18 HP / 6 Def / 10 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid : This spread is only run by Focus Sash variants. Whimsicott will survive Dual Wingbeat from Jolly Aerodactyl almost the entire time, with the rest of the SPs prioritized towards Speed in order to Speed tie other Whimsicott. 30 HP / 17 Def / 9 SpA / 10 SpD with Bold : This spread is only run by Fairy Feather variants, as Focus Sash variants do not need to hit as many benchmarks. Whimsicott is guaranteed to survive Iron Head from Adamant-natured Kingambit and will almost always survive Moonblast from Mega Floette. The offensive investment allows Whimsicott to almost always 2HKO bulky Sitrus Berry Garchomp. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid : When combined with Mega Floette's Fairy Aura, this SP spread allows Whimsicott to deal a large amount of damage. Whimsicott can afford to run this spread when holding Focus Sash, as Dual Wingbeat from Aerodactyl is the only attack it needs bulk to survive. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : While Whimsicott is almost never totally useless, as Encore will almost always achieve something, it struggles against Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox , as they usually don't mind being Encored and resist Moonblast from Whimsicott. Venusaur , in a similar vein, resists Moonblast and is not bothered by Encore too much. However, Moonblast can break Venusaur's Focus Sash, so attacking Venusaur can still be worthwhile. Additionally, Incineroar can pose problems for Whimsicott due to its immunity to Encore, that allows it to shrug off Moonblast, and access to Fake Out to stop Whimsicott from using Encore. Good Partners and Synergies : While there are many Pokemon that appreciate Whimsicott's support and improve its performance in return, Mega Floette stands out as one of the best. Tailwind allows Mega Floette to outspeed nearly every other Pokemon barring other Tailwind-supported threats, while Fairy Aura allows Whimsicott to deal a surprisingly large amount of damage with Moonblast. Encore also helps Mega Floette beat foes it can struggle with, such as setup Corviknight and Aurora Veil Mega Froslass . Mega Charizard Y is another good partner, as Whimsicott's Tailwind lets even bulky variants outspeed Garchomp, one of Mega Charizard Y's biggest threats. Garchomp resists Weather Ball and Heat Wave, and Solar Beam isn't strong enough to take it out, but Whimsicott can bring Garchomp in range of Weather Ball with Moonblast. Garchomp itself is also a great partner, as it has a very good matchup against Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, which Whimsicott struggles with. How to Overcome Whimsicott's Weaknesses : When using Whimsicott, well-placed Encores can get its team out of many bad positions. Leveraging Whimsicott's presence on the field with Protect is also important for this, as the opponent may feel locked out of several moves while Whimsicott is present. Moves such as Aqua Jet and Aurora Veil, as well as Earth Power from Venusaur, are examples of options that require positioning around Encore. Certain moves are only used in specific situations, such as when Venusaur uses Earth Power against Glimmora or when Aqua Jet picks off a foe at low HP, while others, such as Protect, can render a Pokemon useless if it is forced to use them multiple turns in a row. As such, these moves require much more precise positioning when Whimsicott is on the field. Leveraging this pressure alongside Whimsicott's Protect and the opportunity cost of manually switching can exponentially increase Whimsicott's usefulness. The partners mentioned in the previous section can help cover Whimsicott's common switch-ins, with Garchomp beating Incineroar using Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum as well as Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y using Rock Slide. When facing opposing Tailwind teams, using defensive options such as an allied Incineroar or bulky Pokemon may be more consistent than attempting to win Speed ties against opposing Whimsicott and lock it into Tailwind.
