movesets.name: Bulky Offensive
movesets.description_plain: Sylveon is a bulky offensive sweeper that fires off powerful Fairy-type attacks like Hyper Voice and Hyper Beam thanks to Pixilate. In addition to its bulk, Sylveon's middling Speed lets it make use of both Tailwind and Trick Room, ensuring it moves before its foes. Sylveon's Fairy-type attacks are devastating in the metagame, threatening KOs on Dragon- and Dark-types like Garchomp , Mega Tyranitar , and Hydreigon as well as dealing strong neutral damage against foes like Kingambit and Archaludon . Hyper Voice : Hyper Voice is Sylveon's most commonly used attack. It provides strong spread damage, OHKOing low-bulk Garchomp and 2HKOing bulky Sitrus Berry and Roseli Berry Garchomp variants as well as Sneasler . This attack, however, can be neutralized by Incineroar 's Throat Chop. Hyper Beam vs Moonblast : Both of these moves provide Sylveon with a powerful single-target Fairy-type attack, allowing it to still deal damage when facing potential Wide Guard users like Aerodactyl and Pelipper . They also allow Sylveon to OHKO Soundproof Kommo-o . Hyper Beam is used as a powerful attack, potentially OHKOing bulkier foes such as Kingambit, Archaludon, and Mega Dragonite through Multiscale as well as Garchomp through its Roseli Berry. Using Hyper Beam is risky, as it leaves Sylveon vulnerable, although it can potentially KO a major threat. Moonblast, on the other hand, deals significantly less damage and has no drawbacks. Moonblast lets Sylveon 2HKO Sinistcha and bulky Pelipper. Quick Attack : Quick Attack provides a priority Fairy-type attack that can finish off weakened foes and break Focus Sashes. It can also be used to cause Kingambit's Sucker Punch to fail if it targets Sylveon. Other Options Yawn : Sylveon occasionally runs Yawn, usually over Quick Attack, to put foes to sleep, disrupt them, and slow the pace of the game for its team. This lets Sylveon secure KOs or gives its partners chances to set up safely. Yawn is also great at disrupting setup sweepers like Calm Mind Mega Floette and Bulk Up Ceruledge , forcing them to switch out or be put to sleep. Items Fairy Feather : Fairy Feather increases the damage of Sylveon's Fairy-type attacks. It is a vital item to ensure that Sylveon can 2HKO Basculegion-M with Hyper Voice and OHKO bulky foes like Archaludon with Hyper Beam. SP Spreads 25 HP / 24 Def / 12 SpA / 5 Spe with Modest : The defensive investment lets Sylveon almost always survive Dire Claw from Adamant Sneasler. The Speed investment lets Sylveon outrun Garchomp under Tailwind. The remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack to maximize Sylveon's damage. 6 HP / 32 SpA / 28 Spe with Modest : The Speed investment allows Sylveon to outrun Jolly Choice Scarf Basculegion-M while Tailwind is active. The HP investment lets Sylveon take Moonblast from +1 Modest Mega Floette with 15 Special Attack SPs invested, while Sylveon's given Special Attack investment with Modest maximizes its damage output. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Sylveon struggles most against hard-hitting foes that move before it, such as Mega Charizard Y and Basculegion-M. They deal a lot of damage, helping their partners easily pick off Sylveon or even outright OHKO it. Mega Charizard Y in particular resists Sylveon's attacks and threatens it with Weather Ball. Mega Gengar and Sneasler easily outrun Sylveon and threaten it with Sludge Bomb and Dire Claw, respectively. Mega Venusaur and Glimmora are also problematic, since they are bulky, resist all of Sylveon's attacks, and threaten it with heavy damage from Sludge Bomb. Steel-types like Kingambit and Aegislash threaten Sylveon with massive damage from Iron Head. Wide Guard from Aerodactyl and Pelipper is troublesome, as it forces Sylveon to rely on its single-target attacks instead of Hyper Voice, most commonly Hyper Beam and Quick Attack, leaving Sylveon open to taking huge damage after using Hyper Beam or dealing little damage when using Quick Attack. Sableye 's dual screens and Mega Froslass 's Aurora Veil prevent Sylveon from achieving important OHKOs with Hyper Beam against foes such as Archaludon and bulky Basculegion-M. Good Partners and Synergies : Incineroar is one of Sylveon's best partners. It can threaten Steel-types that Sylveon can't threaten at all, like Aegislash, with Flare Blitz while providing damage reduction via Intimidate and Fake Out support. Sneasler also works well with Sylveon, applying more pressure to Kingambit and Archaludon while providing Fake Out support. Sneasler also threatens to OHKO Mega Floette, which is particularly valuable against Calm Mind sets that can beat Sylveon one-on-one. Aerodactyl provides Tailwind support, letting Sylveon outspeed faster foes like Garchomp. Aerodactyl and its Mega Evolution also threaten Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and Sneasler with Dual Wingbeat. Garchomp threatens Poison- and Steel-types like Mega Gengar and Aegislash with Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum, as well as Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. Farigiraf provides Trick Room support, letting Sylveon move before faster foes, and Armor Tail helps prevent Fake Out. Farigiraf also threatens Poison-types like Sneasler and Glimmora with Psychic and Twin Beam. How to Overcome Sylveon's Weaknesses : Sylveon often relies on its partners to defeat faster, powerful foes, such as Garchomp and Aerodactyl OHKOing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and Kingambit OHKOing Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch. If Sylveon is caught in a bad position where a partner that typically threatens the foes that threaten it is not on the field, Sylveon can use Detect for the turn while pivoting a partner onto the field to threaten those foes the following turn. Setting up Tailwind or Trick Room lets Sylveon move before faster threats like Basculegion-M. Fake Out support from Incineroar and Sneasler also helps Sylveon deal damage without fear of being double-targeted.

movesets.name: Trick Room Support
movesets.description_plain: Farigiraf's solid resilience and unique ability to deny Fake Out give it a strong niche as a reliable Trick Room setter. Offensively, a Psychic typing grants it a great matchup against Poison-types like Sneasler , Glimmora , and Venusaur . Psychic : Even with no Special Attack investment, Psychic will always 2HKO maximum HP variants of Mega Gengar and Mega Venusaur . Thunderbolt vs. Hyper Voice : Thunderbolt pressures Flying- and Water-types like Mega Charizard Y , Mega Aerodactyl , and Basculegion-M , notably having a good chance to 2HKO the latter two with no investment. Hyper Voice sacrifices useful coverage for the ability to constantly pressure the opposing team with spread damage, especially if Farigiraf has the initiative under Trick Room. Protect vs. Helping Hand : If Farigiraf's support is integral to your team, it can use Protect to defensively position itself and guard against double targeting. Helping Hand can be used over Protect if you can afford to sacrifice Farigiraf, allowing it to bolster the team's damage output even when it's about to be KOed. Farigiraf can run both moves in the last two moveslots only if it's supporting a Pokemon that can deal so much spread damage, like Torkoal or Mega Blastoise , that having an auxiliary attack isn't necessary. Other Options Twin Beam : Twin Beam is a weaker alternative to Psychic that's capable of OHKOing Focus Sash variants of Sneasler and, with enough investment, Glimmora. Roar : Roar can be used in the last moveslot to deny setup sweepers like Mega Floette from gaining boosts and users of Trick Room like Sinistcha and opposing Farigiraf from setting it up. Ally Switch : Although it's reliant on predicting your opponent's actions, Ally Switch's ability to essentially redirect an incoming attack away from Farigiraf's ally can make it a worthwhile consideration for the last moveslot. Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry's burst healing lets Farigiraf repeatedly survive strong attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and handle double targeting much more easily, making it the preferred held item. Colbur Berry : If Sitrus Berry isn't available, Colbur Berry can be used to guarantee survival against Black Glasses Kingambit 's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Tyranitar 's Knock Off. Abilities Armor Tail : Armor Tail's most notable application is denying Fake Out from users like Sneasler and Incineroar . Additionally, it protects Farigiraf's team from Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Prankster-boosted moves like Whimsicott 's Encore and Sableye 's Quash. SP Spreads Speed-reducing Natures : A Relaxed, Quiet, or Sassy nature can be used over a Bold, Modest, or Calm nature, respectively, if you want Farigiraf to outspeed neutral-natured base 60s like Sylveon and Incineroar under Trick Room. 30 HP / 24 Def / 12 SpD with Bold or Relaxed : This is a physically defensive spread that lets Farigiraf survive Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Scizor 's Bug Bite. With Sitrus Berry, Farigiraf is also likely to avoid getting 2HKOed by Sneasler's Close Combat, Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash, and Modest Mega Floette's Dazzling Gleam. 12 HP / 24 Def / 27 SpA / 3 SpD with Modest or Quiet : This offensive spread lets Farigiraf usually OHKO Focus Sash Glimmora with Twin Beam and potentially OHKO maximum HP Mega Gengar with Psychic. The bulk investment lets Farigiraf avoid the OHKO from non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Floette's Moonblast, as well as the 2HKO from uninvested Incineroar's Throat Chop with either Berry. 32 HP / 11 Def / 23 SpD with Calm or Sassy : With the heavy special bulk investment, Farigiraf cannot be OHKOed by Mega Floette's Light of Ruin and is unlikely to be OHKOed by its +1 Moonblast, while 11 Defense SPs give favorable odds to survive non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. Sitrus Berry lets Farigiraf dodge the 2HKO from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Archaludon 's Electro Shot, as well as the 3HKO from Jolly Garchomp 's Dragon Claw almost all of the time. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Kingambit is the most threatening Pokemon to Farigiraf, as it can easily KO non-Colbur Berry variants with Kowtow Cleave, comfortably take Farigiraf's STAB attacks, and benefit from Trick Room with its low Speed. Additionally, Farigiraf is a sitting duck against other Dark-types like Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar; Mega Tyranitar can threaten an OHKO with Knock Off and proceed to set up as it switches out, while Incineroar can gradually wear it down and lock out Hyper Voice with Throat Chop. Steel-types like Aegislash and Corviknight easily tank Farigiraf's STAB attacks, which lets them freely attack and, in Corviknight's case, set up. Bug-types like Kleavor and Mega Scizor pressure Farigiraf with their STAB moves; additionally, Mega Scizor can set up Swords Dance and gain free recovery by eating its Sitrus Berry with Bug Bite. Although it's fairly bulky, Farigiraf can be easily KOed if it's targeted by a pair of very strong foes; a combination of attacks like Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball and Sneasler's Close Combat can put it out of commission if it attempts to set up Trick Room. Farigiraf's lack of coverage and Speed can make it passive outside of Trick Room, especially if it uses a bulky SP spread. This can put the burden on its on-field ally to pick up the slack offensively, which the opponent can exploit by double targeting the ally. Good Partners and Synergies : Farigiraf should be ideally paired with slow teammates like Kingambit and Sylveon, as they appreciate the ability to attack first and still tank a couple blows with their bulk investment. In this case, a Tailwind setter like Whimsicott or Aerodactyl can be beneficial for an alternate team mode if Trick Room isn't needed, and Farigiraf can still contribute to this mode by blocking Fake Out with Armor Tail to preserve the setter's Focus Sash. This also prevents Pokemon that don't run Protect, like Choice Scarf Garchomp and most Chople Berry Kingambit variants, from getting disrupted and losing momentum. Fire-types like Torkoal and Mega Charizard Y can blast through Steel- and Bug-types with their STAB moves.   • Psychic: Even with no Special Attack investment, Psychic will always 2HKO maximum HP variants of Mega Gengar and Mega Venusaur.

  • Thunderbolt vs. Hyper Voice: Thunderbolt pressures Flying- and Water-types like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Basculegion-M, notably having a good chance to 2HKO the latter two with no investment. Hyper Voice sacrifices useful coverage for the ability to constantly pressure the opposing team with spread damage, especially if Farigiraf has the initiative under Trick Room.

  • Protect vs. Helping Hand: If Farigiraf's support is integral to your team, it can use Protect to defensively position itself and guard against double targeting. Helping Hand can be used over Protect if you can afford to sacrifice Farigiraf, allowing it to bolster the team's damage output even when it's about to be KOed. Farigiraf can run both moves in the last two moveslots only if it's supporting a Pokemon that can deal so much spread damage, like Torkoal or Mega Blastoise, that having an auxiliary attack isn't necessary.

Other Options

  • Twin Beam: Twin Beam is a weaker alternative to Psychic that's capable of OHKOing Focus Sash variants of Sneasler and, with enough investment, Glimmora.

  • Roar: Roar can be used in the last moveslot to deny setup sweepers like Mega Floette from gaining boosts and users of Trick Room like Sinistcha and opposing Farigiraf from setting it up.

  • Ally Switch: Although it's reliant on predicting your opponent's actions, Ally Switch's ability to essentially redirect an incoming attack away from Farigiraf's ally can make it a worthwhile consideration for the last moveslot.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing lets Farigiraf repeatedly survive strong attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and handle double targeting much more easily, making it the preferred held item.

  • Colbur Berry: If Sitrus Berry isn't available, Colbur Berry can be used to guarantee survival against Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Tyranitar's Knock Off.

  • Armor Tail: Armor Tail's most notable application is denying Fake Out from users like Sneasler and Incineroar. Additionally, it protects Farigiraf's team from Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Prankster-boosted moves like Whimsicott's Encore and Sableye's Quash.

  • Speed-reducing Natures: A Relaxed, Quiet, or Sassy nature can be used over a Bold, Modest, or Calm nature, respectively, if you want Farigiraf to outspeed neutral-natured base 60s like Sylveon and Incineroar under Trick Room.

movesets.name: Special Tank
movesets.description_plain: Mega Venusaur 's respectable defensive stats, great typing, and access to the fantastic Thick Fat ability often make it a Mega Evolution of choice for bulky teams. It notably walls the most popular Primarina , Mega Lopunny , and Meowscarada sets; can stomach hits from powerful special attackers like Mega Gengar , Mega Charizard Y , and Archaludon ; and provides utility with its immunity to Toxic against the likes of Umbreon , Toxapex , and Bellibolt . Sludge Bomb : Sludge Bomb's decent chance to poison foes can punish defensive switch-ins and cripple bulky Pokemon that Mega Venusaur otherwise struggles to damage, like Umbreon, by chipping away at their health, especially when combined with the damage from Leech Seed. Earth Power : Earth Power provides complementary coverage against the Poison- and Steel-types that Mega Venusaur's STAB attacks cannot hit well. For example, Earth Power will always 2HKO Archaludon. Leech Seed : Leech Seed's healing can allow Mega Venusaur and potentially its teammates to remain healthy throughout the game; for example, a Timid Leech Seeded Mega Charizard Y has a very slim chance to 2HKO Mega Venusaur with Flamethrower in sun, giving it the opportunity to alternate between attacking and using Synthesis. Additionally, defensive Pokemon don't appreciate Leech Seed's chip damage, and it provides great insurance against Yawn cycling from Hippowdon and Umbreon by healing off some of the entry hazard damage taken by Mega Venusaur's teammates if it's forced to switch out to avoid falling asleep. Giga Drain : At the cost of some of Leech Seed's more general utility, Giga Drain makes Mega Venusaur a bit more threatening to Ground-types like Hippowdon and Garchomp and Water-types like Mega Gyarados and Mega Blastoise . Though it does considerable damage to Basculegion-M , keep in mind that a 150-Base Power Last Respects 2HKOes Mega Venusaur even after Giga Drain's healing, meaning that this matchup is unfavorable for it unless Basculegion-M has already lost some HP. Chlorophyll : While both of Venusaur's possible base abilities are very situational, Chlorophyll allows it to always outspeed and potentially revenge kill Mega Charizard Y in sun and is therefore generally preferred over Overgrow even on sets using Giga Drain. Beware of Corviknight : Corviknight, as well as other slow and bulky pivots like Galarian Slowking to a lesser extent, is particularly annoying for Mega Venusaur because it can shrug off any attacks the Grass / Poison type throws at it and denies Leech Seed healing with U-turn. Mega Venusaur greatly appreciates teammates that can set hazards, such as Garchomp and Archaludon, to dissuade the opponent from repeatedly switching Corviknight in and out. Other Options Toxic : Though it's less useful against offensive teams than Leech Seed, stall teams can be devastated by a well-timed Toxic. If you elect to use Toxic, Sludge Wave may be preferable to Sludge Bomb to lessen the chance of Mega Venusaur inadvertently inflicting the weaker poison effect. Other SP Spread 32 HP / 21 Def / 13 SpD with Bold : Mega Venusaur can run a physically defensive set, giving it a better matchup against Mega Lucario , Aegislash , and Swords Dance Garchomp at the cost of not being able to easily switch in on special attackers. With this spread, it avoids the 2HKO from Jolly Mega Lucario's Meteor Mash, and it has enough Special Defense to always survive Timid Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Overheat from full HP and avoid getting 2HKOed by Timid Mega Gengar's Sludge Wave.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Mega Venusaur is a solid option thanks to its bulk, good coverage, and excellent matchup against Basculegion-M , Sylveon , Rotom-Wash , and Mega Floette . It also has a decent matchup against many common threats, such as Sneasler , Kingambit , and Incineroar . Earth Power : Earth Power provides coverage against Steel- and Poison-types that Mega Venusaur would otherwise be unable to damage. Examples include Kingambit, Sneasler, Archaludon , and Mega Gengar , all of which Mega Venusaur can 2HKO. It also notably 3HKOes Incineroar, which Mega Venusaur can beat thanks to Thick Fat. Mega Evolving Venusaur : When in the sun, Venusaur can outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. This means it may not always be optimal to Mega Evolve Venusaur when facing foes like Mega Charizard Y , as remaining in its base forme allows it to use an extremely fast Sleep Powder or clean up a weakened foe before it can attack. Alternatively, Mega Evolution provides Mega Venusaur with Thick Fat, which turns Mega Dragonite 's Flamethrower from a 2HKO into a 4HKO, Mega Froslass 's Blizzard from a 2HKO into a 3HKO, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball in the sun from a guaranteed OHKO into a 2HKO. Other Options Leech Seed : Leech Seed lets Mega Venusaur deal residual damage and increase its longevity. It helps Mega Venusaur win in the long term against bulky foes like Corviknight , which it otherwise can't damage well. Leech Seed will usually replace Earth Power or Giga Drain due to the importance of Sludge Bomb and Protect. Without Earth Power, Mega Venusaur lacks meaningful damage against Steel- and Poison-types like Kingambit and Sneasler. Without Giga Drain, Mega Venusaur becomes far less threatening to Water-types like Basculegion-M. Sleep Powder : Sleep Powder can end a game if it hits, and Venusaur can use it multiple times in a single game thanks to its amazing bulk. However, Sleep Powder also comes at the cost of a precious move slot, meaning it will most likely replace Earth Power or Giga Drain. It can also make Venusaur a more inconsistent Pokemon to bring due to its poor accuracy. SP Spreads 32 HP / 7 Def / 18 SpA / 9 Spe with Modest : This spread allows Venusaur to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M in the sun. The HP and Defense investment allows Venusaur to survive +2 Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack to maximize damage, allowing Mega Venusaur to still 2HKO specially defensive Archaludon sets. 32 HP / 19 Def / 12 SpD / 3 Spe with Bold : 3 Speed SPs allow Venusaur to outspeed Mega Delphox in the sun. The remaining SPs are invested in bulk, allowing Venusaur to comfortably survive Psychic from Modest Mega Delphox, Brave Bird from Talonflame , and even a 200-Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion-M. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Although Mega Venusaur is protected from its usual weaknesses through Thick Fat, it is still weak to Flying- and Psychic-type attacks. This includes Pelipper , Mega Aerodactyl , Talonflame, Farigiraf , and Mega Delphox. Mega Delphox and Talonflame are particularly big problems, as they resist Giga Drain, are immune to Earth Power, and threaten it back with Psychic and Brave Bird, respectively. Mega Dragonite can also tank any attack from Mega Venusaur and 3HKO it with Dragon Pulse. It can also set up Tailwind right in front of Mega Venusaur. Corviknight completely walls Mega Venusaur; it can easily set up in front of Mega Venusaur and KO it with Brave Bird. Good Partners and Synergies : Rain teams appreciate Mega Venusaur's ability to switch into Grass-, Fighting-, and Electric-type attacks such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt for partners like Archaludon, Pelipper, and Basculegion-M. It can also use Earth Power against Kingambit for Basculegion-M. In return, Archaludon can use Electro Shot to deal with Flying-types like Corviknight and Talonflame, while Basculegion-M can take out Mega Delphox. Pelipper can also switch in and massively reduce Mega Charizard Y's damage to Mega Venusaur with Drizzle. Kingambit and Incineroar are decent switch-ins to Psychic-type moves. They help check Farigiraf, which can easily tank Mega Venusaur's attacks and 2HKO it, while Mega Venusaur can switch into Fighting-type moves for them. Sableye is also a good switch-in to Psychic-type moves, as it can set up screens to make Mega Venusaur even harder to remove. In return, Mega Venusaur can handle the Fairy-types that threaten Sableye. How to Overcome Mega Venusaur's Weaknesses : Pelipper, Archaludon, and Basculegion-M are great partners to bring against weather teams, as Pelipper hampers Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball and shuts down Mega Froslass's Aurora Veil, while Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten them with Electro Shot and Last Respects. Partners like Sableye are better against setup spam and hyper offense teams; Sableye can use Encore to lock Mega Blastoise into Shell Smash while providing priority screens. Knowing when to use Protect is also very important for positioning, as it gives the team an extra turn to bring in Basculegion-M to threaten Psychic- and Fire-types, Pelipper against Mega Charizard Y, or Sableye to set up screens and shield Mega Venusaur from a strong attack.

movesets.name: Chlorophyll Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Venusaur, due to its ability in Chlorophyll and excellent coverage, is a strong offensive threat in the metagame. These traits are complemented by Venusaur's access to Sleep Powder, which lets it put threats it and its partners struggle with like Garchomp and Aerodactyl to sleep. Earth Power versus Grass-type Coverage : Earth Power deals with Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit that resist its STAB moves. This coverage pairs well with its best partner in Mega Charizard Y , as Earth Power also deals with Rock- and Fire-types that Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal with, such as Glimmora and Blaziken . However, if the rest of the team is able to handle these threats, Grass-type coverage may be used instead. Sleep Powder versus Grass-type coverage : Sleep Powder has shaky accuracy but makes Venusaur especially terrifying. This is because Venusaur's boosted Speed under the sun lets it shut down checks like Mega Staraptor and Incineroar . If Venusaur is using Life Orb, a third move in Solar Beam or Leaf Storm is preferred to take advantage of the damage boost. Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm : Solar Beam gives Venusaur a more spammable STAB move. When boosted by Helping Hand, Solar Beam OHKOes Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl . On the other hand, Leaf Storm OHKOes threats like Milotic regardless of the weather at the cost of dropping Venusaur's Special Attack. Abilities : Chlorophyll boosts Venusaur's Speed under the sun, letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon , Sneasler , and Mega Aerodactyl and put these threats to sleep or heavily damage them. Items : Focus Sash makes Sleep Powder's inaccuracy easier to handle, as it lets Venusaur at least have another chance to put a foe to sleep in case it misses. Focus Sash can also be crucial to let Venusaur deal some damage or inflict sleep in case the opponent sets up Tailwind. Alternatively, Life Orb boosts Venusaur's damage, letting it take out most Pelipper with Leaf Storm and non-bulky Mega Floette with Sludge Bomb. Other Options Protect versus a Third Attacking Move : Protect may be dropped in favor of a third attacking move to maximize Venusaur's offensive capabilities, as Venusaur will generally go first under the sun and put an opposing threat to sleep or finish it off before it can attack. Furthermore, Venusaur has decent bulk, surviving hits from Kingambit, Archaludon, Garchomp, and can have extra insurance if it's using a Focus Sash. However, dropping Protect leaves it vulnerable to Fake Out disruption. Energy Ball : Energy Ball is not dependent on the weather and does not drop Venusaur's Special Attack while still doing enough damage to remove Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert . However, this leaves Venusaur unable to OHKO bulky Basculegion-M. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : While Venusaur can invalidate most of its offensive checks with Sleep Powder, it can find itself in an extremely bad situation if Sleep Powder misses. Venusaur also fails to OHKO most threats like Mega Staraptor, Mega Metagross , and Hydreigon even with the Life Orb boost and will get OHKOed back. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Charizard Y is Venusaur's best partner, as it sets sun to activate Chlorophyll and deals with Steel- and Grass-types that Venusaur struggles with, such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha , and Mega Venusaur. Aerodactyl also deals with opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox , while Whimsicott provides more disruption in Encore and can also use Fake Tears to allow Venusaur to pick up surprise OHKOs. movesets.name: Bulky Entry Hazard Setter
movesets.description_plain: Archaludon is one of the best walls in the entire game thanks to its incredible bulk and Stamina. With access to Stealth Rock, phazing support, and Draco Meteor, Archaludon can efficiently wear down lineups that lack dedicated checks to it. Thunderbolt versus Flash Cannon : Thunderbolt is Archaludon's best complementary move to Draco Meteor for its ability to hit key bulky targets Primarina and Corviknight , which comfortably check Archaludon otherwise, as well as hitting many other Steel-types neutrally. Flash Cannon is a more consistent damage source overall, but it doesn't help Archaludon against Steel-types like Corviknight, Scizor , and Aegislash . Roar versus Dragon Tail : Roar is the preferred phazing option for racking up Stealth Rock damage, as Pokemon immune to it are extremely uncommon, and it works through Substitute. Dragon Tail is more generally oppressive by dealing direct damage and phazing at the same time, and it additionally cannot be shut down by Taunt. However, Dragon Tail can make Archaludon struggle against Substitute users and does not work at all on Mega Floette , which can set up on Archaludon and threaten to snowball out of control. Mirror Coat : Archaludon's bulk makes it a viable user of Mirror Coat, which allows it to deal significant damage or completely take out targets such as Primarina and Mega Gengar . Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers : Sitrus Berry's burst recovery is more effective at helping Archaludon survive multiple hits from big attacks, including super effective ones like Garchomp 's Earthquake. On the other hand, Leftovers is superior when Archaludon can capitalize long-term on Stamina boosts from favorable defensive matchups against foes such as Meowscarada and Mega Starmie . Other Options Foul Play : Foul Play gives Archaludon a direct option against difficult physical attackers like Aegislash and Mega Metagross . Rest and Chesto Berry : Restoring Archaludon to full health after receiving several Stamina boosts can completely ruin physically offensive lineups that rely on attrition to beat Archaludon. SP Spreads All 2HKOs mentioned below factor in Archaludon having a +1 Defense boost from Stamina for the second hit. 32 HP / 23 Def / 11 SpD with Bold : With this spread, Archaludon is guaranteed to avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Basculegion-M 's 150-Base Power Last Respects and, when using Sitrus Berry, Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake. Leftover SPs are put into Special Defense. 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm : Maximum special bulk investment allows Archaludon to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and Modest Primarina's Moonblast, assuming no Fairy Feather on the latter. This spread works particularly well with Mirror Coat, as Archaludon also has a significant chance to survive +1 Moonblast from offensive Mega Floette.

movesets.name: Pseudo-Focus Sash
movesets.description_plain: Archaludon can perform consistently as an offensive lead thanks to Sturdy, which lets it take full advantage of its respectable Speed and high-power attacks. Thunderbolt : Thunderbolt provides strong overlapping coverage with Draco Meteor, in particular pressuring defensive mainstays Primarina and Corviknight . Flash Cannon versus Steel Beam : Flash Cannon is the safest option for a Steel-type STAB attack and is more than sufficient against the likes of offensive Mimikyu and Glimmora . However, Steel Beam's massive Base Power makes dealing with bulkier threats like Hippowdon much more viable, even if it comes at the cost of survivability. Aura Sphere : Aura Sphere helps Archaludon win the mirror matchup while avoiding Draco Meteor usage, keeping its Special Attack stable and making it less likely to become setup bait. Even specially defensive Archaludon has a high chance to be 2HKOed. Aura Sphere is also the best option for taking on Kingambit . Stealth Rock : The combination of Archaludon's Speed and Sturdy allows it to reliably set Stealth Rock. Roar : Roar can disrupt dangerous setup sweepers like Iron Defense Mega Metagross and Swords Dance Mega Blaziken . Timid versus Modest : Many offensive threats such as Adamant Mimikyu, Jolly Basculegion-M , Jolly Hisuian Samurott , and Jolly Mega Gyarados are at or just below Archaludon's positive-nature Speed tier. As such, a Timid nature is usually preferred. However, the power increase from a Modest nature is still worth considering; for example, it gives Archaludon a decent chance to OHKO offensive Mega Gengar with Draco Meteor. Other Options Dark Pulse : Dark Pulse is offensive Archaludon's best means of pressuring Aegislash and Gholdengo directly. Mirror Coat : Sturdy allows for more confident Mirror Coat usage, especially against targets like Gholdengo that boost their Special Attack, but it limits the direct offensive nature that this set likes to utilize and is very reliant on Sturdy being active. Items White Herb : White Herb allows Archaludon to fire off Draco Meteor once without worrying about the subsequent Special Attack drop, giving it incredible burst potential and generally making it less exploitable by setup attackers. Sitrus Berry : Archaludon's defensive typing and stats are so strong naturally that Sitrus Berry can still be worth running on an offensive set. Sitrus Berry will also always activate after using Steel Beam, giving Archaludon an extra health buffer as well as the potential to fire off a second Steel Beam without fainting.

movesets.name: Rain Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: When paired with a rain setter like Pelipper , Archaludon can build dangerous offensive momentum with Electro Shot. Electro Shot : Thanks to the Special Attack boost, even the first Electro Shot used can be difficult to switch into without an Electric resistance, and it can also OHKO frailer targets like Mega Lucario . Draco Meteor : Electro Shot may be the star of the show, but Draco Meteor is often Archaludon's best option when you're trying to play around Ground-type switch-ins such as Garchomp . Aura Sphere : Aura Sphere provides consistent coverage independent from the weather, pressuring Dark-types like Kingambit and opposing Archaludon. Thunderbolt : Thunderbolt is an alternative Electric-type option to use outside of rain, which can be especially relevant for keeping pressure on Mega Charizard Y . SP Spreads and Items 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid : A standard offensive spread for use with Choice Scarf. A Timid nature is mandatory, as Archaludon wants to outrun Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M . 32 HP / 11 Def / 15 SpA / 8 Spe with Modest : Going with a bulkier spread along with a Sitrus Berry sacrifices immediate offensive pressure, but it eases the need for prediction and allows Archaludon more flexibility in and out of rain. Enough Special Attack investment is maintained to guarantee that Electro Shot OHKOes offensive Mega Gyarados , and the Speed investment is enough to outrun fully invested base 60s like Primarina . The remaining SPs go into HP and Defense, giving Archaludon a decent chance of avoiding the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake after Sitrus Berry healing and a Stamina activiation.

movesets.name: Focus Energy
movesets.description_plain: By utilizing Focus Energy and Scope Lens for guaranteed critical hits, not only can Archaludon ignore its own Draco Meteor's stat drops, but it can also rip through the defensive boosts of tanky threats like Clefable and its Mega Evolution! Draco Meteor : Draco Meteor can still be used as an upfront burst option prior to using Focus Energy, allowing Archaludon to adapt to what works best in each matchup. This can make Focus Energy + Draco Meteor a nasty surprise for anything trying to set up on a "weakened" Archaludon. Flash Cannon : Flash Cannon is for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and Primarina , which can ignore Draco Meteor. After Archaludon uses Focus Energy, it will always OHKO physically defensive Unaware Clefable. Thunderbolt : Thunderbolt is more immediately threatening to Primarina than Flash Cannon, and it also prevents Archaludon from getting walled by Corviknight . While Flash Cannon is much more consistent against Clefable overall, Focus Energy + Thunderbolt can still get the job done on Mega Clefable because of its new typing. Substitute : Substitute can block status moves like Yawn from Hippowdon and Umbreon , giving Archaludon an opportunity to set up Focus Energy safely. Stamina versus Sturdy : The choice between abilities comes down primarily to what SP spread Archaludon is running. If Archaludon is using a bulky spread, it should have Stamina; if it's using a purely offensive spread, Sturdy is preferable. Other Options Foul Play and Dark Pulse : Even with a Modest nature and a Focus Energy boost, Archaludon cannot reliably 2HKO HP-invested King's Shield Aegislash with Thunderbolt. Foul Play allows Archaludon to always 2HKO physical attacker Aegislash in Shield forme, and it will also always 2HKO special attacker variants after a Focus Energy boost. Dark Pulse is another option that isn't as efficient against physical attacker Aegislash but makes it possible to threaten Gholdengo , which Foul Play can't do. EV Spreads 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest : This is a simple bulky attacker spread that lets Archaludon work particularly well against slower cycle and stall teams; it also helps Archaludon respond better to threats that try to set up while using Focus Energy. For example, maximum HP Archaludon avoids the OHKO from Mega Gyarados 's +1 Earthquake. Substitute sets appreciate the HP investment as well, since Umbreon's Foul Play will almost never break Substitute in one hit. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Timid : Focusing on Speed lets Archaludon outrun variants of Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott that have some Speed investment. A Modest nature gives an unboosted Draco Meteor the best shot of OHKOing specially defensive variants of Garchomp, but a Timid nature will allow Archaludon to outrun Adamant Mimikyu and Speed tie at worst with opposing Archaludon.

movesets.name: Bulky Rain Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Archaludon is one of the main centerpieces of rain in Regulation M-A, capable of sweeping through entire teams while being exceptionally difficult to take down thanks to its immense physical bulk, Leftovers, Electro Shot, and Stamina. Electro Shot and Archaludon's typing give it a good matchup against Aerodactyl , Rotom-Wash , Talonflame , Mega Gengar , and Mega Blastoise . Electro Shot : Electro Shot is Archaludon's main way of setting up while threatening common Pokemon like Basculegion-M , Pelipper , and Aerodactyl. Positioning with Archaludon : Archaludon can switch into weaker attacks such as Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar to accumulate Stamina boosts. Archaludon should stay on the field as long as possible, as each Stamina boost makes it harder to take down. Other Options Draco Meteor : Draco Meteor can be used in place of Dragon Pulse to give Archaludon access to more firepower. This allows Archaludon to OHKO bulky Garchomp . Aura Sphere : Aura Sphere is used to check opposing Kingambit , with a 50% chance to OHKO it. At +2, Archaludon also OHKOes Mega Tyranitar in sand with Aura Sphere. Items Leftovers : Leftovers grants Archaludon more longevity, enabling it to clean up games more easily. Abilities Stamina : Stamina allows Archaludon to become nigh impossible to KO with physical attacks, letting it tank several Earthquakes from Adamant Garchomp and Low Kicks from Kingambit. SP Spreads 32 HP / 1 Def / 5 SpA / 25 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest : This SP spread allows Archaludon to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion in Tailwind and survive Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat. The remaining points are put into Special Attack and Special Defense to maximize Archaludon's damage output and special bulk. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Archaludon's main weakness is its rather lackluster Special Defense, leaving it vulnerable to moves such as Mega Charizard Y 's Weather Ball, Sylveon 's Hyper Beam, and Mega Dragonite 's Draco Meteor. Despite Archaludon's great physical bulk, Sneasler can threaten to OHKO it with Close Combat. Archaludon is extremely exploitable without any Stamina boosts, and its reliance on rain can make it tough to use in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y. Good Partners and Synergies : Archaludon is typically found on rain teams along with Pelipper, Politoed , Sinistcha , and Basculegion-M. Pelipper and Politoed provide Archaludon with rain so it can set up with Electro Shot freely. Politoed is naturally bulkier and faster, whereas Pelipper has access to a Flying-type STAB move in Hurricane to threaten opposing Grass- and Fighting-types such as Sinistcha and Kommo-o . Pelipper also has access to supporting moves like Wide Guard to block moves such as Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Floette 's Dazzling Gleam and Tailwind to allow Archaludon to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Basculegion. Basculegion-M covers for Archaludon's weaknesses well, acting as a switch-in to Fighting-type moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat while threatening to OHKO most Garchomp with rain- and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash. Basculegion-M also has the potential to OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y through sun with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash. Calm Mind Baton Pass Espathra can be utilized on rain compositions to give Archaludon an alternative way of setting up without being forced to use Electro Shot. Mega Dragonite acts as an alternative Tailwind setter for Archaludon while threatening to OHKO Sinistcha with Hurricane, preventing Sinistcha from using Life Dew or Trick Room. Sinistcha gives Archaludon maximum support through Life Dew and Hospitality recovery, Rage Powder redirection, and Trick Room speed control. Sableye gives Archaludon more bulk via dual screens while using moves such as Rain Dance, Encore, Disable, and Will-O-Wisp to disrupt foes. Rain Dance is used in weather wars, Encore can lock foes like Sneasler into Fake Out and Pokemon that may threaten Archaludon into Protect, Disable can prevent attacks such as Sneasler's Close Combat from threatening Archaludon and can force Choice Scarf users to use Struggle, and Will-O-Wisp can harm physical attackers. How to Overcome Archaludon's Weaknesses : Archaludon's weakness to Sneasler's and Kommo-o's Fighting-type STAB moves can be patched up by threatening these Fighting-types with Pelipper's Hurricane, redirecting attacks with Sinistcha's Rage Powder, or switching Basculegion-M or Sinistcha into Sneasler's Close Combat and Kommo-o's Aura Sphere. Basculegion-M can heavily damage Garchomp with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash or Last Respects after two or three allies have fainted. Archaludon's mediocre Special Defense can be patched up with Sableye's Light Screen and Special Defense boosts from Espathra's Calm Mind. Archaludon needs rain to set up with Electro Shot; therefore, having a manual Rain Dance user like Sableye alongside setters like Pelipper is great for keeping weather control when facing Mega Charizard Y.
movesets.description_html:
• Archaludon is one of the main centerpieces of rain in Regulation M-A, capable of sweeping through entire teams while being exceptionally difficult to take down thanks to its immense physical bulk, Leftovers, Electro Shot, and Stamina. Electro Shot and Archaludon's typing give it a good matchup against Aerodactyl, Rotom-Wash, Talonflame, Mega Gengar, and Mega Blastoise.

  • Electro Shot: Electro Shot is Archaludon's main way of setting up while threatening common Pokemon like Basculegion-M, Pelipper, and Aerodactyl.

  • Positioning with Archaludon: Archaludon can switch into weaker attacks such as Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar to accumulate Stamina boosts. Archaludon should stay on the field as long as possible, as each Stamina boost makes it harder to take down.

Other Options

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor can be used in place of Dragon Pulse to give Archaludon access to more firepower. This allows Archaludon to OHKO bulky Garchomp.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere is used to check opposing Kingambit, with a 50% chance to OHKO it. At +2, Archaludon also OHKOes Mega Tyranitar in sand with Aura Sphere.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers grants Archaludon more longevity, enabling it to clean up games more easily.

Abilities

  • Stamina: Stamina allows Archaludon to become nigh impossible to KO with physical attacks, letting it tank several Earthquakes from Adamant Garchomp and Low Kicks from Kingambit.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 1 Def / 5 SpA / 25 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest: This SP spread allows Archaludon to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion in Tailwind and survive Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat. The remaining points are put into Special Attack and Special Defense to maximize Archaludon's damage output and special bulk.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Archaludon's main weakness is its rather lackluster Special Defense, leaving it vulnerable to moves such as Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball, Sylveon's Hyper Beam, and Mega Dragonite's Draco Meteor. Despite Archaludon's great physical bulk, Sneasler can threaten to OHKO it with Close Combat. Archaludon is extremely exploitable without any Stamina boosts, and its reliance on rain can make it tough to use in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is typically found on rain teams along with Pelipper, Politoed, Sinistcha, and Basculegion-M. Pelipper and Politoed provide Archaludon with rain so it can set up with Electro Shot freely. Politoed is naturally bulkier and faster, whereas Pelipper has access to a Flying-type STAB move in Hurricane to threaten opposing Grass- and Fighting-types such as Sinistcha and Kommo-o. Pelipper also has access to supporting moves like Wide Guard to block moves such as Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Floette's Dazzling Gleam and Tailwind to allow Archaludon to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Basculegion. Basculegion-M covers for Archaludon's weaknesses well, acting as a switch-in to Fighting-type moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat while threatening to OHKO most Garchomp with rain- and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash. Basculegion-M also has the potential to OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y through sun with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash. Calm Mind Baton Pass Espathra can be utilized on rain compositions to give Archaludon an alternative way of setting up without being forced to use Electro Shot. Mega Dragonite acts as an alternative Tailwind setter for Archaludon while threatening to OHKO Sinistcha with Hurricane, preventing Sinistcha from using Life Dew or Trick Room. Sinistcha gives Archaludon maximum support through Life Dew and Hospitality recovery, Rage Powder redirection, and Trick Room speed control. Sableye gives Archaludon more bulk via dual screens while using moves such as Rain Dance, Encore, Disable, and Will-O-Wisp to disrupt foes. Rain Dance is used in weather wars, Encore can lock foes like Sneasler into Fake Out and Pokemon that may threaten Archaludon into Protect, Disable can prevent attacks such as Sneasler's Close Combat from threatening Archaludon and can force Choice Scarf users to use Struggle, and Will-O-Wisp can harm physical attackers.

  • How to Overcome Archaludon's Weaknesses: Archaludon's weakness to Sneasler's and Kommo-o's Fighting-type STAB moves can be patched up by threatening these Fighting-types with Pelipper's Hurricane, redirecting attacks with Sinistcha's Rage Powder, or switching Basculegion-M or Sinistcha into Sneasler's Close Combat and Kommo-o's Aura Sphere. Basculegion-M can heavily damage Garchomp with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash or Last Respects after two or three allies have fainted. Archaludon's mediocre Special Defense can be patched up with Sableye's Light Screen and Special Defense boosts from Espathra's Calm Mind. Archaludon needs rain to set up with Electro Shot; therefore, having a manual Rain Dance user like Sableye alongside setters like Pelipper is great for keeping weather control when facing Mega Charizard Y.

movesets.name: Prankster Support
movesets.description_plain: Grimmsnarl utilizes its access to Prankster and dual screens to become a premier support Pokemon within Regulation M-B, supporting big threats like Archaludon and having a favorable type matchup against the likes of Basculegion-M and Garchomp . Parting Shot : Thanks to Prankster, Parting Shot turns Grimmsnarl into a fast pivot option, allowing it to easily get out of sticky situations like a regular swap with the added benefit of lowering the opponent's offenses. Although it acts before most moves, Parting Shot does occur after players switch or Mega Evolve their Pokemon, allowing Grimmsnarl to bring in an ally weather setter on the same turn the opponent attempts to set up weather by one of the aforementioned methods. Spirit Break versus Foul Play : Spirit Break allows Grimmsnarl to hit Dragon-types like Garchomp and Hydreigon hard while reducing the Special Attack of foes like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette , usually when they are switching in due to Grimmsnarl's low Speed. Spirit Break also deals significant damage to Mega Floette. Foul Play, on the other hand, is capable of OHKOing Basculegion-M and 2HKOing Mega Swampert and most Garchomp. Light Clay : Thanks to Light Clay, partners like Archaludon and Gholdengo have more time to set up safely behind dual screens. Other Options Fake Out : Fake Out can be used over its attacking moves, allowing Grimmsnarl to provide further support by giving partners like Gholdengo an opportunity to set up. However, this leaves it vulnerable to moves like Taunt from Maushold . Scary Face : Scary Face can be used over Spirit Break or Foul Play to grant Grimmsnarl an option of speed control, though it leaves Grimmsnarl entirely passive. SP Spreads 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Careful : The given SPs allow Grimmsnarl to survive Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M and, when Light Screen is set up, Moonblast from Mega Floette. The Defense SPs allow Grimmsnarl to always survive Dire Claw from Jolly Sneasler . A Calm nature can be run when using Foul Play to decrease damage from confusion and opposing Foul Play. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit , Mega Metagross , Archaludon, and Gholdengo threaten Grimmsnarl with Iron Head, Flash Cannon, and Make It Rain. Kingambit can switch in on Spirit Break to activate Defiant, while Gholdengo is immune to Parting Shot and can use Nasty Plot to offset the Special Attack drops from Spirit Break, which does minimal damage to it. Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten huge damage onto Grimmsnarl through dual screens, especially against sets without Spirit Break. Farigiraf , thanks to Armor Tail, denies Parting Shot and, if it's run, Scary Face from affecting Farigiraf's allies, severely hindering Grimmsnarl's effectiveness. Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar prevent Grimmsnarl from setting up dual screens, leaving it vulnerable to another attack like Moonblast from Mega Floette. Sneasler itself threatens huge damage onto Grimmsnarl with Dire Claw, while Incineroar is immune to Prankster moves and easily tanks any attacks that Grimmsnarl carries. Outside of pressuring a few select targets like Basculegion-M, Grimmsnarl struggles to carry an offensive presence on the field, leaving itself to be rather easily ignored. Good Partners and Synergies : Offensive partners like Gholdengo are recommended to offset Grimmsnarl's passivity. Gholdengo is able to threaten Fairy-types and walls out Farigiraf and Sneasler, as well as having a good matchup against Mega Metagross without Stomping Tantrum. Archaludon fills this role well as well, acting as a bulkier partner that exchanges Gholdengo's good Fairy-type matchup for a better matchup against physical attackers like Kingambit thanks to a combination of Reflect and Stamina. Mega Staraptor threatens Steel-types with Close Combat. In return, Grimmsnarl not only provides dual screens but can also use Parting Shot on Mega Staraptor to make it even stronger thanks to Contrary. Grimmsnarl can also use Spirit Break to offset boosts granted to opposing Archaludon by Electro Shot, allowing Mega Staraptor to feel less threatened. Sinistcha creates a strong supportive core alongside Grimmsnarl, healing up common partners behind dual screens and allowing them to easily set up and sweep games. Mega Swampert can use Earthquake or High Horsepower to hit Steel-types, Sneasler, and Incineroar hard while also threatening big damage onto the format's Fairy-types with Wave Crash. Grimmsnarl, in return, can easily pivot to Pelipper against opposing weather setters with Parting Shot. Archaludon also appreciates this to become a dangerous sweeper thanks to the combination of dual screens, Stamina, (AC) and Electro Shot.

movesets.name: Bulky Support
movesets.description_plain: Pelipper is the premier rain setter of Regulation M-A. Being on the slower side, it is able to lead against opposing weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and have the rain override whatever the opposing weather is. Thanks to its Flying typing, it can threaten Grass-types like Sinistcha that otherwise spell trouble for rain teams. Weather Ball : Weather Ball threatens foes like Incineroar in rain, though it is useful in other weathers as well. For example, if the snow is set up, Weather Ball is capable of OHKOing opposing Garchomp . Hurricane : Hurricane is fully accurate in the rain, putting pressure on Grass-types like Sinistcha. Pelipper must be wary of using Hurricane, however, as it becomes rather unreliable if an opposing weather setter overrides the rain with their weather. It is also possible to use Hurricane to fish for confusion for a win, though this isn't to be relied on unless it is the only way out. Protect versus Wide Guard : Protect allows Pelipper to better position itself, setting up the rain more easily. Wide Guard, on the other hand, protects Pelipper and its partners from powerful spread moves such as Rock Slide from Mega Aerodactyl and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette . Weather Wars : Because of the abundance of weather within Regulation M-A, you must be careful when using Pelipper. Keeping it in the back to obtain weather control late-game will make it far easier to win, while leading off with your weather and forcing the opposing weather setter to swap in can leave them vulnerable. Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry allows Pelipper to nearly always avoid being 2HKOed by Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette and Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M in the rain. Abilities Drizzle : Drizzle enables partners like Archaludon and Basculegion-M while also shutting down opposing weather from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar . SP Spreads 31 HP / 14 Def / 18 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm : The given SP spread ensures Pelipper survives Moonblast from Mega Floette or 150-Base Power Last Respects from Jolly Basculegion-M while giving it a good chance to survive Power Gem from Timid Glimmora . The Speed SPs allow Pelipper to outrun uninvested Corviknight . 31 HP / 14 Def / 2 SpA / 16 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest : The Speed and Defense benchmarks are the same as the previous spread, but with Modest, Pelipper will always OHKO Mega Delphox and low-bulk Sneasler with Rain-boosted Weather Ball and Hurricane, respectively. The Special Defense and HP SPs allow Pelipper to survive Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite and Archaludon can easily tank a Weather Ball and retaliate with Draco Meteor, threatening Pelipper on its lower Special Defense. Opposing weather also can be a struggle, forcing Pelipper to swap out and possibly leaving it open to be predicted and KOed when attempting to swap back in. Mega Pokemon that set weather, notably Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass , and Mega Charizard Y, handily override Pelipper's rain mid-turn via Mega Evolution. Rotom-Wash resists both of Pelipper's STAB moves and can OHKO it with Thunderbolt, while Milotic can tank attacks and put it to sleep with Hypnosis, leaving it open to be KOed. Good Partners and Synergies : Archaludon is very helpful against Dragon- and Water-types that annoy Pelipper, hitting them hard with Draco Meteor and Electro Shot, respectively. Additionally, it threatens Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Alolan Ninetales with Flash Cannon, all of which are opposing weather setters. Basculegion-M can also threaten opposing weather setters, even having the capability of OHKOing Mega Charizard Y in the sun with Wave Crash. In return, Pelipper can set up the rain for both of these, allowing Archaludon's Electro Shot and Basculegion's Wave Crash to become far more threatening. Mega Venusaur threatens Pokemon like Mega Floette that may hit Pelipper for big damage and the Water-types that disrupt it. Thanks to Pelipper, Mega Venusaur can sit in the rain to avoid being majorly threatened by Fire-type attacks from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Incineroar. Mega Lopunny can more freely fire off attacks due to Pelipper's ability to threaten Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Scovillain , all while providing Fake Out support to protect Pelipper when switching in. Incineroar also provides Fake Out support as well as a slower pivot option with Parting Shot, getting Pelipper in safely. How to Overcome Pelipper's Weaknesses : Attempting to remove opposing weather should be a top priority to allow Pelipper to shine. Partners like the occasional Mega Scovillain, Sinistcha, and Incineroar provide redirection, slow pivoting, and Fake Out support, all of which allow Pelipper to swap in safely. Pelipper should most often be brought in the back against opposing weather teams to try and ensure that rain will be the dominant weather. Against non-weather teams, leading Pelipper with a strong rain Pokemon like Basculegion-M can apply lots of pressure early-game.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Gholdengo, thanks to its naturally strong defensive typing, easily walls out common Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and helps beat top Pokemon like Mega Floette , Sylveon , Mega Aerodactyl , and Sinistcha . This typing allows Gholdengo to set up Nasty Plot, letting it sweep through teams with its STAB moves and threaten nearly all metagame staples with at least neutral damage. Make It Rain : Make It Rain hits nearly anything that doesn't resist it for huge damage after a Nasty Plot, having a solid chance to OHKO Mega Tyranitar with Life Orb. When using Make It Rain, Gholdengo must be careful; using it at the wrong time late-game will leave Gholdengo too weak to contribute much . This forces Gholdengo to use Nasty Plot again and leave itself or its partner open to attacks. Life Orb : Life Orb gives Gholdengo potential for large amounts of burst damage, allowing Gholdengo to OHKO most Mega Froslass with Make It Rain and Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball, though it comes at the cost of Gholdengo's longevity. For this reason, builds that use Life Orb Gholdengo tend to run faster and more offensive SP spreads to turn it into a strong and threatening attacker that doesn't require setup turns. Spell Tag and Metal Coat : Spell Tag and Metal Coat save Gholdengo's longevity but only allow it to boost either Shadow Ball or Make it Rain. Spell Tag allows Gholdengo to 2HKO Sneasler, while Metal Coat allows Gholdengo to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl. Good as Gold : Good as Gold gives Gholdengo good chances to switch into attacks like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Grimmsnarl as well as Sleep Powder from Venusaur . Other Options Leftovers : Leftovers allow Gholdengo to focus more on setting up by increasing its longevity, though the item sacrifices power. SP Spreads 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid : The given SP spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M, almost always survive Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp , and withstand Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise , with the rest dumped into Special Attack. 7 HP / 32 SpA / 27 Spe with Timid : This SP spread is tailored towards Life Orb sets. It lets Gholdengo outrun Jolly Basculegion-M and survive Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Adamant Basculegion-M, allowing Gholdengo to retaliate with Shadow Ball. The remaining SPs are put into Special Attack. 17 HP / 1 Def / 15 SpA / 1 SpD / 32 Spe with Modest : With the SPs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense, Gholdengo can possibly survive Flare Blitz from Incineroar and has a high chance to survive Heat Wave from Timid Mega Delphox . The SPs in Special Attack allow Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball to OHKO Mega Delphox and +2 Make It Rain to OHKO uninvested Mega Tyranitar, which typically uses Dragon Dance sets. The Speed SPs allow Gholdengo to outspeed all Mega Tyranitar. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y , Mega Blaziken , Incineroar, and Mega Scovillain threaten huge damage onto Gholdengo with Heat Wave, Weather Ball, Flare Blitz, and Overheat. Incineroar in particular resists both of Gholdengo's STAB options, tanking Make It Rain and Shadow Ball and retaliating with Throat Chop or Flare Blitz. Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo with Last Respects and Shadow Ball. Hydreigon , Kingambit , and Mega Tyranitar are Dark-types that OHKO Gholdengo with Dark Pulse, Kowtow Cleave, and Knock Off. Additionally, Hydreigon can opt for Snarl instead to slowly chip down Gholdengo and weaken it in the process, and Kingambit can use Sucker Punch to hit Gholdengo before it moves. Ground-types like Mega Swampert and Garchomp threaten Gholdengo with Earthquake. Mega Swampert also resists Make It Rain and is placed on rain teams alongside Pokemon like Hydreigon and Archaludon , which can deal lots of damage to Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and Electro Shot. On the other hand, Garchomp's flexibility enables it to fit on many teams, meaning that it is a hurdle that Gholdengo often has to face. Good Partners and Synergies : Garchomp threatens Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain with Earthquake, and it can handle Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. Incineroar and Kingambit can switch into Ghost-types and threaten them with Throat Chop and Kowtow Cleave, while Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can help Gholdengo handle Dark-types with Close Combat. Sinistcha can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks with Rage Powder; it can also switch into Ground-types and threaten Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Alolan Ninetales can threaten Ground-types with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard.

  • Spell Tag and Metal Coat: Spell Tag and Metal Coat save Gholdengo's longevity but only allow it to boost either Shadow Ball or Make it Rain. Spell Tag allows Gholdengo to 2HKO Sneasler, while Metal Coat allows Gholdengo to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl.

  • Good as Gold: Good as Gold gives Gholdengo good chances to switch into attacks like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Grimmsnarl as well as Sleep Powder from Venusaur.

Other Options

  • Leftovers: Leftovers allow Gholdengo to focus more on setting up by increasing its longevity, though the item sacrifices power.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid: The given SP spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M, almost always survive Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp, and withstand Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise, with the rest dumped into Special Attack.

  • 7 HP / 32 SpA / 27 Spe with Timid: This SP spread is tailored towards Life Orb sets. It lets Gholdengo outrun Jolly Basculegion-M and survive Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Adamant Basculegion-M, allowing Gholdengo to retaliate with Shadow Ball. The remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 17 HP / 1 Def / 15 SpA / 1 SpD / 32 Spe with Modest: With the SPs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense, Gholdengo can possibly survive Flare Blitz from Incineroar and has a high chance to survive Heat Wave from Timid Mega Delphox. The SPs in Special Attack allow Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball to OHKO Mega Delphox and +2 Make It Rain to OHKO uninvested Mega Tyranitar, which typically uses Dragon Dance sets. The Speed SPs allow Gholdengo to outspeed all Mega Tyranitar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Blaziken, Incineroar, and Mega Scovillain threaten huge damage onto Gholdengo with Heat Wave, Weather Ball, Flare Blitz, and Overheat. Incineroar in particular resists both of Gholdengo's STAB options, tanking Make It Rain and Shadow Ball and retaliating with Throat Chop or Flare Blitz.

  • Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo with Last Respects and Shadow Ball. Hydreigon, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar are Dark-types that OHKO Gholdengo with Dark Pulse, Kowtow Cleave, and Knock Off. Additionally, Hydreigon can opt for Snarl instead to slowly chip down Gholdengo and weaken it in the process, and Kingambit can use Sucker Punch to hit Gholdengo before it moves.

  • Ground-types like Mega Swampert and Garchomp threaten Gholdengo with Earthquake. Mega Swampert also resists Make It Rain and is placed on rain teams alongside Pokemon like Hydreigon and Archaludon, which can deal lots of damage to Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and Electro Shot. On the other hand, Garchomp's flexibility enables it to fit on many teams, meaning that it is a hurdle that Gholdengo often has to face.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain with Earthquake, and it can handle Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Incineroar and Kingambit can switch into Ghost-types and threaten them with Throat Chop and Kowtow Cleave, while Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can help Gholdengo handle Dark-types with Close Combat.

  • Sinistcha can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks with Rage Powder; it can also switch into Ground-types and threaten Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Alolan Ninetales can threaten Ground-types with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard.

movesets.name: Defensive Support
movesets.description_plain: Toxapex finds itself serving a unique role within the Regulation M-B metagame as a supportive wall thanks to its valuable Water / Poison dual typing and sky-high defensive stats. These allow it to sit in front of and greatly limit offensive threats such as Mega Charizard Y , Garchomp , and Sylveon . Infestation : Infestation enables Toxapex to provide some level of offensive pressure along with trapping foes on the field, messing up attempts to reposition. Wide Guard : Wide Guard can protect Toxapex and teammates like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit from spread moves such as Rock Slide and Earthquake. Toxic : Toxic forces timers onto foes such as Milotic and Mega Staraptor , preventing them from being able to setup and win games safely. Infestation, Toxic, and Baneful Bunker Synergy : This trio of moves synergizes well with each other and turns Toxapex into an active threat, as the combination of Infestation and poison does immense amounts of damage over time, softening up foes for partners to KO them. Regenerator : Regenerator helps keep Toxapex healthy throughout a match to let it maintain pressure with trapping and spreading poison. SP Spreads 32 HP / 16 Def / 18 SpD with Bold : This spread allows Toxapex to take Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M 's 200-Base Power Last Respects at full HP in addition to Mega Delphox 's Psychic. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Toxapex can be greatly annoyed by Steel- and Poison-types, as their immunity to Toxic prevents them from being worn down quickly and leaves Toxapex with only Infestation to whittle away at them. Archaludon , Mega Metagross , and Venusaur can prove especially problematic for Toxapex because they can also threaten it with powerful attacks like Electro Shot, Psychic Fangs, and Earth Power. Psychic- and Ground-types such as Mega Delphox, Farigiraf , and Mega Swampert , while not immune to Toxic, can still scare Toxapex through their STAB moves. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Charizard Y greatly appreciates Toxapex's Wide Guard blocking Rock Slide from Garchomp and Aerodactyl , and in return, it can melt through Steel-types such as Kingambit and Gholdengo . Kingambit and Incineroar can prey on the Psychic-types that break Toxapex like Mega Delphox and Farigiraf, and they also can deal with Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar and Sinistcha , which can escape Infestation's Bound effect. In return, Toxapex can come in against Fighting-types that handle them such as Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Additionally, Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot complement Toxapex by making it much more troublesome to remove. Garchomp removes Poison-types such as Mega Gengar and opposing Toxapex while also helping it handle threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y . Toxapex for its part can use Wide Guard to prevent Sinistcha and Mega Froslass from reliably threatening Garchomp with Matcha Gotcha and Blizzard. Wide Guard also allows Garchomp to use Earthquake without worrying about it hurting Toxapex. Venusaur can pair well with Toxapex by scaring away Ground- and Water-types that cause Toxapex problems such as Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M with its Grass-type STAB moves. Meanwhile, Toxapex protects Venusaur from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Froslass's Blizzard with Wide Guard.

movesets.name: Aurora Veil Support
movesets.description_plain: Alolan Ninetales provides support in Aurora Veil and weather disruption, the former of which enables scary setup threats like Mega Gyarados , Mega Blaziken , and Mega Delphox . You can pair it with teammates like Aegislash and Gholdengo that can defensively switch into Steel-type threats like Mega Metagross and Archaludon . Freeze-Dry : Freeze-Dry allows Alolan Ninetales to threaten Water-types like Pelipper , Mega Swampert , Mega Gyarados, and Primarina . Blizzard versus Moonblast : Blizzard OHKOes Garchomp , heavily damages Hippowdon , and chunks offensive Archaludon sets that may switch into Alolan Ninetales. On the other hand, Moonblast lets Alolan Ninetales deal more damage to Mega Gyarados, Mega Blaziken, and Hisuian Samurott . Encore : Encore disrupts opposing setup Pokemon like Swords Dance Mega Mawile , Calm Mind Mega Floette , and Iron Defense Corviknight , and it annoys defensive responses such as Defog Corviknight and Toxic Bellibolt . SP Spreads Alolan Ninetales prefers to have an even Defense stat, as it grants Alolan Ninetales one extra point of Defense when under snow. 31 HP / 9 Def / 26 Spe with Bold : This spread allows Alolan Ninetales to generally survive Adamant Mega Metagross's Bullet Punch at full HP under snow, letting it set Aurora Veil for the team. The remaining SPs are invested in Speed, enabling Alolan Ninetales to outspeed Excadrill and Modest Mega Floette. 31 HP / 3 Def / 32 Spe with Timid : Maximum SPs in Speed let Alolan Ninetales set Aurora Veil as early as possible, disrupt setup threats like Swords Dance Mimikyu with Encore, and outspeed and neutralize Garchomp. Near-maximum HP investment in tandem with snow lets it have a good chance to not get 2HKOed by +1 Mega Gyarados's Earthquake and OHKOed by +2 Garchomp's Earthquake, allowing it to set Aurora Veil or outright eliminate those threats. It also allows Alolan Ninetales to survive a Flash Cannon from Archaludon with Aurora Veil up, letting Alolan Ninetales come back later to set up snow or Aurora Veil. 1 HP / 1 Def / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid : A fully offensive SP spread lets Alolan Ninetales's Freeze-Dry have a good chance to OHKO Mega Swampert and guarantee an OHKO on offensive variants of Garchomp, and it also lets Moonblast OHKO offensive variants of Hisuian Samurott.

movesets.name: Redirection Support
movesets.description_plain: Maushold is an excellent support option with moves like Follow Me to prevent its teammates from getting damaged and nullify Ghost-type attacks like Last Respects from Basculegion-M , helping allies such as Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar . With Friend Guard, its presence on the field will help its teammates survive, even against opposing spread moves that ignore Follow Me. Super Fang : It is ideal, but not necessary, that Maushold be faster than its teammates in order to cut a foe's HP with Super Fang so a teammate can finish it off. Super Fang also lets Maushold continue to get value even if it is Taunted. Feint versus Encore versus Helping Hand : Feint is useful for breaking a foe's Focus Sash or Wide Guard to let teammates like Mega Gardevoir continue to get value with spread moves like Hyper Voice; it also breaks Protect, preventing foes from stalling out turns of Tailwind and Trick Room. Encore can punish Fake Out from Incineroar and can be paired with Disable from Pokemon like Mega Gengar. Encore also pressures foes like Kingambit and Mega Floette not to set up with Swords Dance and Calm Mind, respectively. It is easiest to replace Feint with Encore because, like Feint, Encore is itself an answer to opposing Protect. Helping Hand will make Mega Floette's Moonblast always OHKO a bulky variant of Archaludon . It can replace the Feint slot on teams that lack spread attacks. Other Options Taunt : Taunt shuts down Trick Room from Farigiraf , Parting Shot from Incineroar, support options from Sinistcha like Rage Powder and Life Dew, and setup options like Calm Mind from Mega Floette and Swords Dance from Kingambit. It can replace Feint, Encore, or Helping Hand. Rain Dance : Rain Dance only appears on rain teams and is mainly used to overwrite sun after Mega Charizard Y activates Drought. It also overwrites Mega Tyranitar 's sand to nullify its Special Defense boost and Mega Froslass 's snow to make its Blizzard inaccurate. It can replace the Feint slot. Items Chople Berry : Chople Berry will essentially guarantee Maushold survives a Fighting-type attack like Close Combat from Sneasler , with enough HP left to survive extraneous damage like Fake Out or sand chip damage. Focus Sash : Focus Sash will guarantee that Maushold survives almost any attack, but opposing Fake Out users may pressure it into using Protect, giving the opponent momentum. Using Focus Sash can make Maushold more comfortable investing less in bulk and more in Speed, allowing it to use Super Fang before an ally moves and punish faster foes with Encore, such as Mega Floette and Garchomp . Abilities Friend Guard : Friend Guard helps Maushold's less bulky teammates like Mega Delphox survive longer. Kingambit survives Heat Wave from Timid Mega Charizard Y, and Earthquake from Garchomp almost always becomes a 3HKO. SP Spreads 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 Spe with Timid : The Speed investment allows Maushold to outspeed Garchomp and Mega Floette, with the remaining SPs dumped into HP and Defense to improve the chance of surviving Wave Crash from Basculegion-M. This spread works well with the Focus Sash set given the relative lack of bulk, though it can be used with Chople Berry too. 32 HP / 17 Def / 17 SpD with Calm : Maushold will always survive Wave Crash from Basculegion-M with this defensive investment, and the remaining Special Defense SPs are used to survive Weather Ball from Mega Charizard Y most of the time. This spread is only intended for the Chople Berry set. 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 Spe with Timid : This spread is only intended for Focus Sash builds. Its Speed investment allows it to outrun Lycanroc-D and Alolan Ninetales . Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Taunt from Pokemon like opposing Maushold and Incineroar shuts down most of Maushold's options. Opposing Fake Out from Incineroar or Sneasler can shut down Maushold's Follow Me for a turn, which can leave the partner vulnerable. Hyper offensive options like Wave Crash in rain from Basculegion-M and Light of Ruin from Mega Floette can OHKO Maushold without Focus Sash. Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Sinistcha are immune to Super Fang and Feint. Good Partners and Synergies : Maushold is unable to provide high damage on its own; thus, it must be paired with high-damage partners like Mega Delphox, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M. Mega Delphox and Basculegion-M in particular appreciate Maushold's Follow Me to redirect threatening attacks like Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Friend Guard lets Mega Floette survive Dire Claw from Sneasler and lets Archaludon survive Moonblast from opposing Modest Mega Floette. Slower partners like Mega Floette and Archaludon appreciate Super Fang cutting down foes like Kingambit and opposing Mega Floette; after Super Fang, Mega Floette can KO Kingambit with Moonblast, while Archaludon can KO opposing Mega Floette with Electro Shot or Flash Cannon. Mega Blastoise benefits from Follow Me making it easier to set up with Shell Smash and Feint preventing Wide Guard from stopping Water Spout. How to Overcome Maushold's Weaknesses : Mega Delphox covers opposing Fighting-types that threaten Maushold such as Sneasler and Kommo-o . Basculegion-M is a useful pivot if the opponent is threatening a Fighting-type attack. Though Maushold is commonly in the lead, bringing it in the back can help prevent its Focus Sash from being broken by Fake Out and help allies like Mega Delphox and Mega Floette clean up an endgame. Kingambit can use Kowtow Cleave to threaten the aforementioned Ghost-types Maushold cannot hit.
