movesets.name: Sand Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Excadrill is a staple of sand teams due to its ability and STAB combination allowing it to outspeed the metagame and threaten common threats to its sand-setting partner, Mega Tyranitar , including Sneasler , Archaludon , Mega Floette , and Sylveon . Earthquake versus High Horsepower : Earthquake gives Excadrill an incredibly powerful spread move; however, it can't be safely used next to partners without a Ground immunity and makes Excadrill susceptible to Wide Guard. High Horsepower can be safely used next to any partner, but it comes at the cost of Excadrill's ability to deal big spread damage and leaves Excadrill more susceptible to redirection. Rock Slide : Rock Slide gives Excadrill an option to hit Mega Charizard Y for big damage and works as an alternative spread option that doesn't hit partners. Excadrill can also effectively fish for flinches with Rock Slide due to its high Speed in sand. Items Focus Sash : The extra survivability given by Focus Sash is necessary to let Excadrill fire off more attacks before being KOed. Focus Sash lets Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill 2HKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M while surviving Wave Crash; it also allows Excadrill to tank a Close Combat from Unburden-boosted Sneasler deal an OHKO in return with Earthquake or High Horsepower. Abilities Sand Rush : While sand is active, Sand Rush allows Excadrill to outspeed every Pokemon in the metagame besides Sneasler with an Unburden boost. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Without sand, Excadrill is relatively slow, allowing Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Sneasler, and Mega Charizard Y to outspeed and threaten it if sand is stalled out or overwritten by another weather. Excadrill commonly wants to be led alongside Tyranitar to activate Sand Rush; however, this lead can be exploited because the two share weaknesses to Water-, Fighting-, and Ground-type moves. Garchomp can be a particularly bad matchup, since Rough Skin can break Excadrill's Focus Sash if Excadrill goes for Iron Head or High Horsepower, allowing Garchomp to OHKO it with Earthquake. Basculegion-M is another tough matchup, as non-Choice Scarf variants can bring Excadrill down to its Focus Sash with Wave Crash, tank an attack, and then KO it before it can move with Aqua Jet. Excadrill is unable to deal meaningful damage to both Corviknight and Rotom-Wash , and it's also susceptible to being burned and redirected by Mega Scovillain 's Spicy Spray and Rage Powder, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Tyranitar is a must-have partner for Excadrill, since it sets up sand and threatens Mega Charizard Y and Basculegion-M with Rock Slide and Knock Off, respectively. Excadrill really appreciates Ground-immune partners because they can freely switch into Garchomp and let Excadrill use Earthquake with no drawback. Corviknight is excellent for this role; it effectively walls Garchomp, threatens Grass-types with Brave Bird, and can set up with Bulk Up while Excadrill puts on offensive pressure. Hydreigon and Rotom-Wash are other great options for Ground-immune partners. Hydreigon can offensively threaten Garchomp, Mega Scovillain, and Basculegion-M, while Rotom-Wash can threaten Water-types with Thunderbolt and physical attackers with Will-o-Wisp. Sinistcha can be a great partner, since it resists all the weaknesses that Excadrill and Mega Tyranitar share while providing redirection to protect Excadrill from attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. How to Overcome Excadrill's Weaknesses : Mega Tyranitar and Excadrill should always be chosen together during Team Preview. Use Excadrill as an immediately deadly sweeper, especially to outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Floette that would otherwise be huge threats to Mega Tyranitar. Against opposing weather teams, time Tyranitar's Mega Evolution so that it can keep sand up, and position it well to keep it out of danger and preserve sand. Use the rest of the team to deal with threats to this duo, most importantly Garchomp, while keeping up offensive pressure.

• Excadrill is a staple of sand teams due to its ability and STAB combination allowing it to outspeed the metagame and threaten common threats to its sand-setting partner, Mega Tyranitar, including Sneasler, Archaludon, Mega Floette, and Sylveon.

  • Earthquake versus High Horsepower: Earthquake gives Excadrill an incredibly powerful spread move; however, it can't be safely used next to partners without a Ground immunity and makes Excadrill susceptible to Wide Guard. High Horsepower can be safely used next to any partner, but it comes at the cost of Excadrill's ability to deal big spread damage and leaves Excadrill more susceptible to redirection.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide gives Excadrill an option to hit Mega Charizard Y for big damage and works as an alternative spread option that doesn't hit partners. Excadrill can also effectively fish for flinches with Rock Slide due to its high Speed in sand.

Items

  • Focus Sash: The extra survivability given by Focus Sash is necessary to let Excadrill fire off more attacks before being KOed. Focus Sash lets Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill 2HKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M while surviving Wave Crash; it also allows Excadrill to tank a Close Combat from Unburden-boosted Sneasler deal an OHKO in return with Earthquake or High Horsepower.

Abilities

  • Sand Rush: While sand is active, Sand Rush allows Excadrill to outspeed every Pokemon in the metagame besides Sneasler with an Unburden boost.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Without sand, Excadrill is relatively slow, allowing Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Sneasler, and Mega Charizard Y to outspeed and threaten it if sand is stalled out or overwritten by another weather. Excadrill commonly wants to be led alongside Tyranitar to activate Sand Rush; however, this lead can be exploited because the two share weaknesses to Water-, Fighting-, and Ground-type moves. Garchomp can be a particularly bad matchup, since Rough Skin can break Excadrill's Focus Sash if Excadrill goes for Iron Head or High Horsepower, allowing Garchomp to OHKO it with Earthquake. Basculegion-M is another tough matchup, as non-Choice Scarf variants can bring Excadrill down to its Focus Sash with Wave Crash, tank an attack, and then KO it before it can move with Aqua Jet. Excadrill is unable to deal meaningful damage to both Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, and it's also susceptible to being burned and redirected by Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray and Rage Powder, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar is a must-have partner for Excadrill, since it sets up sand and threatens Mega Charizard Y and Basculegion-M with Rock Slide and Knock Off, respectively. Excadrill really appreciates Ground-immune partners because they can freely switch into Garchomp and let Excadrill use Earthquake with no drawback. Corviknight is excellent for this role; it effectively walls Garchomp, threatens Grass-types with Brave Bird, and can set up with Bulk Up while Excadrill puts on offensive pressure. Hydreigon and Rotom-Wash are other great options for Ground-immune partners. Hydreigon can offensively threaten Garchomp, Mega Scovillain, and Basculegion-M, while Rotom-Wash can threaten Water-types with Thunderbolt and physical attackers with Will-o-Wisp. Sinistcha can be a great partner, since it resists all the weaknesses that Excadrill and Mega Tyranitar share while providing redirection to protect Excadrill from attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash.

  • How to Overcome Excadrill's Weaknesses: Mega Tyranitar and Excadrill should always be chosen together during Team Preview. Use Excadrill as an immediately deadly sweeper, especially to outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Floette that would otherwise be huge threats to Mega Tyranitar. Against opposing weather teams, time Tyranitar's Mega Evolution so that it can keep sand up, and position it well to keep it out of danger and preserve sand. Use the rest of the team to deal with threats to this duo, most importantly Garchomp, while keeping up offensive pressure.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Kommo-o has the potential to sweep through teams after using Clangorous Soul. It boasts good matchups against metagame staples like Kingambit and Incineroar while its defensive typing gives it an edge versus Mega Charizard Y and Mega Blastoise . Clangorous Soul : It is necessary for Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul to ensure crucial OHKOs, such as with Clanging Scales against Garchomp and Aura Sphere against Archaludon . However, given the fact that Clangorous Soul leaves Kommo-o vulnerable for a turn and damages it, Kommo-o has to have support from teammates like Incineroar and Sinistcha in order to set up safely. The HP loss can allow foes Kommo-o is normally comfortable against, like Kingambit and Sneasler , to threaten a double-target KO, making support necessary to set up. Items Leftovers : Leftovers aids Kommo-o's survivability, helping offset the HP loss from Clangorous Soul and allowing Kommo-o to avoid an OHKO from Adamant Sneasler's Close Combat after using Clangorous Soul and receiving one turn of Leftovers recovery. Abilities Soundproof : Soundproof allows Kommo-o to ignore Hyper Voice from Sylveon and Parting Shot from Incineroar, which would otherwise threaten an OHKO or negate most of Clangorous Soul's benefit, respectively. Soundproof also grants Kommo-o an immunity to Perish Song, improving its matchup against Mega Gengar while also making it a good partner. SP Spreads 8 Def / 29 SpA / 29 Spe with Modest : At +1, the Special Attack investment lets Kommo-o almost always OHKO Chople Berry Kingambit with Aura Sphere. The Speed investment allows it to outrun Aerodactyl and Mega Gengar after using Clangorous Soul. The Defense investment optimizes Kommo-o's chance of surviving 150-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M after its Defense is boosted. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid : The Speed investment allows Kommo-o to outrun Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a Speed boost, while the Special Attack investment maximizes its chance of OHKOing Chople Berry Kingambit with Aura Sphere after a Special Attack boost. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Fairy-types like Mega Floette , Whimsicott , and Sylveon threaten to OHKO Kommo-o while it cannot do much damage in return. Mega Floette in particular uses Dazzling Gleam to prevent Sinistcha's Rage Powder from saving Kommo-o. Whimsicott threatens an OHKO with Moonblast, which also cannot be redirected by Sinistcha, and can use Encore to lock Kommo-o into Clangorous Soul. Mega Froslass threatens heavy damage with Blizzard, which cannot be redirected, and can survive Clanging Scales even after two boosts to Kommo-o's Special Attack. Aegislash resists Kommo-o's attacks and blocks Clanging Scales with Wide Guard. Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp can threaten an OHKO or heavy damage before Kommo-o moves, preventing it from using Clangorous Soul. Good Partners and Synergies : Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew help recover HP lost from Clangorous Soul and may allow Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul a second time, and Rage Powder redirects attacks like Dragon Claw from Garchomp and Dragon Pulse from Archaludon to make it easier for Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul in the first place. Kommo-o is immune to Mega Gengar's Perish Song, while Mega Gengar handles the aforementioned Fairy-types and Mega Froslass. In exchange, Kommo-o beats Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar that threaten Sinistcha and Mega Gengar. Incineroar provides Fake Out support and Parting Shot to weaken foes, making it easier for Kommo-o to use Clangorous Soul. Kommo-o in turn covers for Mega Tyranitar with Aura Sphere and is better versus Mega Blastoise. How to Overcome Kommo-o's Weaknesses : Poison-type attacks like Sludge Bomb from Mega Gengar and Dire Claw from Sneasler deal with threatening Fairy-types, and Mega Gengar has Shadow Ball to handle Mega Froslass and Aegislash. Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag allows it to trap and KO these threats before Kommo-o comes in to sweep. Redirection from Sinistcha is effective against Sylveon, as Kommo-o blocks Hyper Voice, leaving Sylveon without spread moves that can ignore Rage Powder; this redirection is also useful against foes without spread attacks like Basculegion-M and Archaludon. Incineroar has offensive options against Mega Froslass and Aegislash with Flare Blitz and Throat Chop while also having Fake Out and Intimidate to help Kommo-o set up in the face of Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp.

movesets.name: Redirection Support
movesets.description_plain: Vivillon is a fast supporter that gives offensive teams both disruption and redirection, forcing opponents to respect Compound Eyes-boosted Sleep Powder while using Rage Powder to protect teammates trying to set up or attack. These give it a niche different from bulkier redirection users such as Sinistcha and Maushold . Vivillon is useful next to teammates such as Mega Blastoise , Farigiraf , Kingambit , and Basculegion-M , which appreciate Vivillon creating openings without giving up too much offensive momentum. Sleep Powder : Sleep Powder is Vivillon's main disruption tool, preventing a foe from acting and giving its partner room to set up or attack the other foe. Compound Eyes makes it reliable enough to threaten metagame staples such as Incineroar , Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Mega Charizard Y . Hurricane : Hurricane prevents Vivillon from being completely passive after using its support moves, pressuring targets such as Sneasler , Kommo-o , Mega Venusaur , and Sinistcha. Even without Special Attack investment, Hurricane has a chance to OHKO Sneasler and always 2HKOes Kommo-o and Mega Venusaur. Hurricane also gives Vivillon something meaningful to do when Sleep Powder is blocked by Grass-types. Pollen Puff versus Rain Dance versus Protect : Pollen Puff gives Vivillon a way to heal partners such as Mega Blastoise, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M after redirecting or forcing a sleep turn. Rain Dance is mainly for teams with Mega Blastoise or Basculegion-M, strengthening their Water-type attacks while removing sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal . Protect should only be used on Focus Sash sets, as this lets Vivillon avoid Fake Out, stall opposing Pokemon's speed control, or preserve itself to use its powder moves later. Items Choice Scarf : Choice Scarf is preferred to make Vivillon a fast disruptor, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Gengar , Mega Aerodactyl , Sneasler, Mega Froslass , and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M before putting them to sleep with Sleep Powder. However, being locked into Rage Powder or Sleep Powder can make Vivillon exploitable, especially if the opponent has Grass-types, which are immune to both moves, or spread attackers that can ignore Rage Powder. Focus Sash : Focus Sash trades Choice Scarf's Speed for more flexible move use, letting Vivillon switch between support and offense more freely. It is especially useful if Vivillon needs to survive a strong attack and still redirect an attack or put a foe to sleep, but it leaves Vivillon vulnerable to faster threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, and other Choice Scarf users. Abilities Compound Eyes : Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder and Hurricane accurate enough for Vivillon to reliably disrupt and threaten Pokemon such as Sneasler, Incineroar, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Mega Charizard Y. It also makes Hurricane much safer to use, letting Vivillon consistently punish targets like Sneasler, Kommo-o, Sinistcha, and Whimsicott instead of being limited to support moves. Compound Eyes is especially important on Choice Scarf sets, where missing Sleep Powder can make Vivillon's team lose a lot of momentum by giving the target a free turn to attack, set speed control, or reposition. Friend Guard : Friend Guard can be used on Focus Sash sets if Vivillon's teammates value extra damage reduction, especially against spread moves that Rage Powder cannot redirect. However, losing Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder and Hurricane much less reliable, so Friend Guard is usually worse. SP Spreads 24 Def / 5 SpA / 5 SpD / 32 Spe with Timid : This bulkier spread is mainly for Choice Scarf Vivillon. It keeps maximum Speed investment to outspeed key fast threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Froslass, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, as well as getting the jump on Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp . The defensive investment lets Vivillon survive Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Sylveon 's Hyper Voice, and it gives Vivillon an extremely good chance to survive Jolly Talonflame 's Dual Wingbeat. Focus Sash sets can also consider this spread if they want to avoid being KOed by Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Vivillon relies heavily on Sleep Powder to force progress, so Pokemon that can ignore Sleep Powder are its biggest obstacles. Sinistcha and Whimsicott are immune to Sleep Powder entirely. Whimsicott can use Prankster Encore to lock non-Choice Scarf Vivillon into Rage Powder, Sleep Powder, or Protect, while Sinistcha can set or remove Trick Room to disrupt Vivillon's team. Fake Out from Pokemon such as Sneasler, Incineroar, and Mega Kangaskhan can stop Vivillon before it uses its powder moves, which is especially punishing for Choice Scarf sets because they can't use Protect. Tailwind robs Vivillon much of its Speed advantage and makes it easier to KO. Gale Wings Talonflame is particularly threatening, as it can set priority-boosted Tailwind and can also threaten Vivillon directly with Flying-type STAB moves. Vivillon is also weak against strong spread damage moves, as Rage Powder cannot redirect moves like Garchomp's and Aerodactyl 's Rock Slide, Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave, Sylveon's Hyper Voice, and Mega Froslass's Blizzard. Rock-types can be major problems for Vivillon because they resist Hurricane, while Rock Slide hits it extremely effectively, bypasses Rage Powder, and pressures its partner all at the same time. Aerodactyl outspeeds non-Choice Scarf Vivillon and can KO Vivillon through Focus Sash or set Tailwind, and Mega Tyranitar can nullify Vivillon's Focus Sash with sand chip damage. Sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal makes Hurricane much less reliable, limiting Vivillon's ability to deal respectable damage. Good Partners and Synergies : Vivillon should be paired with teammates that can immediately take advantage of the free turns it creates with its powder moves. Farigiraf is one of Vivillon's best partners, as Armor Tail blocks Fake Out, which would otherwise stop Vivillon from using Sleep Powder. In return, Vivillon can help Farigiraf set Trick Room through Rage Powder or by putting a foe to sleep. Mega Blastoise is one of Vivillon's strongest partners, as Vivillon's powder moves can create opportunities for it to use Shell Smash, while Pollen Puff can restore its HP to keep Water Spout strong. Rain Dance also strengthens Water Spout and removes sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal. Basculegion-M similarly appreciates Rain Dance support, while Rage Powder can redirect Kingambit's Sucker Punch and give it safer turns to use Wave Crash or Last Respects. Sneasler threatens Rock- and Steel-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Archaludon , which Vivillon struggles to damage. Incineroar can weaken physical attackers with Intimidate, which is especially useful for Choice Scarf Vivillon because Intimidate allows it to sometimes survive attacks it normally could not, such as Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. Additionally, Incineroar's Parting Shot can bring Vivillon or one of its offensive partners onto the field more safely. Kingambit appreciates Vivillon pressuring Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Kommo-o with Hurricane, while Vivillon can redirect Fighting-type attacks that threaten Kingambit. Mega Floette and Sylveon can pressure some Rock Slide users such as Mega Tyranitar and Garchomp with Fairy-type spread damage, while Vivillon helps them by threatening Sneasler with Hurricane and disrupting faster threats with Sleep Powder. How to Overcome Vivillon's Weaknesses : Vivillon should avoid trying to use its powder moves against teams that can easily counter it. If Grass-types such as Sinistcha or Whimsicott are on the field, Hurricane is usually the better option, while Rage Powder should be saved for turns where it enables Vivillon's partner to attack or set up safely. Armor Tail from Farigiraf blocks Fake Out, Whimsicott's Prankster Encore, and Talonflame's Gale Wings Flying-type attacks while also letting Farigiraf set Trick Room in front of Tailwind teams. Incineroar can help Vivillon by using Fake Out to stop one foe while Vivillon puts the other to sleep. Because Rage Powder cannot redirect spread damage, Vivillon needs partners that can pressure common spread attackers directly. Mega Blastoise and Basculegion-M threaten Rock Slide and Heat Wave users such as Aerodactyl, Mega Charizard Y, and Torkoal, while Kingambit pressures Mega Froslass, Sylveon, and Mega Floette. Teammates such as Mega Blastoise, Basculegion-M, and Kingambit can pressure Rock-types like Mega Aerodactyl and Tyranitar , limiting their opportunities to force Vivillon out.

movesets.name: Special Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Mega Dragonite is a strong special attacker with endless coverage and Multiscale, which lets it trade well against offensive teams while being difficult to revenge kill at full health. Its ability to threaten Pokemon such as Corviknight , Garchomp , and Primarina without needing setup gives it immediate value over Dragon Dance variants. Draco Meteor : Draco Meteor is Mega Dragonite's strongest attack, giving it immediate damage against neutral targets and Dragon-types such as Garchomp, Hydreigon , and opposing Mega Dragonite. Its Special Attack drop can make Mega Dragonite easier to take advantage of afterward, so it is best used when picking up a KO or forcing major damage on a key target. Thunderbolt : Thunderbolt pressures Water- and Flying-types such as Primarina, Corviknight, Basculegion-M , and Mega Gyarados , preventing them from switching into Mega Dragonite safely. movesets.name: Dragon Dance
movesets.description_plain: Dragonite uses Multiscale to find setup opportunities with Dragon Dance, letting it become a threatening late-game sweeper with strong priority in Extreme Speed and the ability to break past common defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Aegislash with Earthquake. Scale Shot versus Outrage : Scale Shot is preferred for boosting Dragonite's Speed further after Dragon Dance, making it harder to revenge kill without requiring multiple Dragon Dance boosts. Unlike Outrage, Scale Shot does not make contact, helping Dragonite avoid contact damage from Garchomp 's Rough Skin. Outrage is a much stronger Dragon-type attack, but locking Dragonite into it can make it easier for Fairy-types like Primarina , Sylveon , and Mega Floette to punish it. Earthquake : Earthquake gives Dragonite important coverage against Steel-, Fire-, Rock-, and Poison-types such as Aegislash, Kingambit , Mega Charizard X , Mega Tyranitar , and Toxapex. Extreme Speed versus Roost : Extreme Speed gives Dragonite strong priority, letting it pick off weakened faster threats such as Sneasler , Mega Lopunny , and Greninja without relying on Scale Shot boosts. Roost is an alternative that helps Dragonite preserve Multiscale and set up more reliably against defensive Pokemon, but dropping Extreme Speed makes it easier to revenge kill. Jolly versus Adamant : On Lum Berry sets, a Jolly nature lets Dragonite outspeed threats Adamant Dragonite cannot after Dragon Dance, such as Mega Gengar , Mega Delphox , Mega Lopunny, and Mega Greninja . An Adamant nature gives Dragonite more power while still outspeeding threats such as Meowscarada , Sneasler, Garchomp, and Hydreigon after a boost. On Dragoninite sets, Adamant Mega Dragonite already outspeeds the faster unboosted threats Jolly regular Dragonite aims for, while a Jolly nature improves Mega Dragonite's matchup against opposing boosted sweepers such as Adamant Scale Shot Garchomp, Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar and Mega Charizard X, and Quiver Dance Volcarona . Other Options Thunder Punch : Thunder Punch lets Dragonite pressure Water- and Flying-types, such as Primarina, Azumarill , Corviknight , and Mega Clefable , but it is difficult to justify over Extreme Speed due to its revenge killing utility. Fire Punch : Fire Punch can be used to hit Steel- and Grass-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor , Skarmory , and Mega Meganium more directly, but Earthquake is generally preferred for its stronger coverage. Items Lum Berry versus Dragoninite : Lum Berry gives Dragonite more freedom to set up through status from Pokemon such as Rotom-Wash , Umbreon , and Hippowdon . Dragoninite trades Dragonite's higher base Attack for Mega Dragonite's improved Speed tier, making it harder to revenge kill after a Dragon Dance.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description_plain: Hydreigon can serve as a pivotal offensive piece for teams using its high Special Attack and solid natural Speed. Its good typing and ability enable it to safely come in against the likes of Hippowdon and Ceruledge , then proceed to break apart the opposition. Flamethrower can help Hydreigon break through the likes of Corviknight and Scizor . U-turn : U-turn enables Hydreigon to keep up momentum against checks such as Primarina and Sylveon . Taunt : Taunt can shut down the likes of Hippowdon and Umbreon , preventing them from forcing Hydreigon out with tools like Yawn. Nasty Plot : Nasty Plot enables Hydreigon to threaten OHKOs on foes such as Mega Venusaur with Draco Meteor. Modest : With a Modest nature, Hydreigon can threaten an OHKO on specially defensive targets like Hippowdon and Corviknight after a Nasty Plot boost with Draco Meteor and Flamethrower, respectively. Items Focus Sash : Focus Sash allows Hydreigon to trade against threats such as Sneasler and Mega Starmie with Draco Meteor and Dark Pulse, respectively. White Herb : White Herb enables Hydreigon to fire off two full-power Draco Meteors in a row, potentially overwhelming a would-be check such as Umbreon. movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description_plain: Hydreigon finds its place in the metagame as an excellent Choice Scarf user, outspeeding and being a good answer to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M as well as other common Pokemon such as Garchomp , Sinistcha , Mega Froslass , Mega Delphox , and Mega Gengar . Hydreigon's typing is also helpful against Mega Charizard Y , allowing it to resist Heat Wave, sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Solar Beam while hitting it back hard with STAB Draco Meteor. Earth Power vs. Heat Wave : Both Earth Power and Heat Wave can hit Steel-types, with Earth Power having the advantage of dealing more damage to Kingambit and Archaludon . On the other hand, Heat Wave being a spread move allows Hydreigon to hit Kingambit on teams that have redirection while also threatening Corviknight and Whimsicott . Snarl : Snarl can weaken a plethora of special attackers, such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Floette , Archaludon, Sylveon , and Mega Dragonite . After inducing a Special Attack drop, Hydreigon can always survive Mega Froslass's Blizzard as well as Archaludon's and Mega Dragonite's Dragon Pulse. Items Choice Scarf : Choice Scarf allows Hydreigon to always outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl . Abilities Levitate : Levitate provides Hydreigon with a helpful Ground immunity, making it a good partner for Pokemon that like spamming Earthquake like Excadrill . Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon are the easiest and best way to keep Hydreigon in check, always OHKOing it with their STAB moves, while it can only slow them down with Special Attack drops from Snarl. After activating Unburden with White Herb or Focus Sash, Sneasler will always outspeed Hydreigon and OHKO it with Close Combat. Sneasler can also use Fake Out on Hydreigon, which is incredibly helpful for Sneasler's teammates like Garchomp and Basculegion-M, allowing Garchomp in particular to OHKO Hydreigon with Dragon Claw. Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar , and Corviknight are huge roadblocks for Choice Scarf Hydreigon: Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar can take any hit Hydreigon throws at them and retaliate with Low Kick or set up with Dragon Dance and Swords Dance. Alternatively, Corviknight can always survive a few Heat Waves and set up Tailwind. Good Partners and Synergies : Choice Scarf Hydreigon is a great piece on sand teams, as they appreciate its ability to threaten and potentially OHKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and most Garchomp sets, which they can struggle against. In return, Excadrill, a common feature on sand teams, threatens both Fairy- and Steel-types for Hydreigon with its STAB moves. Rotom-Wash also works well with Hydreigon, threatening damage on Corviknight as well as crippling Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar with Will-O-Wisp. Mega Charizard Y is also a potential partner that appreciates Hydreigon threatening and removing Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Garchomp while helping it in return by removing Steel-types, resisting Fairy-type attacks, hitting Fairy-types especially hard with sun-boosted Weather Ball, and cleanly removing Sneasler. * How to Overcome Hydreigon's Weaknesses : Hydreigon appreciates partners that can threaten and deal huge damage to the Fairy- and Steel-types that wall it. Pokemon like Sneasler, Mega Charizard Y, Hisuian Arcanine , Corviknight, and Excadrill are all great against Fairy-types; some are also great against Kingambit and opposing Corviknight. Sneasler in particular is a good Hydreigon partner, hitting most Steel-types incredibly hard with Close Combat as well as having a great matchup against Fairy-types with Dire Claw or Gunk Shot. Mega Froslass and Corviknight have a great matchup against Sneasler, with Mega Froslass being immune to Close Combat and resisting Dire Claw while hitting Sneasler hard with either of its STAB moves. Corviknight is immune to Dire Claw and removes Sneasler with Brave Bird.

movesets.name: Glass Cannon
movesets.description_plain: Lycanroc-D rose to prominence as a strong and fast attacker, capable of hitting top threats for big damage thanks to a good offensive typing for the format, a strong ability, solid coverage, and good Speed. Notably, Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit are easily OHKOed by Lycanroc-D. Accelerock : Accelerock is capable of OHKOing Mega Charizard Y, allowing Lycanroc-D to remove Mega Charizard Y despite any speed control, and it can also 2HKO Mega Froslass . Furthermore, it allows Lycanroc-D to remove low-HP Pokemon, typically those taken down to their Focus Sash like Whimsicott and Sneasler . Close Combat : Close Combat is the best coverage option for Lycanroc-D, as it is able to OHKO Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar , Pokemon that would otherwise easily shrug off Lycanroc-D's Rock-type options. Rock Slide Spamming : While Rock Slide's flinch chance isn't to be relied on, Lycanroc-D's high Speed enables it to fish for flinches. With enough flinches, Rock Slide can slowly chip down Pokemon into range of Close Combat. Items Focus Sash : Focus Sash allows Lycanroc-D to survive a powerful attack such as Sucker Punch from Black Glasses Kingambit after it uses Swords Dance, allowing Lycanroc-D to retaliate with Close Combat. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Lycanroc-D struggles to deal significant damage to Pokemon that resist its options such as Aegislash . Garchomp can tank a Close Combat, break Lycanroc-D's Focus Sash because of Rough Skin, and OHKO it with Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can move before Lycanroc-D and take it down to its Focus Sash, leaving it vulnerable. Non-Choice Scarf sets can do the same with Water-type attacks like Wave Crash and Liquidation, and they can then finish it off the following turn with Aqua Jet. Sneasler resists all of Lycanroc-D's most popular options and takes it out with a combination of Fake Out and Close Combat. Sinistcha can redirect Close Combat easily, keeping allies like Kingambit safe, or it can 2HKO Lycanroc-D by itself with Matcha Gotcha. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Froslass loves Lycanroc-D's ability to handle common threats to it like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Kingambit. In return, Mega Froslass is able to take down Garchomp, Sneasler, and Sinistcha with Blizzard, and it can even outspeed and OHKO non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M sets. Mega Scovillain is another popular Mega-Evolved partner for Lycanroc-D, since it also appreciates Lycanroc-D's ability to threaten Mega Charizard Y. Mega Scovillain can protect Lycanroc-D from Basculegion-M with Rage Powder while using Overheat to take out Aegislash and Sinistcha. Kingambit is able to threaten Basculegion-M, Sinistcha, and Aegislash with Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave, while your own Basculegion-M can also take out Sinistcha and Aegislash with Last Respects and threaten big damage onto Incineroar with Wave Crash. Sneasler, on the other hand, provides Fake Out support for Lycanroc-D to allow it to safely attack while deterring Incineroar from switching in, allowing Lycanroc-D to attack at full power. Sneasler is also able to take on Mega Floette , which Lycanroc-D can sometimes struggle to deal damage to. How to Overcome Lycanroc-D's Weaknesses : Lycanroc-D is best utilized early to pick up KOs on threats to sweeper allies like Mega Froslass, so you should aim to take out Kingambit and Mega Charizard Y with Lycanroc-D before it goes down. Bringing allies that benefit from these foes' removal like the aforementioned Mega Froslass and Basculegion-M is a good choice, as they can easily take down the Pokemon that Lycanroc-D may struggle with. Note that Lycanroc-D is only meant to come out in specific matchups, most commonly against sun teams. Therefore, knowing when to bench it is key, as it may sometimes just be a sitting duck in matchups that aren't favorable towards it, such as Mega Blastoise and Mega Floette.

  • How to Overcome Lycanroc-D's Weaknesses: Lycanroc-D is best utilized early to pick up KOs on threats to sweeper allies like Mega Froslass, so you should aim to take out Kingambit and Mega Charizard Y with Lycanroc-D before it goes down. Bringing allies that benefit from these foes' removal like the aforementioned Mega Froslass and Basculegion-M is a good choice, as they can easily take down the Pokemon that Lycanroc-D may struggle with. Note that Lycanroc-D is only meant to come out in specific matchups, most commonly against sun teams. Therefore, knowing when to bench it is key, as it may sometimes just be a sitting duck in matchups that aren't favorable towards it, such as Mega Blastoise and Mega Floette.

movesets.name: Rain Support
movesets.description_plain: For rain teams, Politoed is a bulky support Pokemon that enables Archaludon while also threatening with Perish Song late-game. Politoed's Drizzle allows it to do well against Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y , Incineroar , and Mega Delphox by weakening their attacks and allowing Politoed to pressure them with Weather Ball. Meanwhile, Perish Song pressures foes late-game, as they have limited opportunities to switch. Weather Ball : Weather Ball gives Politoed a reliable single-target attack in rain, letting it pressure Fire-types such as Incineroar, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Delphox without relying entirely on its partner for damage. On teams with Mega Froslass , Weather Ball allows Politoed to pressure Garchomp if rain has been replaced with snow. Perish Song : Perish Song forces opponents to reposition their Pokemon or risk losing both of them. Mega Gengar can trap targets so that they cannot escape Perish Song normally. Protect helps Politoed stall turns and avoid being removed before the Perishing count finishes. Hypnosis versus Ice Beam versus Encore : Hypnosis can temporarily remove a key threat from play and give Politoed's partner room to attack or set up, though its poor accuracy makes it unreliable. Ice Beam gives Politoed consistent coverage against Garchomp, Dragonite , and Sinistcha regardless of the active weather. Encore punishes passive moves like Protect, Trick Room, and setup moves, which is especially useful when the opponent attempts to stall out rain. Other Options Muddy Water : Muddy Water can be used over Weather Ball for spread damage and accuracy drops, which can be useful when Politoed wants to support its partner while still attacking. However, Muddy Water's lower power makes Politoed worse at immediately pressuring Fire-types like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y. Helping Hand : Helping Hand compensates for Politoed's limited offensive presence by boosting a partner's attack. It notably amplifies Archaludon's wallbreaking power, allowing +1 Flash Cannon to OHKO bulky Mega Floette and Sylveon and Electro Shot to OHKO bulky Rotom-Wash . Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry, in combination with the given defensive spread, gives Politoed the longevity to use Perish Song and stall its turns with Protect while remaining healthy enough to switch out and reset rain later. It notably prevents Adamant Black Glasses Kingambit 's Kowtow Cleave and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast from 2HKOing Politoed. Mystic Water : Mystic Water should be used with an offensive spread, as it further strengthens Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball. This gives Politoed much greater immediate offensive pressure at the cost of Sitrus Berry's longevity. SP Spreads 31 HP / 23 Def / 12 SpD with Calm : 31 HP SPs let Sitrus Berry activate immediately after Politoed gets hit by Maushold 's Super Fang. 12 Special Defense SPs let Politoed survive Modest Mega Floette's Light of Ruin from full health. The remaining SPs are invested in Defense, giving Politoed a solid chance to survive Adamant Basculegion-M 's 150-Base Power Last Respects while improving its ability to take physical attacks from Garchomp and Sneasler . 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA with Modest : This spread maximizes Politoed's Special Attack while maintaining bulk. It should be used with Mystic Water to strengthen Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball enough to guarantee OHKOs on offensive Sneasler and specially bulky Incineroar. The Special Attack investment also allows Ice Beam to always OHKO offensive Garchomp. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Politoed struggles against strong Electric- and Grass-type attacks from Pokemon such as Archaludon and Sinistcha, both of which take little damage from Weather Ball. Opposing weather setters like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar , Mega Froslass, and Torkoal can also remove rain, stopping your own Archaludon from using Electro Shot. Without Ice Beam, Politoed also struggles to threaten Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite , which can deal heavy damage to it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies : Archaludon is the main rain sweeper, using Politoed's rain to fire off Electro Shot immediately and threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Basculegion-M, Milotic , and Aerodactyl . Espathra is a great partner on Baton Pass rain teams, passing Speed and Calm Mind boosts to Archaludon so that it can snowball much more easily once Politoed sets rain. Mega Gengar is the main partner on Perish Song archetypes; it traps foes so that they cannot freely switch out. Incineroar and Sneasler provide Fake Out support to help Politoed use Perish Song or land Hypnosis. Sinistcha gives Politoed teams redirection and Hospitality recovery, while Mega Froslass can set Aurora Veil and reset rain later with Rain Dance. How to Overcome Politoed's Weaknesses : Politoed should be preserved carefully in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Froslass, as maintaining weather control makes these foes far easier for Politoed to deal with. Mega Dragonite can handle Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler threatens Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat, and Kingambit deals with Mega Froslass. Additionally, your own Mega Froslass can use Rain Dance to restore rain without forcing Politoed back onto the field. Against Electric- and Grass-types, Politoed should avoid sitting on the field and instead use Protect, Encore, or Hypnosis, or it should switch out to better position itself later on. Archaludon resists both Electric- and Grass-type attacks and can switch into moves such as Electro Shot from opposing Archaludon and Matcha Gotcha from Sinistcha, accumulating Stamina boots to make itself progressively more difficult to remove with physical attacks, while Incineroar resists Grass-type attacks and threatens Sinistcha. Perish Song should usually be saved for late-game scenarios or situations where the opponent has limited switching options, such as times when Mega Gengar is trapping a target. Sneasler’s Fake Out and Politoed’s Protect can also safely stall turns of the Perishing count.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description_plain: With its typing, Glimmora can resist the STAB moves of multiple attackers in the format, making it a good check to Mega Charizard Y , Mega Floette , and Aerodactyl . Furthermore, its own STAB moves can OHKO several common threats, such as Mega Charizard Y, Aerodactyl, and Whimsicott , while pressuring most of the metagame for super effective damage. Earth Power is used to threaten Steel-types such as Archaludon and Kingambit that both resist its STAB moves and are immune to Toxic Spikes. Ability Toxic Debris punishes physical attackers that attack Glimmora. With Focus Sash, Toxic Spikes can be set up more reliably. This helps punish Pokemon that like to pivot in and out often, such as Incineroar . Items Focus Sash protects Glimmora from being OHKOed by some of the format's heavier hitters, such as Garchomp , Basculegion-M , and Mega Delphox . Focus Sash further helps Glimmora by granting it more opportunities to set up Toxic Spikes through its ability. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Metagame staples such as Garchomp and Mega Delphox reliably outspeed Glimmora, threatening major damage. Furthermore, even though it can hit many Pokemon for super effective damage, Glimmora can still fail to OHKO them. For example, Mega Floette requires two Sludge Bombs to be taken out. Similarly, Kingambit can tank an Earth Power and OHKO back with Iron Head. Special attackers like Mega Delphox and Rotom-Wash threaten to OHKO Glimmora without triggering Toxic Debris. Good Partners and Synergies : Whimsicott is a strong ally for Glimmora, using its Prankster-boosted Tailwind to reliably set the pace of the battle for Glimmora to outspeed threats such as Mega Floette while using STAB Fairy-type attacks to check Garchomp. Additionally, Glimmora can help OHKO Sneasler , which Whimsicott can struggle with. Mega Charizard Y is another good partner; its Fire-type STAB moves help check Steel-types, and its Drought protects Glimmora from Water-type attacks such as Wave Crash from Basculegion-M. Mega Charizard Y likewise benefits from Glimmora, as Glimmora's Power Gem can hit Incineroar , which would otherwise resist Mega Charizard Y’s attacks, for super effective damage. How To Overcome Glimmora's Weaknesses : Partnering Glimmora with Mega Charizard Y helps it cover threats such as Basculegion-M and Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam, and the sun weakens their Water-type attacks. Additionally, Kingambit threatens Farigiraf and Mega Delphox, which can threaten Glimmora with Twin Beam and Psyshock, respectively.

movesets.name: Offensive Support
movesets.description_plain: Talonflame can consistently set the pace of the battle due to the priority boost on Tailwind granted by Gale Wings. Gale Wings also gives it immediate offensive pressure with its primary STAB Flying-type moves. With its high Speed, Talonflame can threaten many prominent Pokemon like Kingambit , Sneasler , and Whimsicott with its STAB Fire- and Flying-type attacks. Flare Blitz vs. Will-O-Wisp : Flare Blitz can threaten large damage onto Kingambit, Sinistcha , and Mega Froslass , while Will-O-Wisp provides damage reduction against physical attackers like Garchomp and Corviknight . Furthermore, Will-O-Wisp and Flare Blitz are Talonflame's only ways to pressure Kingambit and Aegislash . Brave Bird vs. Dual Wingbeat vs. Acrobatics : Brave Bird, when boosted by Gale Wings, becomes a powerful priority attack, giving Talonflame immediate pressure. It is much stronger than Dual Wingbeat and Acrobatics, as only Brave Bird can OHKO Scovillain . However, Dual Wingbeat can also be valuable due to its ability to KO Pokemon such as Sneasler and Whimsicott through Focus Sash without breaking Gale Wings. Finally, the lack of recoil damage from Acrobatics allows no-item Talonflame to threaten heavy Flying-type damage without deactivating Gale Wings. Other Options Taunt : Taunt can be used over Flare Blitz or Will-O-Wisp for an extra tool against Trick Room teams. Furthermore, Taunt can be used to disrupt redirectors like Maushold and Sinistcha as well as setup Pokemon such as Calm Mind Mega Floette . Quick Guard : Quick Guard is a niche move that can be used over Protect, Flare Blitz, or Will-O-Wisp. It protects allies against Fake Out users like Incineroar as well as other priority attacks like Aqua Jet from Basculegion-M and Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Pokemon with Intimidate, such as Incineroar, severely weaken Talonflame's damage output. Rock Slide users like Garchomp, Tyranitar , and Aerodactyl are strong checks to Talonflame, as they are able to OHKO it. Garchomp is notable, as Rough Skin breaks Gale Wings regardless of what Flying-type move Talonflame is carrying. Furthermore, Mega Tyranitar 's sand works similarly in breaking Gale Wings. Archaludon is also a great check to Talonflame, resisting its Flying-type moves and boosting up with Stamina. Fake Out users like Incineroar can break Talonflame's Gale Wings, removing the option to use priority Tailwind. Good Partners and Synergies : Garchomp and Mega Floette are some of the best Pokemon to pair Talonflame with. Talonflame's priority Tailwind and immunity to Earthquake allows Garchomp to put immense pressure on opponents. Additionally, Garchomp's Rock Slide in Tailwind lets it act as a great check against prominent Mega Charizard Y compositions by always outspeeding Mega Charizard Y in Tailwind. Mega Floette and Mega Gardevoir also benefit greatly from Tailwind, and Talonflame's STAB moves cover Sneasler and Kingambit for both. In return, their STAB Fairy-type moves handle Dragon-types like Garchomp and Dragonite . Kingambit discourages Pokemon with Intimidate from switching in with Defiant and provides high priority damage with Sucker Punch, which can OHKO opposing Basculegion-M. Finally, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can take advantage of Tailwind by capitalizing on its powerful STAB attacks to KO threats such as Mega Aerodactyl . Additionally, bulky variants with Sitrus Berry or Mystic Water can use Tailwind to outspeed Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Gengar . How to Overcome Talonflame's Weaknesses : Protecting Talonflame and preserving Gale Wings is a viable strategy against other Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott. Another viable strategy is to preserve Gale Wings for late-game scenarios, mainly by manually switching out. Kingambit can be used to threaten Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl, which would otherwise use Aqua Jet or Rock Slide on Talonflame. Mega Floette also helps Talonflame, as its Light Of Ruin can quickly KO Archaludon and Garchomp.

movesets.name: Focus Sash Offensive Support
movesets.description_plain: Aerodactyl leverages both its high Speed to set Tailwind and STAB Rock Slide to either check metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y or simply steal turns with flinches. A fast Rock Slide in particular sets Aerodactyl apart from other Tailwind users such as Whimsicott and Talonflame , as Rock-type coverage pairs well with other spread move attackers' STAB moves, such as Garchomp with its Earthquake and Mega Charizard Y with its Heat Wave, making Aerodactyl a key component in these offensive cores. Dual Wingbeat versus Wide Guard : Dual Wingbeat covers Fighting-types that resist Rock Slide, most notably Sneasler , as Aerodactyl is one of the few Pokemon that can outspeed and OHKO it. Dual Wingbeat hitting multiple times cuts through any potential Focus Sash from Sneasler and Whimsicott. Wide Guard protects both Aerodactyl and its partners from opposing Aerodactyl and Garchomp using Rock Slide, which Mega Charizard Y in particular appreciates. It also offers defensive counterplay against other strong spread move users, such as blocking Water Spout Mega Blastoise , Blizzard Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales , as well as Hyper Voice Sylveon . Other Options Taunt : Taunt is a viable option over Dual Wingbeat or even over Protect as a surprise option in a best-of-one setting. Suppressing moves like Trick Room, Follow Me, Rage Powder, and Mega Gengar 's Perish Song can stop such strategies without relying on Rock Slide flinches. Items Focus Sash : Focus Sash ensures Aerodactyl can set Tailwind regardless of its common weaknesses. In particular, it ensures that Tailwind is set against faster threats such as Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash , Rotom-Heat , and Basculegion , as well as Sand Rush Excadrill and priority attackers such as Mega Scizor with Bullet Punch. Abilities Unnerve : Unnerve is uniquely positioned in Regulation M-A, as many commonly used items are berries. Stopping Sitrus Berry from being used helps deal with problematic defensive Pokemon such as Incineroar and Sinistcha , with targets like the latter notably being stopped from activating Sitrus Berry midway through Dual Wingbeat. Unnerve also assists partner attackers such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler score in scoring OHKOs despite opposing resist berries such as Occa Berry defensive Whimsicott, Chople Berry Kingambit , and Incineroar's choice of Passho Berry, Chople Berry, or Shuca Berry. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Aerodactyl has many common weaknesses, notably to Water-, Rock-, and Steel-type moves such as Wave Crash, Rock Slide, and Iron Head from Basculegion, Garchomp, and Excadrill. Aerodactyl's Flying typing opens it up to other Rock Slides, especially from Choice Scarf Garchomp and Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill, which outspeed it and resist Aerodactyl's Rock Slide. Excadrill can also use Iron Head to avoid Wide Guard and deal more damage to Aerodactyl. Choice Scarf Basculegion can similarly easily bring it Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before it moves. Non-Choice Scarf Basculegion, while not able to outspeed Aerodactyl, can use Wave Crash or Liquidation to bring it down to Focus Sash, and then attack with Aqua Jet the following turn to finish it off. Priority moves can easily dispatch Aerodactyl after its Focus Sash is broken. Notably, Aerodactyl's typing makes it weak to Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor. Kingambit's unboosted Sucker Punch deals upwards of half Aerodactyl's health, making it similarly effective at finishing off Aerodactyl. Both Kingambit and Aegislash can use Iron Head to easily bring Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before finishing with Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak, respectively, while resisting Rock Slide and Dual Wingbeat. Wide Guard from Aegislash, Pelipper , and opposing Aerodactyl blocks Rock Slide and is similarly annoying for Aerodactyl's common partners like Heat Wave Mega Charizard Y and Earthquake Garchomp. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Charizard Y weakens Water-type moves and hits Basculegion super effectively with the sun and Solar Beam, respectively. Garchomp covers Steel-types and other common Rock Slide users such as Tyranitar and Excadrill with Earthquake, which it can freely use next to Aerodactyl. Mega Floette and Sylveon are effective Tailwind recipients with their spread Fairy-type attacks and pair well with Dual Wingbeat Aerodactyl, as it can quickly dispatch Sneasler before it can threaten them with Dire Claw. How to Overcome Aerodactyl's Weaknesses : Aerodactyl's checks can actually answer themselves when used in tandem with Aerodactyl. Garchomp and Basculegion can hit opposing Garchomp and Basculegion super effectively with their STAB Dragon Claw or Scale Shot and Last Respects, and hitting first with these moves is easier with Aerodactyl's Tailwind support. Similarly, Kingambit can check opposing Kingambit with Low Kick and threaten an OHKO with Sucker Punch against the ever-present Basculegion. Tailwind generally has a problem with Trick Room, so being able to KO or Taunt Trick Room setters before they can set up is vital. Mega Charizard Y can easily clear Sinistcha and more cleanly KO Farigiraf after Aerodactyl's Rock Slide damage. • Aerodactyl leverages both its high Speed to set Tailwind and STAB Rock Slide to either check metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y or simply steal turns with flinches. A fast Rock Slide in particular sets Aerodactyl apart from other Tailwind users such as Whimsicott and Talonflame, as Rock-type coverage pairs well with other spread move attackers' STAB moves, such as Garchomp with its Earthquake and Mega Charizard Y with its Heat Wave, making Aerodactyl a key component in these offensive cores.

  • Dual Wingbeat versus Wide Guard: Dual Wingbeat covers Fighting-types that resist Rock Slide, most notably Sneasler, as Aerodactyl is one of the few Pokemon that can outspeed and OHKO it. Dual Wingbeat hitting multiple times cuts through any potential Focus Sash from Sneasler and Whimsicott.

  • Wide Guard protects both Aerodactyl and its partners from opposing Aerodactyl and Garchomp using Rock Slide, which Mega Charizard Y in particular appreciates. It also offers defensive counterplay against other strong spread move users, such as blocking Water Spout Mega Blastoise, Blizzard Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, as well as Hyper Voice Sylveon.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt is a viable option over Dual Wingbeat or even over Protect as a surprise option in a best-of-one setting. Suppressing moves like Trick Room, Follow Me, Rage Powder, and Mega Gengar's Perish Song can stop such strategies without relying on Rock Slide flinches.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures Aerodactyl can set Tailwind regardless of its common weaknesses. In particular, it ensures that Tailwind is set against faster threats such as Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Basculegion, as well as Sand Rush Excadrill and priority attackers such as Mega Scizor with Bullet Punch.

Abilities

  • Unnerve: Unnerve is uniquely positioned in Regulation M-A, as many commonly used items are berries. Stopping Sitrus Berry from being used helps deal with problematic defensive Pokemon such as Incineroar and Sinistcha, with targets like the latter notably being stopped from activating Sitrus Berry midway through Dual Wingbeat. Unnerve also assists partner attackers such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler score in scoring OHKOs despite opposing resist berries such as Occa Berry defensive Whimsicott, Chople Berry Kingambit, and Incineroar's choice of Passho Berry, Chople Berry, or Shuca Berry.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Aerodactyl has many common weaknesses, notably to Water-, Rock-, and Steel-type moves such as Wave Crash, Rock Slide, and Iron Head from Basculegion, Garchomp, and Excadrill. Aerodactyl's Flying typing opens it up to other Rock Slides, especially from Choice Scarf Garchomp and Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill, which outspeed it and resist Aerodactyl's Rock Slide. Excadrill can also use Iron Head to avoid Wide Guard and deal more damage to Aerodactyl. Choice Scarf Basculegion can similarly easily bring it Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before it moves. Non-Choice Scarf Basculegion, while not able to outspeed Aerodactyl, can use Wave Crash or Liquidation to bring it down to Focus Sash, and then attack with Aqua Jet the following turn to finish it off. Priority moves can easily dispatch Aerodactyl after its Focus Sash is broken. Notably, Aerodactyl's typing makes it weak to Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor. Kingambit's unboosted Sucker Punch deals upwards of half Aerodactyl's health, making it similarly effective at finishing off Aerodactyl. Both Kingambit and Aegislash can use Iron Head to easily bring Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before finishing with Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak, respectively, while resisting Rock Slide and Dual Wingbeat. movesets.name: Tailwind Setter
movesets.description_plain: Mega Aerodactyl is the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, which makes it an incredibly consistent Tailwind setter while also outspeeding and threatening OHKOs on common Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler . Rock Slide : Mega Aerodactyl is an exceptional user of Rock Slide, since it is able to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y. Thanks to its incredible Speed, Mega Aerodactyl can consistently threaten flinches with Rock Slide. Dual Wingbeat : Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat is incredibly strong thanks to Tough Claws, making it a solid neutral attack against Pokemon like Basculegion-M . Dual Wingbeat is able to OHKO Sneasler, Venusaur , and Whimsicott through their Focus Sash and deal huge damage to Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur . Mega Evolving Aerodactyl : In its base forme, Aerodactyl can still function well as a fast Tailwind setter, so it can be brought to a battle to support another Mega Evolution. Base forme Aerodactyl can also make use of Unnerve to prevent Sitrus Berry on Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf and Chople Berry on Kingambit from activating. Other Options Ice Fang : Mega Aerodactyl's Ice Fang is able to OHKO Garchomp but isn't very useful against other Pokemon. This move can be run over Tailwind or Protect, which will either remove Mega Aerodactyl's ability to support its teammates or make it more vulnerable to Fake Out. Wide Guard : Wide Guard can be used over Protect to shield partner Mega Charizard Y from opposing Rock Slide and stop other spread moves like Mega Froslass 's Blizzard or Garchomp's Earthquake. Dropping Protect makes Mega Aerodactyl more vulnerable, making positioning with it much harder. Abilities Tough Claws : Tough Claws boosts Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Ice Fang, allowing the former to OHKO Sneasler and Whimsicott and the latter to OHKO Garchomp. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Mega Aerodactyl is incredibly weak to Steel-types like Kingambit, Archaludon , and Excadrill , which can easily tank any of its attacks and OHKO it back with their Steel-type attacks. Without Ice Fang, Garchomp can be problematic, since it can deal big damage with Rock Slide, and hitting it with Dual Wingbeat will trigger Rough Skin twice. Other Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar and Rotom-Wash can easily tank Mega Aerodactyl's attacks and then threaten big damage back. Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash can be a particularly bad matchup for Mega Aerodactyl, since it can outspeed and threaten heavy damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Thunderbolt or Hydro Pump or slow it down with Electroweb. Mega Aerodactyl is also susceptible to having its damage output reduced by Incineroar's Intimidate and Mega Scovillain 's Spicy Spray. Good Partners and Synergies : Garchomp is an excellent partner for Mega Aerodactyl, since it can freely use Earthquake next to it and threaten the Steel-types that Mega Aerodactyl struggles against. Sylveon is a great beneficiary of Mega Aerodactyl's Tailwind, with it being able to spam powerful Hyper Voices that threaten Garchomp while Mega Aerodactyl deals with common threats to Sylveon such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Kingambit is able to deter Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf, which could otherwise slow down Mega Aerodactyl with Intimidate and Trick Room, respectively, while also threatening to deal heavy damage to opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Low Kick. Mega Charizard Y works as a great alternative Mega Evolution for Mega Aerodactyl, since it melts through Steel-types and works well with Aerodactyl's base forme. Mega Charizard Y can also handle Mega Evolutions that Mega Aerodactyl might struggle against, such as Mega Scovillain and Mega Floette , while Mega Aerodactyl can deal with Mega Dragonite in return. Farigiraf can block Fake Out thanks to Armor Tail, which is very useful for Mega Aerodactyl sets that aren't running Protect. Farigiraf also blocks Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet while being able to reverse Trick Room. How to Overcome Mega Aerodactyl's Weaknesses : Pair Mega Aerodactyl with powerful sweepers to make full use of its fast Tailwind. Pokemon like Garchomp and Sylveon can threaten powerful spread damage on the field while also threatening some of Mega Aerodactyl's checks, such as Archaludon and Mega Tyranitar. Use Mega Aerodactyl to threaten Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Sinistcha, which could otherwise disrupt your offense. Use an alternative Mega Evolution like Mega Charizard Y and Pokemon like Garchomp and Kingambit to deal with matchups where Mega Aerodactyl shouldn't be brought, such as against rain, sand, and Trick Room teams.

movesets.name: Focus Sash
movesets.description_plain: Ceruledge's strong typing and access to Swords Dance make it a powerful offensive presence, which includes the ability to overwhelm targets like Corviknight and Volcarona that normally wall physical attackers well. Weak Armor : The combination of Weak Armor and Focus Sash can turn Ceruledge into a deadly fast sweeper, making it risky for prominent physical threats like Mega Lopunny and Sneasler to attack it. Shadow Sneak : Paired with Weak Armor, Ceruledge with Shadow Sneak can win priority wars it would otherwise lose, on top of being a strong cleaning attack in general. Poltergeist : Poltergeist is Ceruledge's strongest STAB attack and best overall source of damage, but be careful against targets that potentially use Sitrus Berry or other consumable items; some checks like Toxapex will go without an item to render Poltergeist useless from the start! Bitter Blade : Bitter Blade's strong recovery is useful after being taken down to its Focus Sash, potentially giving Ceruledge more of a buffer against priority moves. Against weaker attacks, it can also heal Ceruledge back to full so that it can still utilize Focus Sash. Close Combat : After a Swords Dance, Close Combat has a high chance of OHKOing physically defensive versions of both Archaludon and Umbreon ! It's also strong against Mega Gyarados , which will often Mega Evolve to resist Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak. Beware of Garchomp : Be wary of Rough Skin Garchomp that try to switch into Ceruledge's Bitter Blade or Shadow Sneak, as the passive damage nullifies Focus Sash and leaves Ceruledge vulnerable. Scale Shot can also be problematic, since it can trigger Weak Armor's Defense drop several times, though usually four hits are required to OHKO. Other Options Jolly Nature : The loss in power can be problematic elsewhere, but going Jolly over Adamant with the given SP spread will allow Ceruledge to outrun Choice Scarf Meowscarada after a single Weak Armor activation. Flash Fire : Flash Fire allows Ceruledge to create momentum from the back by switching in on Mega Charizard Y 's Fire-type attacks. Furthermore, an undamaged Ceruledge can take Stealth Rock chip damage and still always survive Timid Mega Charizard Y's Scorching Sands.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Ceruledge rose to popularity as a solid answer to many metagame threats, namely the combination of Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette as well as Pokemon like Sylveon and Sneasler , thanks to its typing, ability, and stats. Shadow Sneak : Shadow Sneak makes up for Ceruledge's rather lackluster Speed and inability to boost it, picking off low-HP Pokemon like Sneasler and Kingambit that are common users of Focus Sash. Bulk Up : Bulk Up allows Ceruledge to better take on Pokemon like Incineroar and, notably, Kingambit. Other Options Swords Dance : Swords Dance allows Ceruledge to play more aggressively, using fewer turns to get more powerful, though it also means Ceruledge will oftentimes go down quicker. Items Colbur Berry : Colbur Berry allows Ceruledge to survive Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch from Kingambit. This gives Ceruledge an opportunity to set up, outdamage Kingambit with Bitter Blade, and end the encounter with a solid amount of HP. Abilities Flash Fire : Flash Fire turns Ceruledge into a Mega Charizard Y counter, allowing Ceruledge to sit in front of it and set up with ease while also benefiting from an even stronger Bitter Blade thanks to the sun and a potential Flash Fire boost. SP Spreads 32 HP / 23 Atk / 3 Def / 8 SpD with Adamant : The given SPs allow Ceruledge to survive Stomping Tantrum from Jolly Garchomp and +2 Kowtow Cleave from Black Glasses Kingambit when at +1 Defense from Bulk Up, and they give it the best odds of surviving Shadow Ball from Mega Gengar . The Attack SPs allow Ceruledge to OHKO no-bulk Basculegion-M with +2 Shadow Sneak and nearly always OHKO Kingambit with +1 Bitter Blade. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Despite Colbur Berry, Incineroar, Hydreigon , and Mega Tyranitar are still issues for Ceruledge, resisting both of Ceruledge's attacking moves and retaliating with Throat Chop, Dark Pulse, and Knock Off, respectively. Garchomp also heavily threatens Ceruledge with Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum while shrugging off Bitter Blade and Shadow Sneak. Basculegion-M can easily OHKO Ceruledge with 100 Base Power Last Respects and Wave Crash, the latter of which even OHKOes Ceruledge after it uses Bulk Up. Mega Blastoise and Milotic also threaten huge Water-type damage with Water Spout and Muddy Water, respectively; Milotic can even use Coil to match Ceruledge's Bulk Up boosts. Rock-type Pokemon like Hisuian Arcanine , Mega Aerodactyl , and the aforementioned Mega Tyranitar all resist Bitter Blade and threaten Ceruledge with Rock Slide. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Floette hits the Dark- and Dragon-types that Ceruledge struggles with, while Ceruledge provides help against Mega Charizard Y and Steel-types like Corviknight in return. Milotic and Sneasler provide coverage against Dark- and Rock-type Pokemon, both notably scaring away Incineroar with Competitive and White Herb, respectively. Sinistcha is able to redirect Water-type attacks with ease and hit Water-types with Matcha Gotcha. It often carries Kasib Berry to even redirect Ghost-type attacks like Shadow Ball from Mega Froslass , giving Ceruledge space to set up. How to Overcome Ceruledge's Weaknesses : Ceruledge must be paired with offensive threats that can handle the foes it can't, such as Mega Floette, which often fulfills this role. It forms a strong offensive duo with Ceruledge, handling the Dragon-types that resist Ceruledge's Bitter Blade, while Ceruledge hits the Steel-types that resist Mega Floette's Fairy-type attacks. On the defensive side, Fake Out and redirection support from Incineroar and Sinistcha give Ceruledge a far easier time setting up. To keep Ceruledge strong, answers to Intimidate users, particularly Incineroar, are important. Milotic and Sneasler threaten Incineroar with big damage, while Kingambit can also deter it, though not as effectively, as Kingambit itself fears Flare Blitz.

strategies.overview_plain: Welcome to the first format of Pokemon Champions, Regulation M-A! Expect rapid changes as this metagame evolves.

movesets.name: Pivot
movesets.description_plain: The combination of an excellent defensive typing, fantastic ability, and solid bulk lets Rotom-Wash act as a great pivot that can handle physical attackers such as Garchomp , Dragonite , Mega Gyarados , and Scizor . Volt Switch : Volt Switch lets Rotom-Wash maintain momentum, allowing its teammates to get on the field safely. Hydro Pump : Hydro Pump gives Rotom-Wash reliable damage against the Ground-types that try to switch into Volt Switch. Will-O-Wisp : Will-O-Wisp acts as a deterrent for physically offensive foes, such as Sneasler , Dragon Dance Dragonite, Aegislash , and Garchomp. Thunderbolt versus Discharge : Thunderbolt has more Base Power than Discharge, but Discharge can be used to paralyze foes faster than Rotom-Wash, such as Mega Lopunny , Sneasler, and Greninja . Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry provides quick healing to Rotom-Wash, especially after surviving high-Base Power moves from strong foes. Leftovers : Leftovers can be used as an alternative option over Sitrus Berry, providing Rotom-Wash passive healing, which makes up for its lack of reliable recovery. Additionally, Leftovers synergizes with a Bold nature and the secondary stat spread better than Sitrus Berry. SP Spreads 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest : Maximizing Rotom-Wash's decent Special Attack stat allows it to roll a very small OHKO chance on Mega Charizard Y , as well as letting Rotom-Wash reliably 2HKO Dragonite after Stealth Rock and specially defensive Hippowdon . 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpA with Bold : When fully invested in Defense, Rotom-Wash can stop powerful physical sweepers, such as Garchomp and Kingambit , while threatening them with Will-O-Wisp.

  • Hydro Pump: Hydro Pump gives Rotom-Wash reliable damage against the Ground-types that try to switch into Volt Switch.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp acts as a deterrent for physically offensive foes, such as Sneasler, Dragon Dance Dragonite, Aegislash, and Garchomp.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: Thunderbolt has more Base Power than Discharge, but Discharge can be used to paralyze foes faster than Rotom-Wash, such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, and Greninja.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry provides quick healing to Rotom-Wash, especially after surviving high-Base Power moves from strong foes.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers can be used as an alternative option over Sitrus Berry, providing Rotom-Wash passive healing, which makes up for its lack of reliable recovery. Additionally, Leftovers synergizes with a Bold nature and the secondary stat spread better than Sitrus Berry.

  • 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest: Maximizing Rotom-Wash's decent Special Attack stat allows it to roll a very small OHKO chance on Mega Charizard Y, as well as letting Rotom-Wash reliably 2HKO Dragonite after Stealth Rock and specially defensive Hippowdon.

  • 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpA with Bold: When fully invested in Defense, Rotom-Wash can stop powerful physical sweepers, such as Garchomp and Kingambit, while threatening them with Will-O-Wisp.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description_plain: Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash trades most of its bulk investment for greater offensive investment, while still being able to tank hits thanks to its naturally high defensive stats. With Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash can more consistently take on the likes of Aerodactyl , Mega Delphox , and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M . Electroweb : Thanks to Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash can consistently use Electroweb to provide Speed control for its team, slowing down fast threats like Aerodactyl and Alolan Ninetales . Volt Switch : As opposed to the bulkier sets, Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash can use Volt Switch to quickly pivot out of unfavorable situations while dealing chip damage, possibly breaking a Focus Sash on a Sneasler , Basculegion-M, Aerodactyl, or Whimsicott . Other Options Will-O-Wisp : Will-O-Wisp can cripple physical attackers and, with Choice Scarf, be used on fast Pokemon like Sneasler before they move. It is generally forgone, however, as locking Rotom-Wash into a status move is undesirable. Running Will-O-Wisp also requires dropping Thunderbolt, Rotom-Wash's most consistent Electric-type STAB option. Items Choice Scarf : Choice Scarf allows Rotom-Wash to outrun faster Pokemon such as Talonflame , Mega Charizard Y , and Mega Gengar . Thanks to the Speed boost from Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash becomes a reliable revenge killer, switching in to take out low-HP Pokemon with either Electroweb, which also hits the other foe and provides Speed control, or Volt Switch, which improves positioning. SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest : This spread maximizes Rotom-Wash's Speed and Special Attack, allowing it to outpace the likes of Mega Delphox and Adamant Mega Aerodactyl . 14 HP / 27 SpA / 25 Spe with Timid : With the given Speed investment, Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash always outruns Choice Scarf (RC) Basculegion-M while surviving Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette ; the remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : While Rotom-Wash has an amazing defensive typing, it struggles against Grass-types, mainly Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur , which resist all of its common attacks. Sinistcha can also redirect these attacks, preventing Rotom-Wash from dealing meaningful damage or burning foes like Kingambit , while Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur can heavily damage Rotom-Wash with Matcha Gotcha and Giga Drain, respectively. Dragon-types like Archaludon and Hydreigon can also shrug off a burn, resist all of Rotom-Wash's common attacks, and retaliate with Electro Shot and Dark Pulse, respectively. Mega Floette and Mega Scovillain pose issues for Rotom-Wash as well, setting up in front of it or heavily damaging it with Giga Drain, respectively; Mega Floette can easily take Rotom-Wash's attacks thanks to its naturally high Special Defense and retaliate with Moonblast or Light of Ruin, with the latter threatening an OHKO. Good Partners and Synergies : Garchomp works well with Rotom-Wash, freely using Earthquake and threatening opposing Dragon-types with Dragon Claw. Excadrill can also use Earthquake next to Rotom-Wash, as well as Iron Head to beat Mega Floette and Rock Slide to hit Mega Charizard Y, which can threaten to OHKO Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam. Corviknight is another great ally that threatens Sinistcha and Mega Floette, while Mega Tyranitar can deal heavy damage across the board to offset Rotom-Wash's passivity and appreciates Rotom-Wash's ability to threaten Basculegion-M. In return, Mega Tyranitar threatens Mega Charizard Y and Sinistcha, both of which boast Grass-type attacks that threaten Rotom-Wash. When building with Rotom-Wash and Mega Tyranitar, however, it is important to keep in mind that they share a weakness to Mega Floette. To counteract this, the aforementioned Steel-types, Excadrill and Corviknight, can be used to take down Mega Floette. How to Overcome Rotom-Wash's Weaknesses : Bringing safe switch-ins to attacks that target Rotom-Wash's weaknesses is recommended; Pokemon like Corviknight work well in this role. Offensive Pokemon like Excadrill and Garchomp work well alongside Rotom-Wash, combining Earthquake with Hydro Pump or Electric-type moves to deal solid damage. Playing Rotom-Wash as a supporting pivot is best, burning foes or providing Speed control and chip damage throughout the game.

movesets.name: Special Wall
movesets.description_plain: Tyranitar uses Sand Stream, excellent special bulk, and Stealth Rock to function as a special wall that can check attackers such as Mega Charizard Y , Mega Gengar , and Mega Delphox while making progress with item removal and chip damage. Stealth Rock : Stealth Rock helps punish common switch-ins and breaks Focus Sash, which is especially valuable against offensive Pokemon such as Sneasler , Meowscarada , and Ceruledge . It also pressures Pokemon weak to Rock, such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona . Knock Off versus Foul Play : Knock Off gives Tyranitar a consistent way to make progress by removing items from switch-ins such as Corviknight , Hippowdon , and Rotom-Wash . Foul Play is an alternative that punishes physical attackers and setup sweepers such as Dragonite , Mega Charizard X , and Garchomp without requiring much Attack investment. Rock Blast versus Rock Tomb : Rock Blast gives Tyranitar a multi-hit Rock-type attack that can break Substitute and pressure Dragonite through Multiscale while still threatening targets such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. Rock Tomb is a weaker alternative, but its Speed drop can punish switch-ins and allow Tyranitar or its teammates to more easily outspeed foes. Earthquake versus Ice Punch : Earthquake gives Tyranitar coverage for grounded Steel- and Rock-types such as Kingambit , Archaludon , and opposing Tyranitar, especially when catching them on the switch. Ice Punch instead targets Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon and Garchomp, which can otherwise take advantage of Tyranitar. Rest : Rest can be used over coverage to give Tyranitar more longevity. However, dropping Earthquake leaves Tyranitar unable to reliably pressure Kingambit and Archaludon, while dropping Ice Punch makes Garchomp and Hippowdon much safer switch-ins. Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry gives Tyranitar general recovery, helping it stay healthy enough to set Stealth Rock and continue checking special attackers throughout a game. Lum Berry : Lum Berry should be used with Rest, letting Tyranitar fully heal once without being forced to stay asleep afterward. Shuca Berry : Shuca Berry fits best on Ice Punch sets, letting Tyranitar survive physical Ground-type attacks from Pokemon such as Garchomp and punish them in return.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: Mega Tyranitar uses its excellent bulk, Sand Stream-boosted Special Defense, and Dragon Dance to turn forced switches and favorable trades into setup opportunities. This lets it set up or trade against special attackers it threatens, such as Mega Charizard Y , Mega Delphox , Mega Gengar , Volcarona , and even would-be checks like Primarina , which can be forced to respect a boosted Stone Edge. Knock Off : Knock Off is Mega Tyranitar's most consistent Dark-type STAB move, letting it heavily pressure Pokemon such as Aegislash , Mega Gengar, and Mega Delphox while removing items from defensive switch-ins like Corviknight , Hippowdon , and Primarina. Stone Edge : Stone Edge gives Mega Tyranitar a strong Rock-type STAB move to OHKO Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, Pelipper , Gyarados , and Dragonite with prior sand chip damage. Ice Punch versus Fire Punch : Ice Punch is preferred for hitting Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon and Garchomp , which can otherwise stomach Mega Tyranitar's STAB attacks. Fire Punch is an alternative for pressuring Steel-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor , and Kingambit more directly, though it leaves Mega Tyranitar worse off against common Ground-types. Jolly versus Adamant : A Jolly nature gives Mega Tyranitar better Speed after Dragon Dance, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Gengar, Meowscarada , and Sneasler after a boost. An Adamant nature gives Mega Tyranitar more immediate power while still letting it outspeed threats such as Garchomp, Mega Floette , and Gengar after a Dragon Dance. Other SP Spread 26 HP / 16 Atk / 1 SpD / 23 Spe with Adamant or Jolly : This bulkier spread lets Mega Tyranitar survive Meowscarada's Flower Trick, Corviknight's Body Press, and Garchomp's Earthquake, giving it more setup opportunities against these threats. Mega Tyranitar's Speed is kept high enough to outspeed uninvested Mega Venusaur and Mega Meganium before boosting. After a Dragon Dance, Adamant Mega Tyranitar still outspeeds positive-natured Garchomp, Mega Floette, and base 100s such as Mega Charizard X , Mega Charizard Y, and Volcarona. A Jolly nature can be used instead to outspeed Gengar and Mega Lucario after a Dragon Dance, though the lower Attack investment and nature make Mega Tyranitar noticeably weaker.
