movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Mega Tyranitar uses its excellent bulk, Sand Stream, and immediate power to pressure bulkier teams without needing Dragon Dance; it uses Knock Off and coverage to punish defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight , Skarmory , Hippowdon , and Mega Meganium . Rock Blast versus Stone Edge : Rock Blast trades raw power for better accuracy and multi-hit utility, letting Mega Tyranitar break Substitute and Focus Sash while pressuring Dragonite through Multiscale. Stone Edge maximizes Mega Tyranitar's immediate Rock-type damage, making it better for punishing neutral targets and bulky switch-ins. Ice Punch versus Fire Punch : Ice Punch hits Ground- and Dragon-types such as Hippowdon, Garchomp , and Hydreigon . Fire Punch is an alternative that pressures Steel-types such as Corviknight, Mega Scizor , Skarmory, and Kingambit more directly. Superpower : Superpower lets Mega Tyranitar hit Dark- and Steel-types such as Umbreon , Kingambit, opposing Tyranitar, and Archaludon . Other Options Taunt : Taunt can be used to stop defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon, Hippowdon, Skeledirge , and Corviknight from using Yawn, Will-O-Wisp, recovery, and phazing moves. Taunt pairs especially well with Superpower against Umbreon, since Superpower is Mega Tyranitar's strongest move against it but can be stalled out by Wish and Protect. However, fitting Taunt usually means dropping Ice Punch, Fire Punch, or a STAB move, making Mega Tyranitar easier for Ground-types, Steel-types, and Fairy-types to handle, respectively. Other SP Spread 32 HP / 20 Atk / 14 SpD with Adamant : This spread keeps Mega Tyranitar bulky while still letting it hit hard, as the extra Special Defense investment lets it almost always survive Timid Mega Gengar 's Focus Blast at full HP while sand is active. The drop in Attack is noticeable compared to maximum Attack variants, but the improved Mega Gengar matchup can justify the trade-off.

movesets.name: Sand Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Mega Tyranitar bolsters a team against opposing weather strategies while boasting good matchups against common Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Incineroar as well as Trick Room staples like Farigiraf and Torkoal . Low Kick versus Dragon Dance : Low Kick threatens Kingambit and opposing Mega Tyranitar. Low Kick Mega Tyranitar is a good Kingambit check, as it outspeeds Kingambit, resists Sucker Punch, and has great physical bulk. Dropping Low Kick for Dragon Dance turns Mega Tyranitar into a game-ending threat when given support in the form of redirection from Sinistcha and damage mitigation from Rotom-Wash and Incineroar. Dragon Dance also enables Mega Tyranitar to go for Rock Slide flinches against a greater number of Pokemon. However, the rest of the team must have a better matchup against Kingambit without Tyranitar's Low Kick. Mega Evolving Tyranitar : Tyranitar should look to Mega Evolve when it knows that it can win the weather war. If it leads against a Froslass holding Froslassite or Charizard holding Charizardite Y, then it should try to Mega Evolve either on the same turn as them or a turn after them. This ensures that sand will be up and these Pokemon cannot benefit from the weather they set. The state of the weather when leading against Pelipper is a bit tricky; fast Tyranitar sets will always concede the early weather advantage, and slow, bulky Pelipper sets will always seize weather control. Tyranitar can Mega Evolve to re-establish weather should rain win out after the lead. SP Spreads 32 HP / 13 Atk / 4 Def / 17 Spe with Adamant : 17 Speed SPs allow Mega Tyranitar to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M under Tailwind. The physical bulk ensures that Mega Tyranitar always survives Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. This bulky spread is best used with Low Kick. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly : Maximizing Speed and power lets Mega Tyranitar make the most of the boosts granted by Dragon Dance. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Fighting-types like Sneasler and Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon directly threaten Mega Tyranitar; it struggles to effectively hit these Pokemon, especially Sneasler. Mega Tyranitar is also not particularly fast, so many attackers get the chance to attack it before it can respond. This includes threats like Garchomp , which is also unthreatened by Mega Tyranitar's attacks, even surviving Knock Off from Mega Tyranitar at +1 Attack. While Mega Tyranitar is excellent at disrupting rain, Pokemon on rain teams like Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten it with their STAB attacks. Finally, Chople Berry variants of Kingambit can turn the tables on Mega Tyranitar by surviving Low Kick and OHKOing it in return with Iron Head. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Tyranitar benefits from having Ghost- and Steel-types that can check the Fighting- and Fairy-types it is afraid of. One of its best partners is Sinistcha, which can redirect away Fighting- and Water-type attacks and set Trick Room to let Mega Tyranitar outspeed Pokemon it otherwise could not, such as Archaludon. Corviknight is strong against Fairy- and Fighting-types, packs Speed control in the form of Tailwind, and resists Garchomp's STAB moves. Pokemon like Rotom-Wash, Hydreigon , and the aforementioned Sinistcha that threaten common Pokemon on rain teams ensure that Mega Tyranitar does not entirely rely on winning the weather war. Similarly, Pokemon that can back up Mega Tyranitar in the fight against Mega Charizard Y 's sun, like Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Incineroar, ensure that it isn't alone in attempting to hold off dangerous sun threats. Mega Tyranitar's sand also enables Sand Rush Excadrill , a fast cleaner that beats Mega Tyranitar checks like Sneasler and Mega Floette. How to Overcome Mega Tyranitar's Weaknesses : Mega Tyranitar has a middling Speed tier, meaning that it is slower than many Pokemon. Speed control in the form of Sinistcha's Trick Room or Corviknight's Tailwind lets Mega Tyranitar threaten a greater number of Pokemon. Sinistcha's redirection also allows Mega Tyranitar to bypass otherwise super effective attacks. Steel-types like Corviknight and Excadrill threaten Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon that threaten Mega Tyranitar.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description_plain: Meowscarada's ability Protean and good base Speed combined with Choice Scarf make it an extremely versatile solution to many speedy threats such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M , Mega Gyarados after a Dragon Dance, and Mega Lopunny . Flower Trick : Because it always lands a critical hit, Meowscarada's signature move is a very consistent source of damage against Intimidate Gyarados and Shell Smash Blastoise behind dual screens. It notably 2HKOes Hippowdon and Garchomp and OHKOes Basculegion-M and Primarina . Triple Axel : Triple Axel covers targets that resist Grass- and Dark-type moves, OHKOing foes such as Multiscale Dragonite , Focus Sash Garchomp, Starapator, and Hydreigon . Triple Axel can also 2HKO both Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y , making it very difficult for them to switch in and forcing Mega Charizard X to refrain from using Dragon Dance, as it still won't outspeed Meowscarada after one boost. Knock Off : Knock Off allows Meowscarada to remove Leftovers and do decent damage to Aegislash . It can be used to remove Leftovers and Sitrus Berry from Archaludon and Leftovers from Corviknight as they switch in. It will also 2HKO Mega Evolutions such as Mega Delphox , Mega Starmie , and Mega Gengar . Thunder Punch : Thunder Punch is useful against Mega Charizard Y, providing more consistent damage compared to Triple Axel. It can also be used to finish off a weakened Corviknight. U-turn : U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's checks and hard counters, such as Blaziken , Kingambit , Corviknight, Mega Scizor , Archaludon, and Mega Venusaur . It will also OHKO opposing Choice Scarf Meowscarada, leading to a coin flip for momentum. Jolly versus Adamant : A Jolly nature provides some niche benefits, as it is what allows Meowscarada to outspeed Timid Choice Scarf Greninja , but the main reason is to compete with opposing Meowscarada. As Meowscarada's Speed is already high with Choice Scarf, an Adamant nature allows it to more consistently OHKO Mega Gyarados with Flower Trick as well as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar with Knock Off. Other Options Throat Chop : Throat Chop can be used as a substitute for Knock Off. It does more consistent damage against Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, since Mega Stones can't be removed. It also stops Skeledirge from using Torch Song. Low Kick : Low Kick can be useful against Archaludon and Kingambit.

  • Flower Trick: Because it always lands a critical hit, Meowscarada's signature move is a very consistent source of damage against Intimidate Gyarados and Shell Smash Blastoise behind dual screens. It notably 2HKOes Hippowdon and Garchomp and OHKOes Basculegion-M and Primarina.

  • U-turn: U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's checks and hard counters, such as Blaziken, Kingambit, Corviknight, Mega Scizor, Archaludon, and Mega Venusaur. It will also OHKO opposing Choice Scarf Meowscarada, leading to a coin flip for momentum.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature provides some niche benefits, as it is what allows Meowscarada to outspeed Timid Choice Scarf Greninja, but the main reason is to compete with opposing Meowscarada. Other Options

  • Throat Chop: Throat Chop can be used as a substitute for Knock Off. It does more consistent damage against Mega Gengar and Mega Delphox, since Mega Stones can't be removed. It also stops Skeledirge from using Torch Song.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick can be useful against Archaludon and Kingambit.

movesets.name: Focus Sash
movesets.description_plain: Focus Sash Meowscarada is useful thanks to its ability to 2HKO many foes and strike first with Sucker Punch. Focus Sash Meowscarada can take on Pokemon such as Glimmora , Mega Delphox , Mega Gyarados , Mega Greninja , and Mega Gengar one-on-one. Flower Trick : Flower Trick is very helpful against Water- and Ground-type Pokemon, providing consistent damage against Gyarados , Primarina , and Hippowdon . Sucker Punch : Sucker Punch gives Meowscarada an edge in finishing off faster Pokemon such as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar. It also provides good damage against Choice Scarf Basculegion-M , and a strong chance to 2HKO offensive Mega Metagross Triple Axel versus Knock Off : Triple Axel is great for beating Garchomp and Multiscale Dragonite , as well as hitting neutral targets such as Sneasler and both of Charizard 's Mega Evolutions. Knock Off is a strong Dark-type move that doesn't count on Meowscarada's foe attacking first while also removing an item. It is particularly helpful against Ceruledge and Aegislash , as they will not always attack when Meowscarada uses Sucker Punch. U-turn : U-turn maintains momentum against Meowscarada's hard counters, such as Archaludon or Corviknight . Taunt : Taunt can avoid messy situations where your opponent's Pokemon tries to set up on Meowscarada, letting it stop Hippowdon and Mega Scizor from using Stealth Rock and Swords Dance, respectively. Jolly versus Adamant : A Jolly nature is heavily preferred for outspeeding Jolly Mega Metagross, a threat Meowscarada has the potential to surprise one-on-one. Other Options Toxic Spikes : Toxic Spikes can be strong in longer drawn-out games. This does little to alleviate Meowscarada's poor matchup against Steel-types, though. Overgrow : Overgrow has good synergy with Focus Sash for boosting Flower Trick. Low Kick : Low Kick is an option against Archaludon and Kingambit .

  • Flower Trick: Flower Trick is very helpful against Water- and Ground-type Pokemon, providing consistent damage against Gyarados, Primarina, and Hippowdon.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch gives Meowscarada an edge in finishing off faster Pokemon such as Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar. It also provides good damage against Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and a strong chance to 2HKO offensive Mega Metagross

  • Triple Axel versus Knock Off: Triple Axel is great for beating Garchomp and Multiscale Dragonite, as well as hitting neutral targets such as Sneasler and both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions. movesets.name: IronPress
movesets.description_plain: Iron Defense Corviknight is an excellent defensive Pokemon and wincon. It can boost alongside setup sweepers such as Kingambit , Dragonite , and Garchomp , allowing it to continue checking them while threatening significant damage with Body Press. Corviknight's fantastic typing, resilience to entry hazards, and key resistances grant it many opportunities to set up throughout a game. Corviknight can extend its utility with Defog, given its great matchup against foes like defensive Garchomp and Hippowdon , thanks in part to Pressure. Alternatively, Corviknight can run Brave Bird to hit threats that would otherwise check it, such as Volcarona , Mega Meganium , and Mega Delphox , as well as Ghost-types like Annihilape and Ceruledge , preventing them from switching in. Leftovers is Corviknight's preferred item, with the passive healing over time being crucial for checking hazard setters and limiting how often it needs to use Roost. Sitrus Berry is also a good option if another teammate is already using Leftovers, and has the added benefit of allowing Corviknight to avoid Poltergeist from Pokemon such as Aegislash after it is consumed. Occa Berry allows Corviknight to survive an otherwise lethal Fire-type attack from Pokemon such as Blaziken , Mega Meganium, and Volcarona. Occa Berry pairs especially well with Brave Bird, as Corviknight can lure in Blaziken, Mega Meganium, and Volcarona and potentially KO them in return. 16 Speed SPs can be used to allow Corviknight to outrun maximum Speed Adamant Kingambit and use Iron Defense before Kingambit attacks. However, this requires Corviknight to sacrifice a notable amount of physical bulk, and it already outspeeds bulkier Kingambit variants without the investment. Mental Herb is another option, allowing Corviknight to avoid being locked into a move by Encore from users such as Maushold and Hisuian Samurott . However, because Encore is uncommon, other items are typically more effective. Corviknight can fit on a wide variety of teams thanks to its ability to clear entry hazards and check a number of dangerous Pokemon such as Garchomp, Sneasler , and Kingambit, though it will find particular success on balance and bulky offense teams. Corviknight benefits greatly from entry hazard support because many of its answers, such as Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and Mega Raichu Y , lack reliable recovery or are weak to Stealth Rock. Bulky entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Hippowdon are thus great partners, as they can set up Stealth Rock to wear down Corviknight's key checks while also handling certain Fire-types such as Blaziken and Ceruledge and switching into Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Corviknight also fits well on hazard-centric teams because Pressure punishes Defog from opposing Corviknight, and Corviknight itself is a great counter to Rapid Spin Excadrill . Key Regenerator Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking , Mega Dragalge , and Toxapex greatly appreciate Corviknight's ability to handle physical attackers such as Kingambit and Garchomp as well as remove entry hazards with Defog. In turn, they can handle special attackers that threaten Corviknight, such as Mega Meganium, Mega Charizard Y , Primarina , and Mega Raichu Y. With or without Brave Bird, Corviknight can find itself struggling against Ghost-types such as Annihilape, Ceruledge, Dragapult , and Aegislash. Hisuian Samurott is a fantastic partner, as it can switch into many of these Ghost-types as well as Fire-type attacks aimed at Corviknight and capitalize on this to begin setting up entry hazards with Ceaseless Edge. It can also revenge kill key threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y either with a Choice Scarf set or by using Sucker Punch. Hydreigon can similarly switch into many of these Pokemon and revenge kill them with Dark Pulse on a Choice Scarf set. However, both Pokemon struggle against Annihilape, so another partner to handle it, such as Clefable or Mega Meganium, is recommended.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive
movesets.description_plain: Corviknight serves as an excellent physical wall, with its incredible typing enabling it to handle physical attackers and Ground-types such as Tyranitar , Garchomp , and Hippowdon with ease. Body Press : Body Press is the main offensive option, weaponizing Corviknight's good natural bulk to dispose of threats such as Meowscarada , Excadrill , and Umbreon safely. Iron Head : If a secondary offensive option is needed, Iron Head allows Corviknight to actually threaten Mimikyu and Sylveon along with Primarina and Mega Floette in a pinch. Iron Defense : Iron Defense improves Corviknight's Defense and Body Press's damage, enabling it to shrug off physical attackers like Dragonite and Sneasler completely. Taunt : Taunt allows Corviknight to shut down Umbreon and Hippowdon, preventing them from forcing Corviknight out with tools such as Yawn, and prevents multiple turns of setup from the likes of Dragon Dance Dragonite. Items Leftovers : Leftovers allows Corviknight to safely stay on the field for multiple turns while it accrues Iron Defense boosts. Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry can provide a solid quick burst of healing, enabling Corviknight to have HP to spare while combating foes such as Tyranitar and Mega Gyarados . Abilities Pressure : Pressure punishes Pokemon reliant on low-PP moves like Garchomp, which needs Stone Edge to reliably damage Corviknight, by quickly draining their moves' PP; Pressure also helps Corviknight handle opposing Corviknight by letting it outlast their Body Press's PP. Mirror Armor : Mirror Armor punishes Intimidate from Gyarados , forcing it to set up with Dragon Dance longer, along with Special Defense drops from the likes of Espathra 's Lumina Crash and Gengar 's Shadow Ball, which can help force them out as Corviknight pivots to a special attacker.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description_plain: With a specially defensive SP spread, Corviknight can still maintain its role of checking Ground-types like Hippowdon as with the a physically defensive spread while also expanding its reaches and allowing it to directly take on special attackers such as Mega Meganium and Gengar . Body Press and Iron Defense : Body Press and Iron Defense can allow Corviknight to still check more physically leaning threats such as Mega Lopunny once it gets going while also making it capable of directly combating Archaludon that lack Electro Shot. Brave Bird : Brave Bird is an alternative offensive tool for Corviknight to bust up Mega Venusaur and Primarina . Taunt : Taunt shuts down Hippowdon and Sylveon 's attempts to force it out with Yawn and prevents Corviknight from being safely set up on by the likes of Hydreigon . Items Leftovers : Leftovers can soften the blow of the recoil from Brave Bird. Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry's burst healing helps Corviknight take on Mega Meganium and quickly recover from an untimely bit of Brave Bird recoil. Abilities Pressure : Pressure helps Corviknight handle Primarina by depleting its Sparkling Aria PP more quickly as well as allowing it to quickly expend Garchomp 's Stone Edge PP. Mirror Armor : Mirror Armor annoys Gyarados by turning Intimidate against it, along with bouncing Special Defense drops back against the likes of Lumina Crash Espathra and Shadow Ball Gengar as Corviknight pivots to a special attacker.

Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y , Mega Delphox , and Ceruledge all hit Corviknight hard with Heat Wave and Bitter Blade. Without boosts or after only one Bulk Up, double targeting from strong physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Sneasler can bring Corviknight to low HP, making it much harder to reliably use Bulk Up. Archaludon and Rotom-Wash threaten high Electric-type damage and can easily tank Corviknight's Brave Bird. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Tyranitar is able to thwart the plans of any Fire-type Pokemon, shutting off sun from Mega Charizard Y and hitting them hard with Rock Slide while resisting their Fire-type attacks. Mega Tyranitar also shuts off rain, making Archaludon far more manageable. In return, Corviknight beats Garchomp and Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette that would otherwise give Mega Tyranitar big trouble. Rotom-Wash also helps against Fire-types and has Electric-type STAB moves to threaten the likes of Basculegion-M and Mega Blastoise. Furthermore, since Rotom-Wash carries Will-O-Wisp to prevent physical attackers from overwhelming it, Corviknight becomes near-impossible to remove with physical blows after a Bulk Up or two. In return, Rotom-Wash appreciates Corviknight's ability to threaten common Fairy-type Pokemon, as they are able to tank attacks from Rotom-Wash and target its typically lower Special Defense with their strong STAB moves. Mega Froslass shuts down other weather and helps against Mega Dragonite, being commonly run alongside Corviknight thanks to its good matchups against Mega Aerodactyl and, after boosting and when using Body Press, Kingambit. Excadrill and Garchomp are good partners for Corviknight, with the former also pairing well with Mega Tyranitar and both carrying Earthquake and Rock Slide to threaten Fire-types. They're also able to offset Corviknight's passive nature before it can set up. Corviknight, thanks to its Earthquake immunity, can sit next to them while they use Earthquake. How to Overcome Corviknight's Weaknesses : Teams with Corviknight should always have ways to beat sun and rain teams; Mega Tyranitar and Mega Froslass are able to do this well by changing the weather. Meanwhile, offensive partners like Excadrill and Garchomp help make dents into teams early-game, removing threats to Corviknight like Mega Charizard Y, which allows it to set up more easily and bring you closer to a good win condition. Sinistcha can provide redirection and recovery in the form of Rage Powder and Hospitality, creating bigger opportunities for Corviknight to set up and get rolling.

movesets.name: Offensive Utility
movesets.description_plain: With excellent natural bulk and a stellar typing combination, Primarina is a premier balance attacker that can provide both excellent offensive trading and strong support options. Aqua Jet : While somewhat weak on Primarina, Aqua Jet is still an excellent move for picking off weakened foes and finishing off Focus Sash users like Garchomp . Flip Turn versus Encore : Flip Turn lets Primarina function as a bulky pivot against faster threats, while Encore lets Primarina disrupt slower, bulkier threats like Hippowdon . Modest versus Quiet : Even if it does weaken Aqua Jet, Modest is the no-nonsense option especially if Primarina is running Encore. On the other hand, Quiet can be run to preserve Aqua Jet's power while also making Primarina a slower pivot with Flip Turn. Other Options Ice Beam : Despite Moonblast already hitting Dragon-types very hard, Ice Beam can be used to catch bulkier Garchomp sets that survive Moonblast by surprise. It’s also a good tool to pressure Mega Meganium on a predicted switch, as Modest Primarina's Ice Beam can 2HKO maximum HP builds. Psychic Noise : Psychic Noise is Primarina's only hope of taking on Mega Venusaur , dealing respectable damage and temporarily stopping any Synthesis or Leech Seed healing. Items Sitrus Berry : Sitrus Berry is the most reliable source of recovery for attacking sets. Mystic Water : Mystic Water is an alternative to healing items that synergizes better with Torrent, allowing Primarina's Sparkling Aria to hit extra hard once it's at low health. Leftovers : If Sitrus Berry is needed elsewhere on the team, Leftovers is a decent alternative for healing. Focus Sash : Focus Sash can be used with fully offensive spreads, allowing Primarina to activate Torrent more easily against targets such as Mega Gengar . Other SP Spreads 32 HP / 2 SpA / 32 SpD with Calm or Sassy : With this spread, Primarina can lean harder into being a special cushion for its team. In particular, it almost always avoids the 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite 's Thunderbolt. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest : A fully offensive spread should always be used for Focus Sash sets. It also greatly increases Primarina's ability to disrupt with Encore.
movesets.description_html:
• With excellent natural bulk and a stellar typing combination, Primarina is a premier balance attacker that can provide both excellent offensive trading and strong support options.

  • Aqua Jet: While somewhat weak on Primarina, Aqua Jet is still an excellent move for picking off weakened foes and finishing off Focus Sash users like Garchomp.

  • Flip Turn versus Encore: Flip Turn lets Primarina function as a bulky pivot against faster threats, while Encore lets Primarina disrupt slower, bulkier threats like Hippowdon.

  • Modest versus Quiet: Even if it does weaken Aqua Jet, Modest is the no-nonsense option especially if Primarina is running Encore. On the other hand, Quiet can be run to preserve Aqua Jet's power while also making Primarina a slower pivot with Flip Turn.

Other Options

  • Ice Beam: Despite Moonblast already hitting Dragon-types very hard, Ice Beam can be used to catch bulkier Garchomp sets that survive Moonblast by surprise. It’s also a good tool to pressure Mega Meganium on a predicted switch, as Modest Primarina's Ice Beam can 2HKO maximum HP builds.

  • Psychic Noise: Psychic Noise is Primarina's only hope of taking on Mega Venusaur, dealing respectable damage and temporarily stopping any Synthesis or Leech Seed healing.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is the most reliable source of recovery for attacking sets.

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water is an alternative to healing items that synergizes better with Torrent, allowing Primarina's Sparkling Aria to hit extra hard once it's at low health.

  • Leftovers: If Sitrus Berry is needed elsewhere on the team, Leftovers is a decent alternative for healing.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash can be used with fully offensive spreads, allowing Primarina to activate Torrent more easily against targets such as Mega Gengar.

Other SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 2 SpA / 32 SpD with Calm or Sassy: With this spread, Primarina can lean harder into being a special cushion for its team. In particular, it almost always avoids the 2HKO from Modest Mega Dragonite's Thunderbolt.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: A fully offensive spread should always be used for Focus Sash sets. It also greatly increases Primarina's ability to disrupt with Encore.

movesets.name: Screens Support
movesets.description_plain: Sableye aims to support its allies while disrupting foes, using dual screens to allow its allies to survive attacks they couldn't otherwise and boasting a great type matchup against Sneasler . Rain Dance : Rain Dance is used to shut down weather set by the likes of Mega Charizard Y , Mega Froslass , and Mega Tyranitar , allowing allies like Archaludon and Basculegion-M to thrive. It also allows for mix-ups, removing the need to bring Pelipper or Politoed to every game to set rain. Encore versus Foul Play : Encore provides more disruptive tools for Sableye, punishing foes for playing passively with Protect or locking foes into setup moves. Foul Play, on the other hand, grants Sableye a damaging option so it doesn't get fully shut down by Taunt; Foul Play can OHKO Adamant Basculegion-M. Other Options Disable : Disable is usable on sets that forgo dual screens and opt to run Sableye as disruptive support, forcing foes to use Struggle when paired with Encore. This does, however, come at the cost of Sableye becoming more of a sitting duck, as it now cannot help its allies defensively. Fake Out : Fake Out is great on Sableye, as, thanks to its Ghost typing, it doesn't have to compete in Speed wars with other Fake Out users. However, this comes at the cost of either Reflect, Light Screen, or the last slot and forces Sableye to switch in and out for Fake Out to be useful. Quash : Quash grants Sableye speed control, allowing slower allies like Archaludon to OHKO faster foes like Garchomp with Draco Meteor. It is typically used over the last slot to allow Sableye and Archaludon to become a devastating combination. Will-O-Wisp : Will-O-Wisp allows Sableye to cripple physical attackers, notably Pokemon like Sneasler and Garchomp. However, it does not work on key threats like Kingambit , Mega Tyranitar, or Ceruledge . Items Roseli Berry : Roseli Berry allows Sableye to survive Fairy-type attacks that would otherwise threaten to OHKO it, including Hyper Voice from Sylveon as well as Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette . Abilities Prankster : Prankster allows Sableye to use Reflect or Light Screen before opposing Pokemon move and to change the weather with Rain Dance before opposing weather Pokemon, such as Mega Charizard Y, can attack. Because Rain Dance is used after opposing Pokemon Mega Evolve, unlike Drizzle from Pelipper and Politoed, Sableye can easily flip weather against Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Mega Charizard Y. SP Spreads 32 HP / 17 Def / 17 SpD with Careful : The given SP spread allows Sableye to survive Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette with Roseli Berry and almost always survive Wave Crash from Jolly non-Mystic Water Basculegion-M. Additionally, it survives attacks such as Kowtow Cleave from +1 non-Black Glasses Kingambit and Bitter Blade from +1 Ceruledge. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Sableye is easily countered by many Dark-types in the format, namely Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Incineroar , as they are immune to Sableye's Prankster moves, resist Foul Play, and can retaliate with Knock Off, Kowtow Cleave, or Flare Blitz, respectively. Strong enough Fairy-type attacks, like a boosted Moonblast from Mega Floette, Light of Ruin from Mega Floette, or Hyper Beam from Sylveon, still threaten to OHKO Sableye despite Roseli Berry. Additionally, Sableye tends to struggle to provide enough offensive pressure, as it is totally reliant on its partners to deal all of the damage. Good Partners and Synergies : Mega Venusaur greatly appreciates Sableye's capability to bolster its bulk further with dual screens and shut off sun to prevent Mega Charizard Y from becoming too threatening. In return, Mega Venusaur threatens the many Fairy-types that Sableye fears. Archaludon similarly appreciates the dual screens and rain provided by Sableye and can threaten Fairy-types while also breaking through Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar; boosted Electro Shot can help blast through Kingambit. Basculegion-M also loves rain while dealing formidable damage that can mitigate Sableye's passivity. Additionally, Reflect from Sableye allows Basculegion-M to survive Sucker Punch from Kingambit. How to Overcome Sableye's Weaknesses : Sableye prefers to be next to a Pokemon that dishes out large amounts of damage at all times; otherwise, the board state will be too passive and will likely leave its team on the back foot. Archaludon, Basculegion-M, and Mega Scizor all excel at this role. Sableye also needs help handling Fairy-type Pokemon, so partners like the aforementioned Mega Venusaur serve it well.

movesets.name: Sweeper
movesets.description_plain: With Intimidate, Gyarados is able to set up, Mega Evolve, and sweep even under the pressure of physically offensive threats! Waterfall : Even after a Dragon Dance, Mega Gyarados has just over a 50% chance to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Waterfall under the sun! Earthquake : An unboosted Earthquake is a reliable option for knocking out Mega Gengar with no HP investment and Mega Mawile . Earthquake also lets Mega Gyarados deal significant damage to Kingambit , Archaludon , and Mega Dragalage. Mega Gyarados is even capable of surviving Kingambit's STAB moves with two Supreme Overlord boosts! And thanks to Mold Breaker, it can also hit Levitate users such as Rotom-Wash , Rotom-Heat , and Mega Delphox . Ice Fang : Ice Fang is extremely effective on Dragonite and Garchomp . It also covers Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur , Mega Meganium , and Meowscarada , which would otherwise be problematic for Mega Gyarados. Crunch : Crunch can be used over Earthquake for landing a OHKO on Mega Gengar variants with maximum HP investment while covering Pokemon like Aegislash , the Basculegion-M , Mega Starmie , and Dragapult . After a Dragon Dance, Mega Gyarados manages to land a surprising OHKO on Shield forme Aegislash as long as it has no Defense investment! Keep in mind Crunch is a contact move, making Mega Gyarados susceptible to the Attack-lowering effect of King's Shield. Power Whip : This is a situational and high-risk, high-reward option for Mega Gyarados to land an OHKO on opposing Mega Gyarados and Mega Swampert , as well as the bulkiest of Primarina and Rotom-Wash after a Dragon Dance. Taunt : At the cost of dropping a coverage move, Taunt prevents defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon and Toxapex from healing themselves and disrupting Gyarados with Yawn and Haze, respectively. It also renders Corviknight incapable of using Iron Defense and Roost. Mega Evolving Gyarados : It is recommended to wait until the right moment to Mega Evolve. This allows Gyarados to come into specific situations to create win conditions for itself. It's also important to note that non-Mega Gyarados and Mega Gyarados share the same Speed stat but have different typing and abilities; therefore, abstaining from Mega Evolving right away can be quite beneficial depending on the situation in question. Before Mega Evolution : For example, Gyarados can switch in on a Choice-locked Earthquake from Garchomp in order to safely set up with Dragon Dance. It can also prevent Corviknight from using Iron Defense with Taunt while resisting Body Press and setting up additional Dragon Dances for a potential sweep. Finally, Gyarados's typing ensures that it won't be OHKOed by Mega Mawile's Play Rough. After Mega Evolution : Mega Gyarados's Dark typing helps it resist Foul Play from Umbreon, Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Archaludon, as well as Sucker Pucnh from targets like Mega Mawile and Kingambit. Mold Breaker also ignores various problematic abilities that can ruin its offensive momentum. Examples include Disguise from Mimikyu , Unaware from Skeledirge , and Levitate from Rotom-Wash and Rotom-Heat, with the last two being huge threats to Gyarados. Abilities Intimidate : This is the preferred option for cycling and safely setting up on physically offensive threats. Moxie : Revenge killing a weakened and slower Pokemon with Moxie is an alternative for gaining an Attack boost before Mega Evolving. SP Spreads 1 HP / 32 Atk / 1 Def / 32 Spe with Jolly : This simple spread not only minimizes Stealth Rock damage but also lets Gyarados outspeed base 80 Speed Pokemon such as Mamoswine and non-Mega Dragonite. It also outspeeds Jolly or Timid Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a Dragon Dance, and Swift Swim Mega Swampert after two uses of Dragon Dance.

  • Taunt: At the cost of dropping a coverage move, Taunt prevents defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon and Toxapex from healing themselves and disrupting Gyarados with Yawn and Haze, respectively. It also renders Corviknight incapable of using Iron Defense and Roost.

  • Mega Evolving Gyarados: It is recommended to wait until the right moment to Mega Evolve. This allows Gyarados to come into specific situations to create win conditions for itself. It's also important to note that non-Mega Gyarados and Mega Gyarados share the same Speed stat but have different typing and abilities; therefore, abstaining from Mega Evolving right away can be quite beneficial depending on the situation in question.

  • Before Mega Evolution: For example, Gyarados can switch in on a Choice-locked Earthquake from Garchomp in order to safely set up with Dragon Dance. It can also prevent Corviknight from using Iron Defense with Taunt while resisting Body Press and setting up additional Dragon Dances for a potential sweep. Finally, Gyarados's typing ensures that it won't be OHKOed by Mega Mawile's Play Rough.

  • After Mega Evolution: Mega Gyarados's Dark typing helps it resist Foul Play from Umbreon, Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Archaludon, as well as Sucker Pucnh from targets like Mega Mawile and Kingambit. Mold Breaker also ignores various problematic abilities that can ruin its offensive momentum. Examples include Disguise from Mimikyu, Unaware from Skeledirge, and Levitate from Rotom-Wash and Rotom-Heat, with the last two being huge threats to Gyarados.

Abilities

  • Intimidate: This is the preferred option for cycling and safely setting up on physically offensive threats.

  • Moxie: Revenge killing a weakened and slower Pokemon with Moxie is an alternative for gaining an Attack boost before Mega Evolving.

SP Spreads

  • 1 HP / 32 Atk / 1 Def / 32 Spe with Jolly: This simple spread not only minimizes Stealth Rock damage but also lets Gyarados outspeed base 80 Speed Pokemon such as Mamoswine and non-Mega Dragonite. It also outspeeds Jolly or Timid Choice Scarf Basculegion-M after a Dragon Dance, and Swift Swim Mega Swampert after two uses of Dragon Dance.

movesets.name: Offensive Pivot
movesets.description_plain: With a Choice Scarf, Rotom-Heat becomes a speedy pivot and disruptor. Levitate also lets Rotom-Heat switch in on Pokemon that often use Ground-type attacks such as Choice-locked Garchomp , Mega Metagross , and Mega Venusaur , and revenge kill them if they're weakened enough. Thunderbolt versus Discharge : Thunderbolt is preferred for higher damage. Discharge can be used instead for the higher chance of paralysis. Volt Switch : This turns Rotom-Heat into an offensive pivot, allowing it to leave matchups where it can't do much damage and safely bring another teammate in the process. Overheat : This is the best and only option for Rotom-Heat to threaten Meowscarada and Scizor . If Rotom-Heat is using a Modest nature, Overheat has a very high chance to OHKO Mega Meganium with maximum HP investment and also deals massive damage to specially defensive Corviknight , but it narrowly misses a chance to land the OHKO even with Stealth Rock damage. In the event Mega Meganium and Corviknight survive, they can use their recovery moves to offset the damage they receive as Rotom-Heat's Special Attack decreases with every use of Overheat, so this should only be used to pick up the KO if they're weakened enough. Trick : Even though Choice Scarf is a highly coveted item for speed control, Trick can be used to lock a defensive Pokemon into a move and make it virtually useless for the rest of the battle. Modest versus Timid : On one hand, a Modest nature allows Rotom-Heat's Thunderbolt to have a very low chance to OHKO Mega Charizard Y , as well as 2HKOing specially defensive Corviknight after Leftovers recovery. On the other hand, a Timid nature can be used for outspeeding Jolly Gyarados that has used Dragon Dance.

movesets.name: Physical Attacker
movesets.description_plain: With its incredible stats, boasting sets of some of the highest offensive and defensive stats of any non-Mega Evolved Pokemon in the format; access to a powerful STAB attack with little drawback in Poltergeist; and its amazing typing, Aegislash is a potent physical wallbreaker that few Pokemon can switch in on without taking serious damage. Shadow Sneak also gives it the option to act as a revenge killer, allowing it to clean up weakened teams and remain useful late-game. Swords Dance : With a Swords Dance boost, Aegislash is able to tear through even defensive teams, and thanks to Shield forme's stellar defenses, it can often find opportunities to set up, especially against common Pokemon like Corviknight , Archaludon , Mega Floette , and Sneasler . At +2, Poltergeist OHKOes bulky Primarina and Rotom-W sets, and Shadow Sneak OHKOes the likes of Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar . King's Shield : At the cost of some offensive power, King's Shield provides Aegislash with much greater longevity, particularly when combined with Leftovers. By using King's Shield to first lower their Attack, Aegislash can take hits from and subsequently OHKO physically attacking counters that commonly run all-out attacking sets like Mega Lopunny and Meowscarada , making it much more difficult for offensive teams to reliably deal with. Close Combat versus Sacred Sword : Aegislash appreciates Fighting-type coverage, which lets it hit Dark- and Normal-type Pokemon for super effective damage. Sets lacking King's Shield typically prefer the additional damage that Close Combat provides, which gives Aegislash the ability to always OHKO Mega Lucario as well as Mega Lopunny and Hydreigon on the switch in. Such sets don't care about Close Combat's drawback thanks to Blade forme's already low defensive stats. With this said, Swords Dance sets can still benefit from Sacred Sword ignoring stat boosts, which prevents Iron Defense Corviknight from using Aegislash to set up. Other Options Brave Nature : King's Shield variants of Aegislash can run a Brave nature, allowing them to always be slower than neutral-nature Primarina and therefore always be in the more defensive Shield forme when taking damage from its attacks. This comes at the cost of a worse matchup against opposing Adamant Aegislash, however, as the one-on-one is often decided by which Pokemon hits Poltergeist first. Iron Head : Iron Head provides a STAB attack that, unlike Poltergeist, doesn't rely on the opposing Pokemon holding an item. This allows Aegislash to deal consistent damage throughout the game if it's paired with a Knock Off user like Meowscarada, as well as against common Sitrus Berry users like Hippowdon . Iron Head's lower Base Power can hinder Aegislash's ability to sweep, however. Items Spell Tag : Spell Tag makes Aegislash's Ghost-type STAB attacks even more potent, making Poltergeist a guaranteed OHKO on Primarina after Stealth Rock damage and giving it a chance to OHKO physically defensive Corviknight after a Swords Dance. Leftovers : Leftovers is generally preferred on King's Shield variants, which greatly appreciate passively healing while they protect themselves. However, Leftovers can still be useful on Swords Dance sets thanks to the pressure Aegislash's massive damage output puts on the opponent to make defensive switches, which often buys it free turns to heal. Focus Sash : Swords Dance sets can make use of Focus Sash to set up on would-be threats like Mega Gengar and threaten a sweep against frail teams with a boosted Shadow Sneak.

movesets.name: Mixed Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Aegislash is a popular threat in BSS thanks to its good defensive typing and priority. This set trades damage for coverage and better offensive versatility against physical walls. Shadow Ball : With Shadow Ball and Special Attack investment, Aegislash fares better against Corviknight and Archaludon due to their low Special Defense. Since Corviknight is prone to using U-turn, Aegislash's Quiet nature allows it to hit the incoming Pokemon instead. Aegislash also heavily threatens Iron Defense Mega Metagross by running Shadow Ball instead of Poltergeist. Shadow Sneak : Aegislash's high offensive stats in Blade Forme mean that Shadow Sneak still has wide utility for revenge killing or dealing damage to faster foes like Basculegion-M , Mega Delphox , Mega Gengar , and Focus Sash Greninja . King's Shield : King's Shield is useful against physical attackers like Meowscarada , Mega Lopunny , and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott . Lowering a foe's Attack allows Aegislash to win many one-on-one scenarios it otherwise wouldn't. However, Contrary users like Mega Staraptor can gain an Attack boost from King's Shield when using Blaze Kick. Close Combat : Close Combat still deals heavy damage to Mega Lucario , Mega Lopunny, Mega Greninja , and Meowscarada. The lack of full Attack investment does mean that Aegislash won't consistently OHKO the first two without chip damage, so having an entry hazard setter is generally recommended with this set. Other Options Flash Cannon versus Iron Head : Flash Cannon provides an additional STAB option against Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and makes use of Aegislash's investment in Special Attack. It does well against Mega Floette , though Iron Head deals more damage even without Attack investment and has a chance to KO offensive variants. Flash Cannon also deals the most damage against Mega Scrafty and Mega Staraptor. Sacred Sword : Sacred Sword does well against Archaludon and provides coverage without the cost of lowering Aegislash's defensive stats. Items Spell Tag : Spell Tag provides a blanket boost to Ghost-type attacks, allowing Shadow Ball to consistently 2HKO uninvested Archaludon and Corviknight and OHKO Mega Metagross. Leftovers : Leftovers has good synergy with King's Shield, allowing Aegislash to recover out of KO range while protecting itself. King's Shield lowering the Attack of foes that use contact moves can also give Aegislash more opportunities to recover with Leftovers. Life Orb : Life Orb provides a helpful damage boost against Pokemon that Aegislash cannot quite OHKO with coverage. Examples include Hisuian Samurott, Mega Lucario, and Mega Lopunny with Close Combat, as well as Mega Floette with Flash Cannon. However, this cuts heavily into Aegislash's longevity.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description_plain: Aegislash solidifies its place in the metagame as a prominent answer to Fairy-types, helping check Sylveon and Mega Floette while being immune to Fake Out and walling Sneasler . Aegislash takes advantage of its high offensive and defensive capabilities to tank an attack and retaliate with its powerful STAB moves and Fighting-type coverage. It also picks off weakened foes with access to Shadow Sneak. Iron Head versus Fighting-type coverage : Iron Head makes it easier for Aegislash to remove Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette, while Fighting-type coverage helps Aegislash deal with Dark- and Steel-types, most commonly Kingambit . Close Combat versus Sacred Sword : Sacred Sword is preferred for the bulkier set because it avoids the defensive drawback of Close Combat, and it can be useful against Archaludon to bypass its Stamina boosts. Close Combat is generally better, especially for the glass cannon set, as it deals more damage than Sacred Sword, notably allowing Aegislash to OHKO Hydreigon . King's Shield versus Wide Guard : King's Shield is typically preferred, as it not only shields Aegislash from attacks but also allows it to switch back to Shield forme after attacking. Wide Guard can be used on the Focus Sash set because Aegislash is already guaranteed to survive an attack, so it does not need to switch formes often. Wide Guard also protects both Aegislash and its teammates from moves like Rock Slide and Earthquake from Garchomp and Heat Wave from Mega Charizard Y . Items Spell Tag : Spell Tag greatly boosts the power of Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak, allowing Aegislash to OHKO physically defensive non-Kasib Berry Sinistcha with Poltergeist and KO uninvested Garchomp with the combination of Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak. Focus Sash : Focus Sash allows Aegislash to withstand a powerful attack such as Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave or Weather Ball in the sun. Abilities Stance Change : After Aegislash attacks, it is extremely vulnerable because its Blade forme has low defenses. This means that it must often alternate between attacking and using King's Shield to change formes. Additionally, using priority Shadow Sneak can be dangerous, since it leaves Aegislash vulnerable before foes have had a chance to attack. SP Spreads 27 HP / 32 Atk / 7 Spe with Adamant : The Speed investment allows Aegislash to outrun Adamant Sneasler and Modest Mega Froslass in Tailwind. The remaining SPs are invested in HP and Attack to maximize its damage output and ability to take hits. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant : This SP spread should only be used with a Focus Sash set because it neglects bulk in favor of striking first. The speed investment notably allows Aegislash to outspeed uninvested Archaludon and, in Tailwind, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl . 32 HP / 11 Atk / 23 Spe with Adamant : The Speed investment allows Aegislash to outspeed Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar in Tailwind. The remaining SPs are invested in HP and Attack, but with more investment in HP because Spell Tag Aegislash already secures the OHKOs it needs, including an OHKO on most bulky Mega Gengar variants with Poltergeist even at -1. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses : Kingambit can be problematic for Aegislash, even for variants that run Fighting-type coverage, as Kingambit often has Chople Berry, allowing it to survive the hit and OHKO Aegislash in return with Kowtow Cleave while Aegislash is in Blade forme. Few threats can outright OHKO Aegislash in Shield forme from full HP, but exceptions include Mega Charizard Y with Heat Wave or Weather Ball in sun and Basculegion-M with a 100-Base Power Last Respects. Garchomp is not a full counter, but it deals a hefty amount of damage with its Ground-type STAB moves, and Aegislash cannot even 2HKO Sitrus Berry variants. Maushold is one of the more problematic support Pokemon for Aegislash because it is immune to Ghost-type attacks and commonly uses either Chople Berry or Focus Sash, forcing Aegislash to attack it twice and leaving Aegislash vulnerable for longer. Additionally, Maushold can lock Aegislash into King's Shield with Encore, preventing it from switching to Shield forme unpunished. In general, Aegislash struggles because its need to switch between Blade and Shield formes is predictable. Mega Scovillain is another redirector that Aegislash struggles against because Aegislash's offensive presence is greatly diminished by the burn from Spicy Spray, and Mega Scovillain also threatens an OHKO with Overheat. Intimidate from Incineroar is also quite troublesome for Aegislash, as it reduces the value Aegislash gets from its attacking turns. In addition, Parting Shot bypasses King's Shield, and if Incineroar is slower, it can also threaten to OHKO Aegislash with its STAB attacks while Aegislash is in Blade forme. Aegislash can struggle against Pokemon that are itemless or have already used their item. Talonflame may choose to run no item, while common Pokemon like Garchomp and Sinistcha can consume their Sitrus Berry or resist Berry. This prevents Aegislash from hitting them with Poltergeist, which is its most powerful option. Good Partners and Synergies : Aerodactyl and Pelipper can provide Tailwind support, allowing Aegislash to reach the previously mentioned Speed benchmarks. They also help against Mega Charizard Y, with Aerodactyl threatening it with Rock Slide and Pelipper able to change the weather upon switching in, weaken its Fire-type attacks, and threaten an OHKO with Weather Ball. Garchomp is one of Aegislash's best partners because it threatens Kingambit and Incineroar with its Ground-type STAB attacks, and it often carries Rock Slide to pressure Mega Charizard Y. In return, Aegislash resists attacks from and threatens Ice- and Fairy-types such as Mega Froslass and Sylveon, which would otherwise OHKO Garchomp. Additionally, Garchomp can freely use Earthquake when paired with Wide Guard Aegislash. Mega Floette also pairs well with Aegislash, as it threatens opposing Garchomp, which can deal significant damage to Aegislash. In return, Aegislash handles Sneasler, one of Mega Floette's biggest threats. Furthermore, unlike Aegislash, Mega Floette is not hindered by Intimidate, making it a strong offensive partner. Mega Charizard Y can also pair well with Aegislash, as it can threaten Kingambit as well as OHKO most Maushold with Weather Ball. Rotom-Wash is another solid partner, as it can use Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical threats such as Garchomp and Kingambit while pressuring Basculegion-M and Incineroar with Thunderbolt and Hydro Pump, respectively. In return, Aegislash can handle Pokemon like Sinistcha that wall Rotom-Wash, and it can pick off weakened foes with Shadow Sneak, as Rotom-Wash often falls just short of scoring OHKOs. How to Overcome Aegislash's Weaknesses : Aegislash's problematic matchups against Kingambit and Mega Charizard Y are greatly improved by partner Garchomp's Ground- and Rock-type coverage. The Focus Sash set itself is an adaptation to work around the predictability of using King's Shield to switch formes because it does not need to focus on bulk and typically drops King's Shield in favor of Wide Guard. However, the predictability of the bulkier set might force riskier plays to prevent Aegislash's partners from being targeted without punishment. Generally speaking, it is much better to pair Aegislash with special-attacking threats like Mega Floette because Incineroar can easily cycle in and out of the field against Aegislash.

Garchomp is one of Aegislash's best partners because it threatens Kingambit and Incineroar with its Ground-type STAB attacks, and it often carries Rock Slide to pressure Mega Charizard Y. In return, Aegislash resists attacks from and threatens Ice- and Fairy-types such as Mega Froslass and Sylveon, which would otherwise OHKO Garchomp. Additionally, Garchomp can freely use Earthquake when paired with Wide Guard Aegislash. Mega Floette also pairs well with Aegislash, as it threatens opposing Garchomp, which can deal significant damage to Aegislash. In return, Aegislash handles Sneasler, one of Mega Floette's biggest threats. Furthermore, unlike Aegislash, Mega Floette is not hindered by Intimidate, making it a strong offensive partner. Mega Charizard Y can also pair well with Aegislash, as it can threaten Kingambit as well as OHKO most Maushold with Weather Ball. Rotom-Wash is another solid partner, as it can use Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical threats such as Garchomp and Kingambit while pressuring Basculegion-M and Incineroar with Thunderbolt and Hydro Pump, respectively. In return, Aegislash can handle Pokemon like Sinistcha that wall Rotom-Wash, and it can pick off weakened foes with Shadow Sneak, as Rotom-Wash often falls just short of scoring OHKOs.

  • How to Overcome Aegislash's Weaknesses: Aegislash's problematic matchups against Kingambit and Mega Charizard Y are greatly improved by partner Garchomp's Ground- and Rock-type coverage. The Focus Sash set itself is an adaptation to work around the predictability of using King's Shield to switch formes because it does not need to focus on bulk and typically drops King's Shield in favor of Wide Guard. However, the predictability of the bulkier set might force riskier plays to prevent Aegislash's partners from being targeted without punishment. Generally speaking, it is much better to pair Aegislash with special-attacking threats like Mega Floette because Incineroar can easily cycle in and out of the field against Aegislash.

movesets.description_html:
• Mega Staraptor is a threatening offensive Mega Evolution in Regulation M-B thanks to its excellent stats, near-unresisted offensive typing, and ability to threaten such foes like Archaludon and Volcarona.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat gives Mega Staraptor a way to boost its defenses. Close Combat also lets it pick off weakened foes while hitting Flying-resistant foes like Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Mega Lucario, in addition to making them excellent starting points for gaining boosts. With these boosts, it becomes very hard to take down.

  • Brave Bird: Mega Staraptor uses its strong STAB Brave Bird to threaten Fighting-resistant or -immune foes such as Mega Delphox, Mega Charizard Y, Basculegion-M, and Mimikyu.

  • Roost: Roost provides Mega Staraptor a consistent way to heal and gives it incredible longevity when combined with boosts from Contrary Close Combat.

  • Blaze Kick: While its offensive typing is excellent, Mega Staraptor can run Blaze Kick to tear down Aegislash and Gholdengo, both of which would otherwise wall its attacks. Also, Aegislash has trouble using King's Shield in this matchup, as King's Shield boosts Mega Staraptor's Attack instead of lowering it.

  • Substitute: Substitute is a way for Mega Staraptor to avoid status-inflicting moves like Mortal Spin from Glimmora and Yawn from Hippowdon. It also lets Mega Staraptor set up more easily while taking advantage of passive Pokemon such as Hippowdon.

  • U-turn: U-turn makes Mega Staraptor a hit-and-run attacker, giving its team momentum while chipping common switch-ins such as Aegislash, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. It also breaks Mimikyu's Disguise; while Brave Bird and Blaze Kick also break Disguise, U-turn lets Mega Staraptor pivot to another teammate, like Archaludon, to deal with Mimikyu.

  • 31 HP / 3 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: A bulky spread allows Mega Staraptor to become even harder to take down, ensuring that it can survive a Psyshock from Timid Mega Delphox.
